BURHAN:v1p366/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p366/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p366/r3.claim: Stops at an object, a specifying circumstantial phrase, or an exception that changes meaning fall between the tighter and looser attachment classes; examples include مسغبة, قليلا, مصيرا, واحدة, زوجها, and نذيرا.
BURHAN:v1p366/r3.anchor: فإن وسطت بين التعلق بالمذكور من المتعلق الذى للمفعول أو الحال المخصصة أو الاستثناء الذى يتغير بسقوطه المعنى

DAMGHANI:v1p207/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p207/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p207/r9.claim: Raqīb can mean a protector or keeper of deeds; two further passages are cited.
DAMGHANI:v1p207/r9.anchor: الرقيب يعني الحفيظ قوله سبحانه في سورة النساء

ASAD-NOTES:4:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:intro/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:4:intro/r1.claim: The title reflects extensive material on women's rights and family law; the opening verse asserts humanity's unity and reciprocal obligations of women and men.
ASAD-NOTES:4:intro/r1.anchor: The opening verse stresses the essential unity of the human race and the mutual obligations

ASAD-NOTES:4:intro/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:intro/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:4:intro/r3.claim: The surah is Medinan, probably revealed in 4 AH, possibly after Al-'Imran or after Al-Ahzab and Al-Mumtahanah, with some verses earlier and 4:58 later.
ASAD-NOTES:4:intro/r3.anchor: it was revealed in the fourth year after the hijrah

STUDYQURAN:4:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:intro/r3.claim: Most of 4:1–36, 4:127–130, and 4:176 is legislative, as are its instructions for conduct in war and peace.
STUDYQURAN:4:intro/r3.anchor: Most of the first part (vv. 1–36, 127–30, 176) is legislative in nature, as is the section dealing with war and peace

THALABI:v3p243/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p243/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v3p243/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says pre-Islamic Arabs denied inheritance to women and children and let the eldest take it.
THALABI:v3p243/r2.anchor: كان أهل الجاهلية لا يورثون النساء والصبيان ويأخذ الأكبر الميراث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p488/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p488/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p488/r1.claim: Raqīb is an intensive form from raqaba: to watch an affair closely to ascertain its true state, with an associated sense of guarding; the passage lists watcher, arrow, snake, lookout, and waiting as related usages.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p488/r1.anchor: الرقيب: فعيل للمبالغة من رقب يرقب رقبا ورقوبا ورقبانا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p488/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p488/r2.speaker: أبو داود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p488/r2.claim: Abu Dawud’s cited verse uses الرقباء in describing watchers positioned in ambush, as lexical evidence for the watcher sense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p488/r2.anchor: وقال أبو داود: كمقاعد الرقباء للضرباء أيديهم نواهد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p492/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p492/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p492/r2.claim: Most scholars consider the surah Medinan, with a reported exception for the verse about returning trusts; al-Nahhas calls it Meccan, and al-Naqqash says it descended at the Migration, though all agree it includes Medinan material.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p492/r2.anchor: الجمهور على أن هذه السورة مدنية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p492/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p492/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p492/r3.claim: Al-Bukhari identifies the inheritance question about collateral relatives as the last verse revealed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p492/r3.anchor: وفي البخاري: آخر آية نزلت يستفتونك، قل الله يفتيكم في الكلالة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p492/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p492/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p492/r4.claim: The opening follows the prior surah’s account of communities and God’s promise not to waste anyone’s work by returning to the common human origin, encouraging concord, affection, and mutual care.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p492/r4.anchor: ومناسبة هذه السورة لما قبلها أنه تعالى لما ذكر أحوال المشركين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p492/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p492/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p492/r5.claim: The single-origin reminder argues for piety: the One able to create humanity in this remarkable way deserves to be obeyed and feared.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p492/r5.anchor: ومن كان قادرا على مثل هذا الإيجاد الغريب الصنع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p492/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p492/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p492/r6.claim: Mentioning one human origin appeals to natural affinity among kindred species and encourages people to unite in piety.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p492/r6.anchor: ونبه بقوله: من نفس واحدة، على ما هو مركوز في الطباع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p492/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p492/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p492/r7.claim: Al-nās is general because of its definite article, and both the call to piety and its rationale apply generally.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p492/r7.anchor: والظاهر في الناس: العموم، لأن الألف واللام فيه تفيده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p492/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p492/r8.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p492/r8.claim: An alternative takes “people” as the Meccans, based on Arabs’ custom of pleading by God and kinship.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p492/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p492/r9.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p492/r9.claim: Another alternative takes “people” to mean the believers, in light of the statement that believers are brothers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p492/r9.anchor: وقيل: المراد المؤمنون نظرا إلى قوله: إنما المؤمنون إخوة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r1.claim: When a people-address includes disbelievers, the Qur'an often follows with proofs of divine unity and lordship; when it addresses believers, it often follows with reminders of blessings they already recognize.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r1.anchor: إذا كان الخطاب والنداء بيا أيها الناس وكان للكفرة فقط

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r2.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r2.claim: Some treat this opening as parallel to the opening of al-Hajj: this surah, fourth in the first half, grounds piety in human origin, while al-Hajj, fourth in the second half, grounds it in the afterlife.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r3.claim: The first mention of piety is general avoidance of whatever brings punishment; another reading is specific piety in preserving people’s rights and maintaining their mutual ties.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r3.anchor: وهو ظاهر الأمر بالتقوى أنها تقوى عامة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses piety as obedience.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: المراد بالتقوى الطاعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r5.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r5.claim: Muqatil glosses piety as fear of God.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r6.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r6.claim: Another explanation defines piety as avoiding major and minor sins.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r7.anchor: والمراد بقوله: من نفس واحدة آدم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r8.claim: The majority read واحدة with feminine agreement to nafs; Ibn Abi Abla reads واحد, matching the intended Adam or treating nafs as masculine.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r8.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: واحدة بالتاء على تأنيث لفظ النفس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r9.claim: Creation here means originating through branching and returning to one source; the cited verse illustrates bodily descent from an origin.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r9.anchor: ومعنى الخلق هنا: الاختراع بطريق التفريع، والرجوع إلى أصل واحد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r10.speaker: الأصم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r10.claim: Al-Asamm says reason alone cannot establish that humanity was created from one self; that claim rests on transmitted revelation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r10.anchor: وقال الأصم: لا يدل العقل على أن الخلق مخلوقين من نفس واحدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p493/r11.claim: The possessive link to Adam treats him as the source of later generations even though descendants arise through procreation; this counters materialist claims about humanity’s origin.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r1.claim: Since Muhammad was unlettered and had not read scripture, creation’s complexity points to divine unity, while the single origin points to prophethood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r1.anchor: ولما كان صلى الله عليه وسلم أميا ما قرأ كتابا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r2.claim: The single origin discourages pride and rivalry and also indicates resurrection: the One who brought diverse people from one person can more readily revive them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r2.anchor: وفي قوله: من نفس واحدة إشارة إلى ترك المفاخرة والكبر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والسدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r3.claim: They identify Adam as the self from whom Eve, his wife, was initially created.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r3.anchor: وبه قال: ابن عباس، ومجاهد، والسدي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r4.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r4.claim: Qatada says Adam slept alone in the Garden, and God made Eve from a short rib taken from his left side, or according to another report his right.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r4.anchor: انتزع الله تعالى أحد أضلاعه القصرى من شماله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r5.claim: Ibn Atiyya cites the authentic hadith that woman was created from a crooked rib and that straightening it breaks it, glossed as divorce.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r5.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ويعضد هذا القول الحديث الصحيح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r6.claim: Abu Hayyan allows a figurative reading of the rib: women’s changeable temperaments and difficult handling resemble a crooked rib, as humanity is described as hasty.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r6.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون ذلك على جهة التمثيل لاضطراب أخلاقهن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r7.speaker: ابن بحر وأبو مسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r7.claim: Ibn Bahr and Abu Muslim say “from it” means from Adam’s kind, as in other verses saying spouses or a messenger are from among you.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r7.anchor: وقيل: هو على حذف مضاف، التقدير: وخلق من جنسها زوجها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r8.speaker: القاضي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r8.claim: The Judge prefers literal creation from Adam, reasoning that if Eve were independently created humanity would have two origins; Abu Hayyan answers that من can mark the starting point of creation.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r9.claim: Another view takes the pronoun in منها to refer to the clay separated from Adam’s clay, so Eve was made of the same material as Adam.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r9.anchor: وقيل: لا حذف، والضمير في منها، ليس عائدا على نفس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r10.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r10.claim: One report says Eve was created while Adam was in the Garden; another says she was made before his entry, as Kaab al-Ahbar, Wahb, and Ibn Ishaq hold.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p494/r10.anchor: وظاهر قول ابن عباس ومن تقدم: أنها خلقت وآدم في الجنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p495/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p495/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p495/r1.claim: The coordinating wāw does not imply temporal order; Adam’s creation is mentioned first because the addressed people are the focus, as in the command to worship the Lord who created them and those before them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p495/r1.anchor: إذ الواو لا تدل على ترتيب زماني كما تقرر في علم العربية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p495/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p495/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p495/r2.claim: Zamakhshari posits an omitted earlier phrase so Eve’s creation follows Adam’s creation in time; Abu Hayyan says this grammatical workaround is unnecessary.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p495/r2.anchor: يعطف على محذوف كأنه قيل: من نفس واحدة أنشأها أو ابتدأها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p495/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p495/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p495/r3.claim: Zamakhshari also connects the phrase directly to “created you,” with Adam as the single self and Eve as the mother of those addressed; Abu Hayyan says this fits Arabic syntax.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p495/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p495/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p495/r4.claim: A further parsing connects “created her spouse” to the participle واحدَة, understood as “a self made single,” with خلق as “created” or “separated.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p495/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون قوله: وخلق منها زوجها معطوفا على اسم الفاعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p495/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p495/r5.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p495/r5.claim: An unusual interpretation reads the single self as the spirit, its spouse as the body, and creation as their composition; Abu Hayyan says this differs from earlier commentators.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p495/r5.anchor: ومن غريب التفسير أنه عنى بالنفس الروح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p495/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p495/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p495/r6.claim: Abu Hayyan says Zamakhshari’s ellipsis is unnecessary because the direct analysis already fits Arabic syntax.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p495/r6.anchor: ولا حاجة إلى تكلف هذا الوجه مع مساغ الوجه الذي ذكرناه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496/r1.claim: بث منهما means that God spread and dispersed humanity from Adam and his wife; Arabic also uses the quadriliteral أبث for this sense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496/r1.anchor: وبث منهما أي من تلك النفس، وزوجها أي: نشر وفرق في الوجود

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496/r2.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496/r2.claim: The indefinite رجال and the added كثيرا emphasize broad spread; men are mentioned first for their superiority, while the adjective “many” is understood with women as well.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496/r2.anchor: قيل: نكر لما في التنكير من الشيوع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496/r3.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496/r3.claim: Another explanation says the adjective is intentionally attached only to men because men publicly appear while women are meant to remain hidden.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496/r3.anchor: على أن اللائق بحالهم الاشتهار والخروج والبروز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496/r4.claim: The division into male and female is taken to mean there is no third sex; apparently ambiguous cases must ultimately belong to one of these two kinds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496/r4.anchor: وفي تنويع ما خلق من آدم وحواء إلى رجال ونساء دليل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496/r5.claim: A variant reads وخالق منها زوجها as an active participle with an omitted subject, “and He is creating her spouse from it.”

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496/r6.claim: The repeated command to fear God reinforces the first, or distinguishes nurture and beneficence in “your Lord” from awe and threat in “God.”

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496/r7.claim: The majority read تساءلون; the Kufans lighten the sin, deriving it from the original تتساءلون.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the light reading deletes the second tāʾ of تتساءلون; Abu Hayyan notes the Kufan grammarian Hisham instead says it deletes the imperfect prefix tāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r1.anchor: أما قول ابن عطية: حذفوا التاء الثانية فهذا مذهب أهل البصرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r2.speaker: أبو علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r2.claim: Abu Ali says adjacent sounds may be lightened through deletion, assimilation, or substitution, and cites طست from طس with an al-Ajjaj verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r2.anchor: قال أبو علي: وإذا اجتمعت المتقاربة خففت بالحذف والإدغام والإبدال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan says Ibn Atiyya should note that retention is original and assimilation is close to it; deletion follows identical consonants, not merely nearby sounds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r3.anchor: كان ينبغي أن ينبه على الإثبات، إذ يجوز الإثبات وهو الأصل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r4.claim: Assimilation is not confined to the tafaʿʿul form but occurs across several verb forms; deletion, however, is limited to imperfects beginning with the extra tāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r4.anchor: أما الإدغام فلا يختص به، بل ذلك في الأمر والمضارع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r5.claim: The claim that close sounds always trigger reduction is too broad; Abu Ali means only that reduction can occur, and طست is an example of doubled consonants instead.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r5.anchor: وأما تمثيله بطست في طس فليس البدل هنا لاجتماع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r6.claim: يتساءلون به means that people ask one another by God, including the formula “I ask you by God to do this,” or invoke God to emphasize their rights.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r6.anchor: ومعنى يتساءلون به: أي يتعاطون به السؤال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r7.speaker: عبد الله
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r7.claim: Ibn Masud reads with the simple verb تسألون, and another form drops the hamza and transfers its vowel to the sin.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله: تسألون به مضارع سأل الثلاثي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r8.speaker: طائفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r8.claim: A group says the phrase means invoking God to claim rights and treating Him as exalted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p496#2/r8.anchor: وقالت طائفة: معناه تسألون به حقوقكم وتجعلونه معظما لها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p497/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p497/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة والسدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p497/r1.claim: They parse الأرْحام accusative as “avoid cutting kinship ties,” with an omitted noun; piety toward God means obedience, while piety toward kin means maintaining ties through kindness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p497/r1.anchor: وعلى هذا المعنى فسرها ابن عباس وقتادة والسدي وغيرهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p497/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p497/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p497/r2.claim: The shared sense of avoiding violation reconciles the different applications and answers the objection that one word cannot carry different meanings; kinship’s coordination with God highlights the gravity of severing ties.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p497/r2.anchor: وفي عطف الأرحام على اسم الله دلالة على عظم ذنب قطع الرحم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p497/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p497/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p497/r3.claim: Other scriptural and prophetic examples emphasize kindness to parents and relatives and the duty to maintain what God commanded to be joined.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p497/r3.anchor: ويقطعون ما أمر الله به أن يوصل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p497/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p497/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p497/r4.claim: Another accusative parse attaches الأرْحام to the implied object of the preposition به, supported by Ibn Masud’s reading with a repeated preposition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p497/r4.anchor: وقيل: النصب عطفا على موضع به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p497/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p497/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p497/r5.claim: The nominative can begin a sentence with an omitted predicate: Ibn Atiyya supplies “kin deserve to be joined,” while Zamakhshari supplies that they are to be revered or invoked; Abu Hayyan prefers the latter as closer to the wording.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p497/r5.anchor: وقدره الزمخشري: والأرحام مما يتقى، أو مما يتساءل به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p497/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p497/r6.speaker: الحسن والنخعي ومجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p497/r6.claim: They explain the genitive reading as coordination with the attached pronoun in به without repeating the preposition, supported by the reading وبالأرحام.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p497/r6.anchor: وعلى هذا فسرها الحسن والنخعي ومجاهد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p497/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p497/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p497/r7.claim: The wording also reflects people invoking God and kinship together when making appeals.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p498/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p498/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p498/r1.claim: Zamakhshari rejects attaching الأرْحام to the bound pronoun without repeating the preposition, arguing that the pronoun and preposition form a tightly joined unit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p498/r1.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وليس بسديد يعني: الجر عطفا على الضمير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p498/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p498/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p498/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya says leading Basran grammarians disallow coordinating an overt noun with a genitive pronoun; Sibawayh permits it only in poetry, though some grammarians accept it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p498/r2.anchor: وهذه القراءة عند رؤساء نحويين البصرة لا تجوز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p498/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p498/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p498/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan says al-Mazani’s analogy fails because رأيتك وزيدا is accepted although رأيت زيداوك is not.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p498/r3.anchor: وتعليل المازني معترض بأنه يجوز أن تقول: رأيتك وزيدا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p498/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p498/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p498/r4.claim: Ibn Atiyya further argues that a genitive pronoun cannot separate from its preposition and therefore behaves like part of a word.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p498/r4.anchor: المضمر المخفوض لا ينفصل، فهو كحرف من الكلمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p499/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p499/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p499/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya objects that the genitive reading contributes no useful exhortation and implies swearing by kinship; he cites the prohibition on swearing by anything but God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p499/r1.anchor: من كان حالفا فليحلف بالله أو ليصمت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p499/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p499/r2.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p499/r2.claim: Some take the wāw as an oath particle rather than coordination, making the following clause the oath’s response and treating kinship as honored by God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p499/r2.anchor: وذهبت طائفة إلى أن الواو في والأرحام واو القسم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p499/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p499/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p499/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan endorses the Kufan rule permitting coordination to a genitive pronoun without repeating the preposition and rejects the Basran restriction as unsound.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p499/r3.anchor: بل الصحيح مذهب الكوفيين في ذلك وأنه يجوز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p499/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p499/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p499/r4.claim: He sharply rebukes Ibn Atiyya for rejecting a mutawatir reading transmitted from the Prophet through senior Companions and the leading reciters.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p499/r4.anchor: عمد إلى ردها بشيء خطر له في ذهنه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p499/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p499/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p499/r5.claim: Abu Hayyan defends Hamza’s integrity and transmission, says readers need not follow Basran grammarians, and insists Arabic usage exceeds what any one school transmitted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p499/r5.anchor: ولسنا متعبدين بقول نحاة البصرة ولا غيرهم ممن خالفهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p500/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p500/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p500/r1.claim: Allah’s being ever watchful is not restricted to past time; He continually observes and knows everything about people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p500/r1.anchor: فهو تعالى رقيب في الماضي وغيره علينا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p531/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p531/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p531/r1.claim: The passage uses antithesis between one and its mate, rich and poor, and few and many.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p531/r1.anchor: الطباق في: واحدة وزوجها، وفي غنيا وفقيرا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p531/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p531/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p531/r2.claim: It repeats key words and meanings: fear, creation, orphan, women, inheritance, and guarding against injustice.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p531/r2.anchor: والتكرار في: اتقوا، وفي: خلق، وفي: خفتم، وأن لا تقسطوا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p531/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p531/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p531/r14.claim: The passage uses ellipsis in several places.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r1.claim: Nisa is Medinan according to the correct view; al-Nahhas calls it Meccan based on the Meccan revelation of the command to return the Kaaba key, but al-Suyuti says that does not determine the whole surah’s provenance.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r1.anchor: ( مدنية على الصحيح وزعم النحاس أنها مكية مستندا إلى أن قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r2.speaker: السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r2.claim: Al-Suyuti argues that a Meccan verse within a long surah, mostly revealed in Medina, does not make that surah Meccan; material after the Hijra is generally Medinan.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r2.anchor: لأنه لا يلزم من نزول آية أو آيات بمكة من سورة طويلة نزل معظمها بالمدينة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r3.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r3.claim: Aisha’s report in al-Bukhari that Baqara and Nisa were revealed while she was with the Prophet, after their post-Hijra marriage, supports Nisa’s Medinan classification.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r3.anchor: ما أخرجه البخاري عن عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها قالت

ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r4.claim: Another view says the surah was revealed around the time of the Hijra.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r5.claim: The Syrian count is 177 verses, the Kufan count 176, and other counts 175; authorities differ on whether two clauses are separate verses.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r5.anchor: وعدة آياتها عند الشاميين مائة وسبع وسبعون وعند الكوفيين ست وسبعون

ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r6.claim: Nisa opens with taqwa after Ali ʿImran ends with it, a strong rhetorical link between surahs known as similarity of endings or tassbigh.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r6.anchor: آل عمران ختمت بالأمر بالتقوى وأفتتحت هذه السورة به وذلك من آكد وجوه المناسبات

ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r7.claim: Other links are that Nisa refers to the aftermath of Uhud, follows Ali ʿImran’s mention of the expedition after Uhud, and develops in detail themes stated earlier; this ordering is better than that in Ibn Masud’s codex.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r7.anchor: في آل عمران ذكر قصة أحد مستوفاة وفي هذه السورة ذكر ذيلها

ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r1.claim: Esoterically, piety means fearing disobedience and attachment to worldly others, while keeping the primordial covenant made when people testified about themselves.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r1.anchor: أي أحذوره من المخالفات والنظر إلى الأغيار وألزموا عهد الأزل حين أشهدكم على أنفسكم

ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r2.claim: The 'single soul' is the Muhammadan Reality, also called the universal rational soul, the world's heart, and the real Adam, father of the historical Adam.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r2.anchor: وهي الحقيقة المحمدية ويعبر عنها أيضا بالنفس الناطقة الكلية التي هي قلب العالم وبآدم الحقيقي الذي هو الأب لآدم

ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r3.speaker: ابن الفارض
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r3.claim: Ibn al-Farid's cited verse has the Reality say that although outwardly a son of Adam, it bears within itself the meaning of fatherhood.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r3.anchor: وإني وإن كنت إبن آدم صورة فلي فيه معنى شاهد بأبوتي

ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r4.claim: The spouse is either nature or the animal soul arising from the first soul; it was created on the side facing the created realm, symbolized by the left rib, as that side is farther from the Real.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r4.anchor: وهي الطبيعة أو النفس الحيوانية الناشئة منها وقد خلقت من الجهة التي تلي عالم الكون وهو الضلع الأيسر

ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r5.claim: Esoterically, the many men are perfected people inclining toward their father, while women are deficient people inclining toward their mother.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r5.anchor: أي كاملين يميلون إلى أبيهم ( ونساءا ) ناقصين يميلون إلى أمهم

ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r6.claim: Calling upon God means denying independent existence, since God manifested people's determinations after they were nothing; piety toward wombs means loving God's saints, the true kinship of the higher principles.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r6.anchor: فلا تثبتوا لأنفسكم وجودا مع وجوده لأنه الذي أظهر تعيناتكم بعد أن لم تكونوا شيئا مذكورا

ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r7.claim: God watches hearts; inclination to anything besides Him and suspicion of the people of His presence drive away the lights, leaving the heart desolate.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p209/r7.anchor: إن الله كان عليكم رقيبا ) ناظرا إلى قلوبكم مطلعا على ما فيها فإذا رأى فيها الميل إلى السوي وسوء الظن

BIQAI-FULL:v2p203/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p203/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p203/r4.claim: Al-Harali identifies al-Nisa's purpose as gathering people around the unity taught by Ali Imran and the scripture directed by al-Baqara, for the religion collected by al-Fatiha, against division incited by Shas ibn Qays and his allies.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p203/r4.anchor: مقصودها الاجتماع على التوحيد الذي هدت إليه آل عمران

BIQAI-FULL:v2p203/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p203/r5.speaker: يوسف بن ماهك
BIQAI-FULL:v2p203/r5.claim: Yusuf ibn Mahak reports that Aisha said the Qur'an first revealed brief Makkan surahs about paradise and hell, then lawful and unlawful rulings after people embraced Islam; early wine or adultery bans would have been rejected.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p203/r5.anchor: عن يوسف بن ماهك أن عراقيا سأل أم المؤمنين عائشة رضي الله عنها

BIQAI-FULL:v2p203/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p203/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p203/r6.claim: Aisha's account shows that revelation followed circumstances for the highest eloquence, and the Qur'an's arrangement then suits what people can understand.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p203/r6.anchor: أن القرآن حاز أعلى البلاغة في إنزاله مطابقا لما تقتضيه الأحوال

BURSEVI:v2p128/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p128/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p128/r1.claim: The source gives the surah’s verse count as either 175 or 177.
BURSEVI:v2p128/r1.anchor: وهي مائة وخمس اوست أو سبع وسبعون آية

BURSEVI:v2p128/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p128/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p128/r2.claim: The address includes those present when it was revealed and later people, but not earlier generations, who were not bound by this law.
BURSEVI:v2p128/r2.anchor: خطاب عام يتناول الموجودين في زمان الخطاب ومن بعدهم دون المنقرضين

BURSEVI:v2p128/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p128/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p128/r3.claim: The exclusion of earlier people follows because they were not obligated by the Prophet’s law; including all Adam’s descendants would imply an impossible retroactive duty.
BURSEVI:v2p128/r3.anchor: بدليل أنهم ما كانوا متعبدين بشرعنا فلو كان عاما لجميع بني آدم

BURSEVI:v2p128/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p128/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p128/r4.claim: Taqwa here means preserving mutual rights and duties of connection instead of neglecting or severing them.
BURSEVI:v2p128/r4.anchor: في حفظ ما بينكم من الحقوق وما يجب وصله ومراعاته ولا تضيعوه ولا تقطعوا ما أمرتم بوصله

BURSEVI:v2p128/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p128/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p128/r5.claim: The Creator formed people through successive stages and with differing forms and colors.
BURSEVI:v2p128/r5.anchor: أي قدر خلقكم حالا بعد حال على اختلاف صوركم وألوانكم

BURSEVI:v2p128/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p128/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p128/r6.claim: The single soul is their one origin, Adam, and recalling the favor of creation turns people toward fearing their Creator.
BURSEVI:v2p128/r6.anchor: من أصل واحد وهو نفس آدم أبيكم وعقب الاتقاء بمنة الخلق كيلا يتقي إلا الخالق

BURSEVI:v2p128/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p128/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p128/r7.claim: The spouse created from the single soul is their mother Eve, made from part of Adam, from his left rib.
BURSEVI:v2p128/r7.anchor: يعني من بعضها {زوجها} أمكم حواء بالمد من ضلع من أضلاعه اليسرى.

BURSEVI:v2p128/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p128/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p128/r8.claim: A report says God put Adam to sleep in the Garden and created Eve from him while he was between sleep and waking; on waking, he felt drawn to her because she was part of him.
BURSEVI:v2p128/r8.anchor: روي أن الله تعالى لما خلق آدم عليه السلام وأسكنه الجنة ألقى عليه النوم

BURSEVI:v2p128/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p128/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p128/r9.claim: Eve is mentioned after Adam although created first because the conjunction waw does not itself establish sequence.
BURSEVI:v2p128/r9.anchor: وأخرت حواء في الذكر وإن كانت مقدمة في الخلق لأن الواو لا ترتيب فيها

BURSEVI:v2p128/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p128/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p128/r10.claim: Humanity spread from Adam and Eve through procreation, producing many men and women.
BURSEVI:v2p128/r10.anchor: من تلك النفس وزوجها المخلوقة بطريق التوالد والتناسل

BURSEVI:v2p128/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p128/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p128/r11.claim: The masculine plural for men reflects collective number; the text says men are numerous, while the source says wisdom implies women are even more numerous.
BURSEVI:v2p128/r11.anchor: واكتفى بوصف الرجال بالكثرة عن وصف النساء بها إذ الحكمة تقتضي أن يكون أكثر.

BURSEVI:v2p128/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p128/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p128/r12.claim: The shared origin prepares the command to preserve household and social rights, since people branch from one root and should not compete destructively.
BURSEVI:v2p128/r12.anchor: لأن المراد به تمهيد للأمر بالتقوى فيما يتصل بحقوق أهل منزله وبني جنسه

BURSEVI:v2p128/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p128/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p128/r13.claim: Calling on one another by God and by kinship reflects the Arab custom of invoking the womb ties to awaken compassion.
BURSEVI:v2p128/r13.anchor: وجرت عادة العرب على أن أحدهم إذا استعطف غيره يقرن الرحم في السؤال

BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r1.claim: Al-arham may be parsed in the accusative as coordinated with the case of the preceding prepositional phrase or with Allah; either way, the command is to maintain kinship and not sever it.
BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r1.anchor: فقوله والأرحام بالنصب عطف على محل الجار والمجرور كقولك مررت بزيد وعمرا أو على الله

BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r2.claim: Mentioning kinship beside God signals its importance and closeness to him.
BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r2.anchor: وقد نبه سبحانه إذ قرن الأرحام باسمه على أن صلتها بمكان منه وعنه صلى الله عليه وسلم

BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r3.speaker: رسول الله
BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r3.claim: The Prophet reports that kinship hangs from the Throne and says God connects with whoever maintains it and cuts off whoever severs it.
BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r3.anchor: وعنه صلى الله عليه وسلم "الرحم معلقة بالعرش تقول : من وصلني وصله الله ومن قطعني قطعه الله"

BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r4.speaker: رسول الله
BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r4.claim: The Prophet says maintaining kinship is a good deed whose reward comes quickly, while injustice is a sin whose punishment comes quickly.
BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r4.anchor: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم "ما من عمل حسنة أسرع

BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r5.claim: People should honor mutual rights because all are siblings through Adam and Eve, especially believers, who also share kinship through faith and religion.
BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r5.anchor: لأن الكل أخ لأب وأم هما آدم وحواء سيما المؤمنين لأن فيهم قرابة الإيمان والدين

BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r6.claim: Al-raqib means the watcher who preserves every deed, observes speech and inward intentions, and intends to recompense people for them.
BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r6.anchor: الرقيب هو المراقب الذي يحفظ عليك جميع أفعالك أي حافظا مطلعا على جميع ما يصدر عنكم

BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r7.claim: Because God knows what is hidden and more hidden, a person must act with caution and fear in all that they do.
BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r7.anchor: فبين الله تعالى أنه يعلم السر وأخفى إذا كان كذلك فيجب أن يكون المرء حذرا خائفا

BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r8.claim: Taqwa is the foundation and the means to the greatest honor in this world and the next.
BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r8.anchor: واعلم أن التقوى هي العمدة وهي سبب الكرامة العظمى في الدنيا والعقبى

BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r9.claim: A man in Basra became known for a musk scent after resisting a woman’s sexual advances by soiling himself; in a dream Gabriel rubbed him, and the fragrance remained as a blessing of taqwa.
BURSEVI:v2p128#2/r9.anchor: فقلت : الله الله فقالت : لا بأس فقلت : إني حازق فدخلت الخلاء وتغوطت ومسحت به وجهي وبدني

BURSEVI:v2p129/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p129/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p129/r1.claim: In religious usage, taqwa is protecting the soul from what harms it in the afterlife.
BURSEVI:v2p129/r1.anchor: والتقوى في عرف الشرع وقاية النفس عما يضرها في الآخرة وهي على مراتب

BURSEVI:v2p129/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p129/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p129/r2.claim: The first level avoids everlasting punishment by disavowing idolatry.
BURSEVI:v2p129/r2.anchor: الأولى التوقي عن العذاب المخلد بالتبري من الشرك وعليه قوله تعالى

BURSEVI:v2p129/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p129/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p129/r3.claim: The second, commonly called taqwa, means avoiding every sin.
BURSEVI:v2p129/r3.anchor: والثانية التجنب عن كل إثم وهو المتعارف باسم التقوى

BURSEVI:v2p129/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p129/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p129/r4.claim: The highest, true taqwa is withdrawing from everything that distracts one from God.
BURSEVI:v2p129/r4.anchor: والثالثة التنزه عن جميع ما يشغله وهو التقوى الحقيقي المطلوب بقوله تعالى

BURSEVI:v2p129/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p129/r5.speaker: ذو النون المصري
BURSEVI:v2p129/r5.claim: Dhu al-Nun told a ministerial retainer seeking spiritual aspiration that fearing God as he feared the ruler would make him one of the truthful saints.
BURSEVI:v2p129/r5.anchor: عن ذي النون المصري أنه لما جاء إليه بغض الوزراء وطلب الهمة وأظهر الخشية من السلطان قال له

BURSEVI:v2p129/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p129/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p129/r6.claim: A spiritual wayfarer should fear the Lord and remain watchful of God in every state.
BURSEVI:v2p129/r6.anchor: فينبغي للسالك أن يتقي ربه ويراقب الله في جميع أحواله كما قال تعالى

BURSEVI:v2p129/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p129/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p129/r7.claim: Muraqaba is the servant's knowledge that the Lord sees him; keeping that awareness present is watchfulness, the root of all good.
BURSEVI:v2p129/r7.anchor: والمراقبة : علم العبد باطلاع الرب سبحانه عليه فاستدامته لهذا العلم مراقبة لربه

BURSEVI:v2p129/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p129/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p129/r8.claim: One reaches watchfulness only after self-accounting, correcting the present, following truth, guarding the heart and each breath with God, and watching all one's states.
BURSEVI:v2p129/r8.anchor: إلا بعد فراغه من المحاسبة فإذا حاسب نفسه على ما سلف وأصلح حاله في الوقت ولازم طريق الحق

BURSEVI:v2p129/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p129/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p129/r9.claim: Neglecting God's constant awareness leaves one far from even the beginning of spiritual connection, let alone true nearness.
BURSEVI:v2p129/r9.anchor: ومن تغافل عن هذه الجملة فهو بمعزل عن بداية الوصلة فكيف عن حقائق القربة

BURSEVI:v2p129/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p129/r10.speaker: حميد الطويل
BURSEVI:v2p129/r10.claim: Humayd warned that sinning in private while believing God sees is grave audacity, while thinking God does not see is disbelief.
BURSEVI:v2p129/r10.anchor: قال سليمان بن علي لحميد الطويل : عظني

BURSEVI:v2p129/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p129/r11.speaker: بعض الصالحين
BURSEVI:v2p129/r11.claim: A righteous teacher explained his special attention to one pupil by testing whether each student could kill a bird where no one could see; the pupil returned his bird alive because God sees everywhere.
BURSEVI:v2p129/r11.anchor: وكان بعض الصالحين له تلامذة وكان يخص واحدا منهم بإقباله عليه أكثر مما يقبل على غيره

ELMALILI:4:1-2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r1.claim: The opening warning is rendered as asking people to fear disobeying their Lord and to seek refuge in his nurturing and protection; the verse also has them appeal to God and kinship ties.
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r1.anchor: Sakının o Rabbinize karşı gelmekten ki sizleri bir tek nefisten yarattı

ELMALILI:4:1-2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r2.claim: Elmalılı describes the surah as covering divine rights and universal human brotherhood, care and rights of children, women and orphans, property, marriage, inheritance, and duties including purification, prayer, jihad, and obedience to authority; these rest on human nature and nurture.
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r2.anchor: Evvelinde hukūk-ı rabbâniye, uhuvvet-i âmme-i insâniye; evlâda, kadınlara, yetimlere re’fet ve şefkat ve hukuklarının edası, mallarının muhafazası, nikâh ve miras gibi husûsâta müte‘allik evâmir ve ahkâm ile başlamış

ELMALILI:4:1-2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r3.claim: The opening general address recalls al-Baqara's first general address, which commanded worship and argued from human creation, especially Adam; here taqwā is followed by the creation of woman, signaling that women's issues are a major duty.
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r3.anchor: O hitâb-ı âm ittikā gayesiyle اُعْبُدُوا رَبَّكُمْ emrini vermiş ve bunu hilkat-i beşeriye delilleriyle tenvir ederek hâlden mebde’e doğru götürmüş

ELMALILI:4:1-2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r4.claim: Only al-Nisāʾ and al-Ḥajj begin with the address to all people; their openings, each fourth in its half of the Qur'an, ground law respectively in creation's beginning and its end and the afterlife, showing the bases for their legal rulings.
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r4.anchor: Kur’an’da يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ matla‘ıyla başlayan iki sûre vardır. Birisi bu, diğeri Sûre-i Hac’dır.

ELMALILI:4:1-2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r5.speaker: Fahreddîn Râzî
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r5.claim: Al-Rāzī says that many subtle secrets lie beneath this discussion.
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r5.anchor: Fahreddîn Râzî der ki: “Bu bahsin altında esrâr-ı kesîre vardır.”

ELMALILI:4:1-2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r6.claim: To fear one's Lord is to enter under his nurturing and protection, submit generally to his command, avoid disobedience, and fear his punishment.
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r6.anchor: Rabbinizin hükm-i terbiye ve vikāyesine giriniz, emrine muhalefetten sakınıp umûmiyetle inzıbâta tâbi‘olunuz, ikābından korununuz

ELMALILI:4:1-2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r7.claim: Creation from one soul means all people descend from one father, share humanity, and are creatures of one Maker; rights should rest on humanity and nurture, with mutual brotherhood observed.
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r7.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh ‘an-asl hepiniz bir babadan gelme kardeşlersiniz ve hepiniz insansınız ve bir hâlıkın mahluklarısınız.

ELMALILI:4:1-2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r8.claim: Creating the spouse from the one soul was a bestowed gift and made a pair in which one comes from the other's life; 36:36 likewise says God created pairs.
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r8.anchor: Biri diğerinin canından kopmuş bir çift meydana getirdi سُبْحَٰنَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلْأَزْوَٰجَ كُلَّهَا

ELMALILI:4:1-2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r9.claim: The diversity of male and female offspring refutes nature as an autonomous fixed cause: neither sex simply repeats the other, while both are distinct complementary forms from one origin.
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r9.anchor: ne topraktan insan zuhur edebilirdi ne de bir erkekten bir dişi evlâd olabilirdi. Çünkü tabiat ıttırad demek değil ise hiçbir şey değildir.

ELMALILI:4:1-2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r10.claim: Even natural scientists acknowledge that pure nature cannot explain this diversity; a Lord above nature produces nurturing effects through creation and selection, so nature alone is no scientific first principle.
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r10.anchor: tabî‘at-ı mahza davası içinde bu tenevvü‘kābil-i îzah değildir. Ve kudret-i hâlıka tabiatın fevkinde terbiyevî bir tesir icrâ eden ve âsârını halk u ıstıfâ ile meydana getiren bir Rabb-i a‘lâdır.

ELMALILI:4:1-2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r11.claim: Iblīs was misled by reasoning from a supposed fiery nature when he claimed superiority over Adam, who was made from clay.
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r11.anchor: diye tabî‘at-ı nâriyeye binâ ettiği kıyasla aldanmıştır.

ELMALILI:4:1-2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r12.claim: At humanity's origin the evidence is clearest: the mind must locate the first cause beyond humans and material nature, in the Creator who made the spouse from one soul and then spread many men and women.
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r12.anchor: ne de tabî‘at-ı eşyâda görmemeli, hepsinin fevkinde Hâlık teâlâ’da görmelidir.

ELMALILI:4:1-2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r13.claim: Humanity's expansion from a single pair demonstrates God's lordship and ability to raise nations from one person; believers should fulfill duties, sacrifice for God's way, honor marriage, have children, nurture them, and avoid misusing sexual inclinations.
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r13.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh hiç yokken topraktan ıstıfâ ile insan yaratan ve o insandan eşini yaratan ve iki insandan bi’ttevâlüd erkek dişi birçok evlâd ve ahfâd yaratıp dünyaya yayan Hâlık teâlâ’nın rubûbiyeti

ELMALILI:4:1-2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r14.claim: The Prophet urged marriage and procreation, saying he would boast of his community before other nations on Resurrection Day, even through a miscarried child.
ELMALILI:4:1-2/r14.anchor: Resûlullah تـَنَاكَحُوا تـَنَاسَلُوا فَإِ ِّني أُبَاهِي بِكُمُ الأُْمَمَ يـَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَلَوْ بِال َّسقْطِ buyurmuştur.

ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r1.claim: He identifies the one soul as Adam and its spouse as Eve, reporting consensus on both identities.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r1.anchor: zevcinden murad da Hazret-i Havvâ olduğunda ittifak ve icmâ‘vardır.

ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r2.claim: Adam was created from dust by divine selection, as indicated by 3:33 and 3:59.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r2.anchor: Hazret-i Âdem إِنَّ ٱللَّهُ ٱصْطَفَىٰٓ ءَادَمَ [Âl-i İmrân 3/33] ve خَلَقَهُۥ مِن تُرَابٍۢ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ [Âl-i İmrân 3/59] medlûlü üzere topraktan bi’l-ıstıfâ halk olunmuş

ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r3.claim: Reports say Eve was created as a branch from Adam, expressing a splitting or bifurcation.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r3.anchor: Hazret-i Havvâ da nefs-i Âdem’den münşa‘ib olarak yaratılmıştır.

ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r4.claim: This branching expresses the foundation of the marital bond.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r4.anchor: bir inşikak mânası ifade eder. Ve bu mâna zevciyet alâkasının esası demektir.

ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r5.claim: A sound hadith compares woman to a crooked rib: trying to straighten it breaks it, and the break is divorce.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r5.anchor: Bir hadîs-i sahihde “Kadın bir dıl‘gibidir; kadın bir dıl‘dan

ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r6.claim: The crooked-rib image also signals natural difference between the sexes and warns that forcing women into male likeness breaks and discards them.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r6.anchor: dıl‘-ı a‘vec bu inşikāka işaretle beraber erkekle kadın beynindeki tehâlüf-i tabîata ve kadınların erkekleştirmeye kalkışılması onları kırıp atmak demek olduğuna tenbîhi hâvî bir temsildir.

ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r7.claim: Reports place the branching in the first creation in Paradise; 2:35 and 7:19 indicate the couple descended to earth afterward.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r7.anchor: cennetteki ibtidâ-yı hilkatte vâki‘olduğu da haberlerde vârid olmuş

ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r8.claim: Although Adam and Eve are certainly meant, the verse expresses the point through a broader concept.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r8.anchor: nefs-i vâhide Âdem, zevci de Havvâ olduğunda şüphe olmamakla âyet bunu e‘am bir mefhum ile ifade etmiştir.

ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r9.claim: The verse is more than a report: it adduces the presently observable course of human creation as evidence of divine power.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r9.anchor: âyet bu mânayı mücerred ihbar olarak değil, kudret-i rabbâniye delîli olmak üzere hâl-i hazırda mâlum ve meşhud olan cereyân-ı hilkati işhâd ederek ifade

ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r10.claim: Human generation begins with a father, while mothers receive fertilization from fathers.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r10.anchor: elyevm mevcut olan insanların hepsinin hilkati evvelâ birer babadan başlıyor, analar telkīhi babalardan alıyor.

ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r11.claim: Fathers do not produce only sons; female offspring also arise, contrary to a uniform pattern of nature.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r11.anchor: Fakat garibi o ki erkek olan babadan gelen evlâd hep erkek olmuyor. Bunda ıttırâd-ı tabîat kāidesi cereyan etmiyor.

ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r12.claim: The union of male and female produces many descendants, and one Adam becomes father of a family, tribe, and race; fathers cannot have children without wives.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r12.anchor: dünkü bir Âdem bir müddet sonra büyük bir ailenin, bir kabilenin, bir ırkın pederi oluyor, babalar eşsiz evlâd yapamıyor.

ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r13.claim: Because the male performs and the female receives fertilization, the author calls the male prior and the female secondary.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r13.anchor: Bu babda telkīhi yapan erkek ve alan kadın olmak haysiyetiyle erkek mukaddem, kadın tâlî bulunuyor.

ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r14.claim: Considering humanity across generations, he reasons that man is the first pillar and woman the second, so woman branches from man.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r14.anchor: hilkat-i beşerin her batnındaki mebde’ine nazaran erkek rükn-i evvel, kadın rükn-i sânî bulunduğundan evvelemirde kadının her hâlde erkekten teşa‘‘ub etmiş olduğu tahlîlî bir surette tebeyyün ediyor.

ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r15.claim: Reversing the geometric growth of descendants back to the origin establishes humanity as the pair Adam and Eve, joined by an original bond of the soul.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r15.anchor: riyâzî bir surette sâbit olur ki mebde’-i beşer Âdem ve Havvâ diye ifade edilen bir çifte

ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r16.claim: In that original bond man is prior and woman secondary, branching from his essence and spirit.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r16.anchor: Ve bu alâkada erkek evvel, kadın tâlîdir. Ve binâen‘aleyh o kadın o erkeğin nefsinden münşa‘ibdir, onun rûhundan kopmuştur.

ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r17.claim: The first branching was miraculous: the pair had no parents, and Eve's branching was unlike the branching of an ordinary child.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r17.anchor: bi’z-zarûre ana baba ile mesbuk değildirler

ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r18.claim: He compares the first pair to a seed bearing both sexes whose differently endowed parts attract one another and serve one purpose.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r18.anchor: birbirlerine telâkī etmek üzere mütekābil bir incizab besleyen ve müttehid bir gayeye hizmet eden muhtelif hâssıyetli fâil ve kābil

ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r19.claim: God's direct creation explains this extraordinary branching, just as divine creation explains the selection of humanity from earth.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r19.anchor: Bu ise topraktan ıstıfâ-yı beşerî gibi bizzat halkullah ile îzah olunur.

ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r20.claim: The rational deduction also depends on considering the earth's origination, discussed earlier.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r20.anchor: Bu istidlâlin tamam olması için arzın hudûsu mülâhazasını unutmamak lâzım gelir ki bu evvelce beyan olunmuş idi.

ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r21.claim: The verse's style combines transmitted teaching with a rational inference from the present back to the past.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r21.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh mazmûn-ı âyet hem naklî hem aklîdir.

ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r22.claim: The word minha implies male precedence, while zawj presents woman's creation as a great blessing that rescues man from loneliness and sterility.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r22.anchor: “Minhâ” kaydıyla erkeğin tekaddümünü ifham ederken aynı zamanda زَوْجَهَا mefhûmuyla da kadının yaratılışı erkeği yalnızlıktan ve ‘akāmetten kurtaran bir ni‘met-i uzmâ olduğunu

ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r23.speaker: Resûlullah
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r23.claim: The author cites the Prophet's saying that a righteous woman is the best of the world's goods.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r23.anchor: bir hadîs-i şerîfte Resûlullah “Dünya bir [1276] metâ‘ve dünya metâ‘ının en hayırlısı mer’e-i sâlihadır” buyurmuştur.

ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r24.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r24.claim: Because people are prone to misuse this blessing, they are first commanded and emphatically urged to fear God.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r24.anchor: İnsanlar bu nimeti sû’-i isti‘mâle müsta‘id bulunduklarından evvelâ ittikā emredilmiş ve şu suretle tekid de olunmuştur

ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r25.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r25.speaker: Âsım, Hamza ve Kisâî
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r25.claim: These readers recite tasa’alūna with an ungeminated s; the other readers geminate it, without a change in meaning.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r25.anchor: Âsım ve Hamza ve Kisâî kıraatlerinde س şeddesiz, mütebâkīsinde şeddeli okunur. Mâna birdir.

ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r26.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r26.speaker: Hamza
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r26.claim: Hamza reads the mīm of wa-l-arḥām with kasra, while other readers use fatḥa.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r26.anchor: وَٱلْأَرْحَامَ Hamza kıraatinde م esre, diğerlerinde üstün okunur.

ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r27.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r27.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r27.claim: One reading takes the phrase as fearing disobedience to God whose name people invoke in appeals, and neglecting the rights and dignity of kin.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r27.anchor: diye nâmına and verdiğiniz Allah’a isyan etmekten ve o rahimlerin hukūk u haysiyetini gözetmemekten

ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r28.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r28.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r28.claim: The second reading urges a divine and merciful ethic through which people invoke God and kinship when making requests of one another.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r28.anchor: ilâhî ve rahmânî bir ahlâk ile hareket ediniz ki, siz o Allah’a ve rahimlere and vererek yekdiğerinizden dilekleşirsiniz

ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r29.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r29.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r29.claim: He explains the second reading with an Arab appeal formula meaning, “I ask you by God and kinship.”
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r29.anchor: Araplar akrabalık hasebiyle mühim bir istirhamda bulunacakları zaman أَسْأَلُكَ بِااللهِ وَال َّرحِمِ derler imiş; “Allah ve rahim hakkı için recâ ederim” mânasınadır.

ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r30.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r30.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r30.claim: The second interpretation works with both readings, while the first applies only outside Hamza's reading.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r30.anchor: Bu ikinci mâna her iki kıraate göre de mümkindir. Fakat evvelki mâna Hamza kıraatinin mâ‘adâsındadır

ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r31.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r31.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r31.claim: The first interpretation makes the legal aspect explicit and the moral aspect implicit; the second reverses that emphasis.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#2/r31.anchor: Evvelkinde hukūkī nokta-i nazar sarih, ahlâkī nokta-i nazar zımnîdir. İkincisi de bilakistir.

ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r1.claim: Arḥām is the plural of raḥim, which means the womb but also extends to kinship and its causes.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r1.anchor: “Erhâm”; “Rahim”in cem‘i, “rahim” ح’nın kesriyle mâlum ki kadında çocuk yatağı olan uzv-i mahsustur. Fakat esbâb-ı karâbete ve akrabalığa dahi ıtlak olunur.

ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r2.claim: Ṣilat al-raḥim means kindness to relatives, while severing the womb means cutting the bond of kinship; here the word means kinship ties.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r2.anchor: “kat‘-ı rahim” alâka-i karâbeti kesmek demektir. Burada da esbâb-ı karâbet mânasınadır.

ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r3.claim: The word raḥim evokes love, mercy, compassion, and tenderness, which he describes as belonging to woman's created nature.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r3.anchor: “rahim” kelimesinin meveddet, merhamet, şefkat ve rikkat iş‘âr ettiği

ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r4.claim: Women should be treated tenderly, their honor and nature protected, and abuse or conduct that frustrates marriage's purpose prevented.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r4.anchor: kadınlara rikkat ü şefkatle muâmele etmek; şeref ü haysiyetleri, muktezâyı fıtratları muhafaza olunmak, tecavüzden ve sû’-i isti‘mâlden

ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r5.claim: Affection for household members and kin should be grounded in taqwa, the synthesis of love and fear of God.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r5.anchor: mahabbetullah ile mehâfetullâhın hâsılı demek olan ittikāullah esas ittihaz edilip

ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r6.claim: Selfish male or female desires contrary to creation and procreation, and relatives' wishes contrary to God's command, must not govern these relationships.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r6.anchor: ne erkeğin ne kadının hikmet-i halkına ve gāye-i tenâsüle muhalif olan hırs ve gurûr-ı nefsânîleri, ne de akrabânın emr-i ilâhîye mugāyir arzu ve temayülleri nazar-ı i‘tibâra alınmayıp

ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r7.claim: A hadith depicts kinship suspended from the Throne, asking God to care for whoever maintains it and abandon whoever severs it.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r7.anchor: “Rahim arşa asılmış, der ki: Beni gözeteni Allah gözetsin, beni terk edeni Allah terk etsin.”

ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r8.speaker: Allah
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r8.claim: A divine report says the Merciful derived the name raḥim from His own name and rewards those who maintain it while depriving those who sever it.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r8.anchor: Allah teâlâ diyor ki: “Ben, Rahmân’ım; o rahimdir. Ben ona ismimden bir isim müştak kıldım

ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r9.claim: A hadith says that maintaining kin brings the quickest reward among obedient deeds.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r9.anchor: Allah’a itaat edilen şeylerde sıla-i rahimden daha çabuk sevaplı hiçbir şey yoktur.

ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r10.claim: A report says charity and kinship ties lengthen life and ward off a bad death and harms.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r10.anchor: Sadaka ve sıla-i rahim, Allah bunlarla ömrü tezyîd eder ve kötü ölümü def‘eder, mahzur ve mekrûhu da def‘eder.

ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r11.claim: A hadith identifies the best charity as giving to a hostile relative.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r11.anchor: أَفْضَل ال َّصدَقَةِ عَلَى ذِي ال َّرحِمِ الْكَاشِحِ “Sadakanın efdali düşman olan akrabâya verilendir.”

ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r12.claim: The command to fear the Lord warns all people against violating universal brotherhood.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r12.anchor: ٱتَّقُوا۟ رَبَّكُمُ ale’l-umûm insanlar beynindeki uhuvvet-i âmmenin ihlâlinden

ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r13.claim: The second command to fear God warns against violating the rights and relationships of family and kin.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r13.anchor: وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ da aile ve akraba hukuk ve

ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r14.claim: People should fear disobeying God in both general and personal relationships because He watches all actions, speech, and intentions.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r14.anchor: Yani gerek münâsebât-ı umûmiye ve gerek münâsebât-ı husûsiyenizde Allah’a isyandan korkunuz

ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r15.claim: God is watchful over people, and none of their actions, words, or intentions are hidden from Him.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r15.anchor: her hâlde Allah üzerinizde gözcüdür. Bütün harekâtınız O’nun taht-ı murâkabesindedir. Ef‘âlinizden, akvâlinizden, niyetlerinizden hiçbiri O’ndan gizli kalamaz.

ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r16.claim: The verse's eloquence signals the surah's main themes and, following Āl ʿImrān, draws attention to repairing the causes of war losses.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r16.anchor: bu âyet-i kerîme, amîk bir belâgatle sûrenin muhteviyât-ı asliyesine işaret etmiş ve Sûre-i Âl-i İmrân’ı tâkip etmesi haysiyetiyle de zâyi‘ât-ı harbiyenin esbâb-ı telâfîsine nazar-ı dikkati celb eylemiştir.

ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r31.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r31.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r31.claim: The same hadith says oppression and false oaths are punished more quickly than other disobedient deeds.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r31.anchor: Allah’a isyan edilen amellerde[^31] de ukūbeti, bağyden ve yalan yere yeminden daha çabuk olan hiçbir amel yoktur.

ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r32.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r32.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r32.claim: The second part of the summary warns against misusing sexual attraction between men and women.
ELMALILI:4:1-2#3/r32.anchor: erkekle kadın beynindeki [1278] temâyülât-ı cinsiyenin sû’-i isti‘mâlinden

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r1.claim: The Qur’anic address “O people” targets all humanity, not believers alone.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r1.anchor: Kur’an-ı Kerîm’de “ey insanlar!” hitabının hedef kitlesi yalnızca müminler değil, bütün insanlardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r2.claim: The verse says to be mindful of your Lord rather than to avoid disrespecting God because Rabb fits the relation of human creation and development, while Allah or ilah fits worship and servitude.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r2.anchor: insanların yaratıcı ile kulluk ilişkisine “Allah ve ilâh”, insan olarak yaratılma ve geliştirilme ilişkilerine ise rab isminin uygun düşmesiyle izah etmek mümkündür.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r3.claim: Rabb denotes creating and granting the created being the ability to exist with particular qualities.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r3.anchor: bu isim, yaratmayı ve yaratılana belli özellikler içinde var oluş imkânı vermeyi ifade etmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r4.claim: The universal address is also shown by grounding human relations in two ties, one broad and one narrower: the shared nafs as original substance and the chain of wombs from Hawwa to each person’s mother.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r4.anchor: insanlar arasındaki ilişkilere –biri geniş, diğeri nispeten dar olan– iki unsuru temel kılmış olmasıdır: a) Bütün insanların asıl maddesi, özü olan “nefis”, b) İlk rahimden

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r5.claim: A common creator, origin, first parents, and later descent and family entail human rights and duties grounded in that unity; Surat al-Nisa explains many of these.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r5.anchor: Yaratanı bir, özü ve aslı bir, ilk oluşta anası babası bir, sonraki oluşlarda da soyu ve ailesi bir olan insanların yalnızca bu birlikten kaynaklanan birtakım hakları ve ödevleri

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r6.claim: Nafs can mean a human being, a person or thing itself, or the living element that makes a human human and continues eternal existence after death.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r6.anchor: Kur’an’da nefis (çoğulu enfüs), “insan, insanın veya başka bir şeyin kendisi, insanın hayatta iken insan olmasını sağlayan

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r7.speaker: Bazı âlimler, filozoflar ve sûfîler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r7.claim: Some scholars, philosophers, and Sufis explain spirit and nafs as two names for the same entity.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r7.anchor: Bazı âlimler, filozoflar ve sûfîler ruh ile nefsi aynı varlığın iki adı olarak açıklamışlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r8.speaker: Gazzâlî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r8.claim: Ghazali is cited as an example of those who treat spirit and nafs as two names for one entity.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r9.speaker: Bazıları
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r9.claim: Other scholars define nafs and spirit as entities of different natures.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r9.anchor: bazıları ise nefis ile ruhu farklı mahiyetler olarak tanımlamışlardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r10.speaker: Şah Veliyyullah
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r10.claim: Under the second definition, God creates an individual nafs for each person as well as a body; Shah Waliullah calls this nafs nasama, whose spiritual constitution and traits vary with a person’s deeds.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r10.anchor: Şah Veliyyullah’ın “neseme” adını verdiği bu nefis, insanın hayatı boyunca yapıp ettiklerine göre mânevî bir yapı ve kişilere göre farklı özellikler kazanır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r11.claim: Spirit is universal rather than personal, like electricity from one source lighting bulbs; it is divine, belongs to God and the command-world, not the created world.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r11.anchor: Ruh ise şahsî değil umumidir; tek bir enerji merkezinden gelip ampulleri aydınlatan elektrik gibidir ve ilâhîdir, Allah’a aittir, “halk âlemi”ne değil “emir âlemi”ne dahildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r12.claim: Spirit illuminates or draws the nafs toward the path that leads to God’s approval.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r12.anchor: nefis için Allah’ın rızâsına götüren yolu aydınlatır veya onu bu yola çeker.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r13.claim: Human nature also contains emotions, drives, and needs that pull against God’s approval, while Satan works to divert people from God’s path.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r13.anchor: İnsanın tabiatında ve yapısında Allah’ın rızâsına aykırı yola çeken güçler de (heyecanlar, güdüler, ihtiyaçlar) vardır, ayrıca şeytanın da işi, insanı Allah yolundan saptırmaya çalışmaktır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r14.claim: Through education and will, the human nafs struggles between these attractions and seeks to fulfill servitude and spiritual development in worldly life through trial.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r14.anchor: İnsan (nefis), aldığı eğitim ve iradesi sayesinde bu iki çekim merkezi arasında mücadele ve imtihan vererek dünya hayatında kulluğunu ve tekâmülünü gerçekleştirmeye çalışır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r15.claim: The nafs strives to rise from ammara, which commands evil, through self-reproaching, divinely inspired, tranquil, content, and God-approved stages.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r15.anchor: “emmâre” (kötüye çeken, kötüyü emreden) nefis olmaktan kurtularak, “levvâme” (kendini tenkit eden, kınayan), “mülheme” (ilâhî ilhama mazhar olan), “mutmainne”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r16.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r16.claim: Because every person has a mother and father and arises through reproduction, “from one nafs” and “from it” mean from its essence and a like kindred root, not a body part such as a rib.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r16.anchor: burada “nefisten, ondan yaratan” sözünü “onun bir parçasından” (meselâ kaburgasından) şeklinde değil, “onun özünden, ona benzer (misli) olan asıldan ve kökten

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r17.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r17.claim: Rūm 30:21 uses nafs for one’s own kind: God made spouses of your kind and placed love and compassion between you.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r17.anchor: “Onlara ısınıp kaynaşasınız diye size kendi türünüzden (nefislerinizden) eşler yaratıp aranıza sevgi ve şefkat duyguları yerleştirmesi de O’nun kanıtlarındandır” meâlindeki âyette de bu kelime aynı mânada kullanılmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r18.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r18.claim: Nahl 16:72 and Shura 42:11 use similar expressions for spouses and creation from one’s kind.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r18.anchor: Nahl (16 /72) ve Şûrâ (42/11) sûrelerinde de benzer ifadeler vardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r19.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r19.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r19.claim: These verses do not mean that a woman was made from a bodily part, so they cannot establish the widespread claim that Hawwa came from Adam’s rib.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r19.anchor: Bütün bu âyetlerde “nefsinden yaratmak”, “vücudunun bir parçasından yaratmak” mânasında değildir. Buna göre meâli ve numaraları verilen âyetler, Havvâ’nın aslının, Âdem’in kaburgası olduğu şeklindeki yaygın inancın delili olamaz.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r20.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r20.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r20.claim: Hadiths about woman being created from a crooked rib figuratively describe innate, enduring differences between women and men; some reports explicitly say woman is like a rib.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r20.anchor: Havvâ’nın veya kadınların eğri kaburgadan yaratıldığını ifade eden hadisler, kadınla erkeğin tabii (fıtrî) olan ve değişmemesi gereken farklılıklarını ve özelliklerini anlatmak üzere yapılmış bir benzetmedir, mecazî bir anlatımdır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r21.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r21.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r21.claim: Trying to make women resemble men and erase their natural characteristics is like trying to straighten a crooked rib: its curve makes it fitting, strong, complete, and able to protect the lung, while straightening it would spoil and break it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r21.anchor: Hadislere göre kadınları erkeklere benzetmeye, tabii özelliklerini yok etmeye kalkışmak, eğimli yaratılmış kaburga kemiğini düz hale getirmeye uğraşmak gibidir. Kaburga ancak kavisli olduğunda uygun, sağlam ve kâmildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r22.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r22.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r22.claim: After Adam and Hawwa were created, many men and women came from them and spread across the earth.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r22.anchor: Âdem ile Havvâ yaratıldıktan sonra bunlardan birçok erkek ve kadının meydana getirildiği ve yeryüzüne dağıtıldığı ifade buyurulmaktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r23.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
