KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r23.speaker: Tabâtabâî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r23.claim: Some exegetes propose that the first children were opposite-sex twins born in successive pairs and married across births, which God permitted because there was no other way.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r23.anchor: “birinci batında ikiz doğan bir erkek ve bir kızın, ikinci batında yine ikiz doğan bir kız ve bir erkekle evlendiklerini, o tarihte başka yolu bulunmadığı için Allah’ın farklı batınlarda doğan kardeşler arasında evlenmeyi câiz kıldığını ifade etmişlerdir (Tabâtabâî, IV, 146).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r24.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r24.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r24.claim: The author says the sibling-marriage scenario is unnecessary because Qur’anic descriptions show God creates humans in diverse ways.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r24.anchor: Bize göre böyle bir tasavvur zaruri değildir; çünkü Allah Teâlâ’nın insanı nasıl yarattığını açıklayan âyetlerde topraktan, çamurdan, nefisten ve Allah’ın ruhundan üflemesiyle yaratıldığı kayıtları ve şekilleri vardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r25.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r25.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r25.claim: The account of creation by breathing God’s spirit refers finally to Jesus, whose conception from Mary is described through the spirit and its appearance in human form.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r25.anchor: Son şekil Hz. Îsâ’nın yaratılmasıyla ilgilidir. Meryem, bir erkekle beraber olmadan Allah’ın ruhundan üflemesi (Enbiyâ 21/91; Tahrîm 66/12) ve bunun açıklaması mahiyetinde olan “ruhun insan şekline bürünüp Meryem’e görünmesi”yle (Meryem 19/17)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r26.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r26.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r26.claim: Mary bore Jesus as God’s word delivered to her, after conceiving without a man through the spirit from God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r26.anchor: hamile kalmış ve Allah’ın ona ulaştırdığı bir “kelimesi” (Nisâ 4/171) olarak Hz. Îsâ’yı doğurmuştur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r27.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r27.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r27.claim: Zakariya prayed for offspring; after hearing he would have Yahya, he asked how because he was old and his wife infertile, and God answered that He does what He wills and that it is easy.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r27.anchor: “İşte böyle; Allah dilediğini yapar” (Âl-i İmrân 3/40); “... O, bana kolaydır; daha önce, sen hiçbir şey değilken seni de yaratmıştım” (Meryem 19/9).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r28.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r28.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r28.claim: The examples show Adam had neither mother nor father, Jesus only a mother, and Yahya both parents despite their inability to conceive.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r28.anchor: Hz. Âdem’in yaratılmasında ana da yoktur baba da; Hz. Îsâ’nın yaratılmasında yalnızca ana vardır; Hz. Yahyâ’nın yaratılmasında ana ve baba vardır, fakat çocuk yapma kabiliyetleri mevcut değildir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r29.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r29.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r29.claim: Since neither the Qur’an nor sound reports say siblings married, the author prefers to leave unknown how the first pair produced many descendants; God may have used the stated forms or another way.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r29.anchor: Kur’an-ı Kerîm’de ve sağlam rivayetlerde “kardeşlerin birbiriyle evlendikleri” bilgisi verilmediğine göre ilk yaratılan erkekle kadından birçok erkek ve kadının türetilmesinin nasıl olduğunun bilinmediğini

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r30.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r30.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r30.claim: Mentioning care for kinship ties alongside avoiding disobedience to God clearly signals the high importance Islam gives to family relations.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r30.anchor: Akrabalık bağının (sıla-i rahim) hakkını vermemekten sakınmanın, Allah’ın emirlerine aykırı davranmaktan sakınma ile beraber zikredilmesi İslâm’da akrabalık ilişkisine ne kadar önem verildiğine güçlü ve açık bir işaret teşkil etmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r31.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r31.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r31.claim: The opening also signals that women connected to men as mothers, sisters, or wives deserve their rights, and frames this as obedience to God that spiritually reinforces the rules to follow.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:1/r31.anchor: Ayrıca bu giriş, sûrede “ana, kız kardeş, eş” gibi sıfatlarla erkeğe bağlı (aralarında akrabalık veya akid ilişkisi bulunan) kadınların haklarına riayet edilmesi gerektiğine ve bunun Allah’ın emirlerine riayet mahiyetinde olduğu hükmüne de işaret etmekte

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, and Ibn ʿĀmir read تساءلون with the first sīn doubled.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر: تساءلون* مشددة.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r2.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r2.claim: ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read تساءلون with a light sīn.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r2.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي: تساءلون مخففة.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r3.speaker: علي بن نصر وهارون بن موسى وعبيد بن عقيل وعبد الوهاب بن عطاء
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r3.claim: These transmitters report Abū ʿAmr reading the form lightly; al-Wāqidī via ʿAdī ibn al-Faḍl and Khārija ibn Muṣʿab also transmit the light form.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r3.anchor: واختلف عن أبي عمرو، فروى علي بن نصر وهارون بن موسى، وعبيد بن عقيل وعبد الوهاب بن عطاء عنه، والواقدي

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r4.speaker: اليزيدي وعبد الوارث
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r4.claim: Al-Yazīdī and ʿAbd al-Wārith transmit the doubled form from Abū ʿAmr; Abū Zayd reports both, while ʿAbbās permits either but says Abū ʿAmr reads lightly.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r4.anchor: وروى اليزيدي وعبد الوارث عنه: تساءلون* مشددة وروى أبو زيد عنه التخفيف والتشديد.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r5.claim: The doubled form comes from تتساءلون, with tāʾ assimilated to sīn because they share articulation near the tongue-tip and upper incisors and are both voiceless.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r5.anchor: من ثقل تساءلون* أراد: تتساءلون فأدغم التاء في السين،

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r6.claim: The light form drops one tāʾ from تتفاعلون because adjacent similar consonants are eased by deletion; such clusters can also be eased through assimilation or substitution.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r6.anchor: ومن خفف فقال: تساءلون، حذف تاء تتفاعلون لاجتماع حروف متقاربة، فأعلها بالحذف،

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r7.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r7.claim: The word طست illustrates substitution of a second sīn with tāʾ because of their closeness and shared voicelessness; al-ʿAjjāj's line is cited for طست.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r7.anchor: فالإبدال كقولهم: طست، أبدلت من السين الثانية التاء لتقاربهما واجتماعهما في الهمس، قال العجاج:

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r8.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r8.speaker: أبو عثمان
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r8.claim: Abū ʿUthmān cites a verse whose final word الطس illustrates the same consonant pattern.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p118#3/r8.anchor:
وأنشد أبو عثمان:
لو عرضت لأيبلي قس ... أشعث في هيكله مندس

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p121/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p121/r1.speaker: حمزة
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p121/r1.claim: Ḥamza reads والأرحام in the genitive; the other readers read it in the accusative.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p121/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p121/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p121/r2.claim: The accusative can coordinate with the syntactic position of the prepositional phrase, or with واتقوا, meaning to honor kinship ties and not sever them.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p121/r2.anchor: من نصب الأرحام احتمل انتصابه وجهين:

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p121/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p121/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p121/r3.claim: The genitive reading coordinates الأرحام with the pronoun governed by bāʾ; Abū ʿAlī considers this weak in analogy and rare in usage, so prefers avoiding it.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p121/r3.anchor: وأما من جر الأرحام فإنه عطفه على الضمير المجرور بالباء.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p121/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p121/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p121/r4.claim: A bound pronoun replaces tanwīn and is too closely attached to its noun for a ظاهر noun to coordinate with it, unlike a visible genitive complement that can be separated by an adverb.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p121/r4.anchor: فإن الضمير قد صار عوضا مما كان متصلا باسم نحو غلامه وغلامك،

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p179/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p179/r1.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن عبد الله بن يزيد
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p179/r1.claim: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd reads والأرحام in the nominative.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p179/r1.anchor: قراءة أبي عبد الرحمن عبد الله بن يزيد1: "الذي تساءلون به والأرحام"2 رفعا

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p179/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p179/r2.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p179/r2.claim: He parses nominative الأرحام as a topic with an omitted predicate: the kinship ties are also something people must revere and protect; this raises their emphasis above an accusative or genitive adjunct.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p179/r2.anchor: أي: والأرحام مما يجب أن تتقوه، وأن تحتاطوا لأنفسكم فيه، وحسن رفعه لأنه أوكد في معناه

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p179/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p179/r3.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p179/r3.claim: An omitted predicate is recoverable from context, whereas deleting an accusative or genitive الأرحام would leave no indication that kinship ties were intended; raising the phrase emphasizes it, as in al-Farazdaq’s complaint.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p179/r3.anchor: وكلما3 قويت الدلالة على المحذوف كان حذفه أسوغ

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p179/r4.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p179/r4.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p179/r4.claim: A separate semantic explanation of the raised poetic phrase treats both coordinated descriptions as remaining after the speaker called only for one of them.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p179/r4.anchor: ومن حمله على المعنى فرفعه وقال: إذا لم يدع إلا مسحتا فقد بقي المسحت وبقي أيضا المجلف

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118/r4.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118/r4.claim: The light reading of تساءلون drops one of the two tāʾs from تتساءلون; the geminated reading assimilates the second tāʾ into sīn.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118/r4.anchor: فالحجة لمن خفف أنه أراد تتساءلون فأسقط إحدى التاءين تخفيفا والحجة لمن شدد أنه أسكن التاء الثانية وأدغمها في السين

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r1.claim: The Basran objection says an overt noun cannot coordinate with a genitive pronoun unless the preposition is repeated, since the pronoun and its preposition form one unit.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r1.anchor: إلا بإعادة الخافض لأنه معه كشيء واحد لا ينفرد منه ولا يحال بينه وبينه ولا يعطف عليه غلا بإعادة الخافض

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r2.claim: The Basrans also appeal to the rule against coordinating an unemphasized noun with a raised pronoun and to the Prophetic prohibition on swearing by anyone besides God.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r2.anchor: وأيضا فإن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم نهانا أن نحلف بغير الله فكيف ننهى عن شيء ويؤتى به

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r3.speaker: البصريون
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r3.claim: The Basrans reject treating the genitive as poetic license because the Qur'an contains no place of metrical necessity.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r3.anchor: وليس في القرآن بحمد الله موضع اضطرار هذا احتجاج البصريين

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r4.speaker: الكوفيون
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r4.claim: The Kufans permit the genitive by supplying an omitted preposition, and support the reader on that analysis.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r4.anchor: فأما الكوفيون فأجازوا الخفض واحتجوا للقارئ بأنه أضمر الخافض

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r5.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r5.speaker: العجاج
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r5.claim: Al-ʿAjjāj's answer خير means بخير, illustrating an omitted preposition in ordinary speech.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r5.anchor: بأن العجاج كان إذا قيل له كيف تجدك يقول خير عافاك الله يريد بخير

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r6.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r6.claim: A cited poetic line supplies another example of an omitted preposition: its opening رسم is understood as ورب رسم.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r6.anchor: وأنشد رسم دار وقفت في طلله كدت أقضي الحياة من خلله

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r7.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r7.claim: Another interpretation is to fear God regarding kinship ties, by not severing them.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم معناه واتقوه في الأرحام أن تقطعوها

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r8.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r8.speaker: الكوفيون
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r8.claim: Although the Kufans allow and defend the genitive, they still choose the accusative reading.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p118#2/r8.anchor: إلا أنهم مع إجازتهم ذلك واحتجاجهم للقارئ به يختارون النصب في القراءة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p226/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p226/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p226/r1.claim: They read تساءلون with a doubled sīn; Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisai use the light form.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p226/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر ﴿ تساءلون به ﴾ مشددة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p226/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p226/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p226/r2.claim: Abu Amr varies by transmitter: several report the light form, al-Yazidi and Abd al-Warith the doubled form, Abu Zayd both, and Abbas permits either but says he read light.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p226/r2.anchor: وروى اليزيدي وعبد الوارث عنه ﴿ تساءلون ﴾ مشددة وروى أبو زيد عنه التخفيف والتشديد

IBNMUJAHID:v1p226/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p226/r3.speaker: حمزة
IBNMUJAHID:v1p226/r3.claim: Hamza alone reads والأرحام in the genitive; the other readers use the accusative.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p226/r3.anchor: فقرأ حمزة وحده ﴿ والأرحام ﴾ خفضا وقرأ الباقون ﴿ والأرحام ﴾ نصبا

QIRAAT-ER:4:1:26#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:4:1:26#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:4:1:26#1/r1.claim: Assimilation of tāʾ into sīn shortens tatasāʾalūna to tassāʾalūna without changing the Form VI meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:4:1:26#1/r1.anchor: Assimilation of tāʾ into sīn: tatasāʾalūna → tassāʾalūna — phonological simplification, same Form VI meaning

QIRAAT-ER:4:1:29#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:4:1:29#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:4:1:29#1/r1.claim: The genitive arḥāmi is governed by the implied bi in bihi, making the wombs objects of oath or invocation alongside God.
QIRAAT-ER:4:1:29#1/r1.anchor: wombs become objects of oath/invocation alongside God

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p145/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p145/r1.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p145/r1.claim: Al-Hasan explains “asking one another by God and by kinship” as someone saying, “I implore you by God and by the ties of kinship.”
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p145/r1.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله تعالى ﴿ واتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به والأرحام ﴾ قال هو قول الرجل أنشدك الله الرحم

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p145/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p145/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p145/r2.claim: Qatada reports hearing that the Prophet said to fear God and maintain ties of kinship.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p145/r2.anchor: عن قتادة قال بلغني أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال اتقوا الله وصلوا الأرحام

QASHANI:4:1/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:1/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:1/r1.claim: Fear God by not claiming His attributes for your good deeds; treat Him as your protection and recognize that good issues from the absolutely powerful.
QASHANI:4:1/r1.anchor: احذروه في انتحال صفته عند صدور الخيرات منكم، واتخذوا الصفة وقاية لكم

QASHANI:4:1/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:1/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:1/r2.claim: The single soul is the universal rational soul, the heart of the world and the real Adam.
QASHANI:4:1/r2.anchor: هي النفس الناطقة الكلية، التي هي قلب العالم، وهو آدم الحقيقي

QASHANI:4:1/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:1/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:1/r3.claim: The spouse is the animal soul that emerges from the rational soul.

QASHANI:4:1/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:1/r4.speaker: قيل
QASHANI:4:1/r4.claim: Another view says the spouse was created from Adam’s left rib on the side facing the created world; without her he would not have descended, and Satan used her to tempt him. Bodily attachment occurs only through her.
QASHANI:4:1/r4.anchor: وقيل: إنها خلقت من ضلعه الأيسر من الجهة التي تلي عالم الكون

QASHANI:4:1/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:1/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:1/r5.claim: The many men are people of heart who incline toward their father, while women are people of soul and temperament who incline toward their mother.
QASHANI:4:1/r5.anchor: أصحاب قلوب ينزعون إلى أبيهم { ونساء } أصحاب نفوس وطبائع ينزعون إلى أمهم

QASHANI:4:1/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:1/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:1/r6.claim: Fear God in His essence by affirming no independent existence of your own, and make Him your protection when remnants of self appear during annihilation in unity, so they do not veil you.
QASHANI:4:1/r6.anchor: في ذاته عن إثبات وجودكم، واجعلوه وقاية لكم عند ظهور البقية منكم في الفناء في التوحيد

QASHANI:4:1/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:1/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:1/r7.claim: The phrase “by whom you ask one another” means asking through God, not through yourselves.

QASHANI:4:1/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:1/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:1/r8.claim: The real wombs are relations to high principles, separate spirits, and the spirits of prophets and saints; cutting them by withholding love turns unity into separation and estranges one from God.
QASHANI:4:1/r8.anchor: أقربة المبادئ العالية من المفارقات وأرواح الأنبياء والأولياء في قطعها بعدم المحبة

QASHANI:4:1/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:1/r9.speaker: رسول الله
QASHANI:4:1/r9.claim: The Prophet says that maintaining kinship increases lifespan, meaning it brings lasting subsistence.
QASHANI:4:1/r9.anchor: قال عليه الصلاة والسلام: " صلة الرحم تزيد في العمر "

QASHANI:4:1/r10.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:1/r10.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:1/r10.claim: Outward kinship images inner connection; the outward rule in unity reflects the inward one, so failure to honor outward kinship predicts failure to honor the inward.
QASHANI:4:1/r10.anchor: الرحم من الظاهر صورة الاتصال الحقيقي في الباطن، وحكم الظاهر في التوحيد كحكم الباطن، فمن لا يقدر

QASHANI:4:1/r11.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:1/r11.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:1/r11.claim: God watches so that people do not become veiled by a manifested attribute or remnant of self and suffer its torment.
QASHANI:4:1/r11.anchor: يراقبكم لئلا تحتجبوا عنه بظهور صفة من صفاتكم، أو بقية من بقاياكم

QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r1.claim: Some derive the word name from elevation and others from a mark; both derivations support inward readings.
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r1.anchor: قال إنه مشتق من السمو وهو العلو ، ومنهم من قال إنه مشتق من السمة وهي الكبة

QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r2.claim: Under the elevation derivation, remembering God raises one's rank, knowing Him raises one's state, and companionship with Him raises one's aspiration; these bring abundant rewards, inward lights, and escape from base attachments.
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r2.anchor: فمن قال إنه مشتق من السمو فهو اسم من ذكره سمت رتبته ، ومن عرفه سمت حاللته ، ومن صحبه سمت همته

QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r3.claim: Under the mark derivation, seeking God marks one with worship, companionship with intention, love with the mark of the elect, and knowledge with the mark of the chosen.
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r3.anchor: ومن قال أصله من السمة فهو اسم من قصده وسم بسمة العبادة ، ومن صحبه وسم بسمة الإرادة

QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r4.claim: The worshipper's mark protects from the fire, the seeker is too honored for the Garden to enslave him, and the elect's mark removes self-conceit about deserving closeness.
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r4.anchor: فسمة العبادة توجب هيبة النار أن ترمي صاحبها بشررها ، وسمة الإرادة توجب حشمة الجنان

QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r5.claim: The mark of the special ones is the heart's grief of separation; union with God elevates His rank beyond imagining, while distance brands the heart with separation.
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r5.anchor: وسمة وسم بكي الفرقة قلبه . ويقال اسم من واصله سما عنده ( عن ) الأوهام قدره ( سبحانه )

QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r6.claim: The word people is a collective noun, and its derivation is not strong.
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r6.anchor: الناس اسم جنس ، والاشتقاق فيه غير قوي

QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r7.claim: It is said that insan derives from visibility; inwardly, people appeared from nonexistence under obligation, while God honors some with knowledge and guidance and disposes of all as He wills.
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r7.anchor: وقيل سمي الإنس إنسا لظهوره فعلى هذه الإشارة : يا من ظهرتم عن كتم العدم بحكم تكليفي

QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r8.claim: It is said God brought people forth from nonexistence as their likenesses and disclosed to no one else the states He disclosed to them.
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r8.anchor: ويقال لم أظهر من العدم أمثالكم ، ولم أظهر على أحد ما أظهرت عليكم من أحوالكم

QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r9.claim: It is said insan derives from forgetfulness: forgetting God is the lowest condition and forgetting His remembrance the most abased state.
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r9.anchor: ويقال سميت إنسانا لنسيانك ، فإن نسيتني فلا شيء أخس منك ، وإن نسيت ذكري فلا أحد أحط منك

QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r10.claim: Whoever forgets the Real has no end to tribulation, while whoever forgets creation has no end to spiritual elevation.
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r10.anchor: من نسي الحق فلا غاية لمحنته ، ومن نسي الخلق فلا نهاية لعلو حالته

QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r11.claim: God calls sinners who forgot His covenant, rejected His love, and exceeded His limits back to His door to receive gentleness and favor.
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r11.anchor: يا من نسيت عهدي ، ورفضت ودي ، وتجاوزت حدي حان لك أن ترجع إلى بابي

QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r12.claim: God tells the knowers who forgot their own share in Him and turned from all else that their right, support, and rank have become great with Him.
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r12.anchor: يا من نسيت فينا حظك ، وصت عن غيرنا لحظك ولفظك - لقد عظم علينا حقك

QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r13.claim: One who delights in the breeze of nearness, rests in witnessing God's face, and gains honor from His majesty is the most honored servant.
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r13.anchor: يا من أنست بنسيم قربي ، واستروحت إلى شهود وجهي ، واعتززت بجلال قدري

QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r14.claim: Taqwa encompasses all obedience, beginning with avoiding associationism and culminating in avoiding every other-than-God; the first other is one's own self.
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r14.anchor: التقوى جماع الطاعات ، وأوله ترك الشرك وآخره اتقاء كل غير ، وأول الأغيار لك نفسك

QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r15.claim: One who guards against the self stands with God without claiming a station or witnessing a spiritual state.
QUSHAYRI:v1p193/r15.anchor: ومن اتقى نفسه وقف مع الله بلا مقام ولا شهود حال

QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r1.claim: The one who stands for God does so without seeking a share in this world or the next.
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r1.anchor: لا لشهود حظ في الدنيا والعقبى

QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r2.claim: The one soul is Adam; since he was created by God's hand, those descended from him share this distinction and are the best of creation.
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r2.anchor: وهو آدم عليه السلام ، وإذا كنا مخلوقين منه وهو مخلوق باليد فنحن أيضا كذلك

QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r3.claim: The word soul is generic, and its generic sense implies exhaustive inclusion.
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r3.anchor: ولفظ ( النفس ) للعموم والعموم يوجب الاستغراق

QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r4.claim: God made creatures dwell with one another so lineage could continue and like could return to like by pairing form with form.
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r4.anchor: حكم الحق - سبحانه - بمساكنة الخلق مع الخلق لبقاء النسل ، ولرد المثل إلى المثل

QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r5.claim: Creating all humanity from one person despite their varied bodies, appearances, characters, aspirations, and conditions proves God's power, lordship, and wisdom.
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r5.anchor: تعرف إلى العقلاء على كمال القدرة بما ألاح من براهين الربوبية ودلالات الحكمة

QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r6.claim: No two people resemble one another in appearance, character, aspiration, and condition, demonstrating the limitless scope of God's power and knowledge.
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r6.anchor: وإن اثنين منهم لا يتشابهان ، فلكل وجه في الصورة والخلق ، والهمة والحالة

QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r7.claim: Repeating the command to fear God emphasizes its force.
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r7.anchor: ثم قال : { واتقوا الله } تكريرالأمر بالتقوى يدل على تأكيد حكمه

QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r8.claim: The instruction concerning God and kinship means to avoid severing family ties: whoever cuts them is cut off, and whoever joins them is joined.
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r8.anchor: أي اتقوا الأرحام أن تقطعوها ، فمن قطع الرحم قطع ، ومن وصلها وصل

QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r9.claim: God's watching means He witnesses and counts breaths, sees the senses, oversees thoughts, and originates movements and stillness.
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r9.anchor: مطلعا شهيدا ، يعد عليك أنفاسك ، ويرى حواسك ، وهو متول خطراتك

QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r10.claim: Knowing that God watches over someone should make that person ashamed before Him.
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r10.anchor: ومن علم أنه رقيب عليه فبالحري أن يستحي منه

QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r11.claim: God litigates against a caretaker who violates those in his care and avenges servants more than He avenges Himself; a just and kind orphan guardian has a claim with God, while an abusive one faces God as adversary.
QUSHAYRI:v1p194/r11.anchor: فجاء على رعيته فخصمه ربه ؛ فإنه - سبحانه - ينتقم لعباده ما لا ينتقم لنفسه

ALUSI-FULL:v4p179/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179/r1.claim: The address يا أيها الناس applies to accountable people from the revelation of the verse until the Day of Judgment.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179/r1.anchor: خطاب يعم المكلفين من لدن نزل إلى يوم القيامة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p179/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179/r2.claim: Most jurists say slaves are included in a general address to people because a slave is one of the people and servitude does not itself bar inclusion.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179/r2.anchor: فذهب الأكثرون إلى التناول لأن العبد من الناس مثلا فيدخل في الخطاب العام له قطعا

ALUSI-FULL:v4p179/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179/r3.claim: Some jurists exclude slaves: since their benefits belong to their masters by consensus, a command using their time for another’s benefit would conflict with that rule; their exclusion from jihad, Friday prayer, pilgrimage, and donations is also cited.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179/r3.anchor: وذهب البعض إلى عدم التناول قالوا : لأنه قد ثبت بالإجماع صرف منافع العبد إلى سيده

ALUSI-FULL:v4p179/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179/r4.claim: The author replies that the master does not own every benefit: near the end of the noon-prayer window, the slave must pray even if obeying the master would make the prayer lapse.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179/r4.anchor: بل قد يستثنى من ذلك وقت تضايق العبادات حتى لو أمره السيد في آخر وقت الظهر

ALUSI-FULL:v4p179/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179/r5.claim: Exclusion from some commands does not prove slaves were outside the general address: specific evidence can exclude them, just as illness or travel excludes people from general commands about fasting, prayer, and jihad.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179/r5.anchor: بأن خروجه بدليل أقتضى خروجه وذلك كخروج المريض والمسافر والحائض عن العمومات

ALUSI-FULL:v4p179/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179/r6.claim: Earlier peoples are not included in this address, since commands and prohibitions address those able to comply, whereas earlier generations lie under the earth until the trumpet is blown.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179/r6.anchor: أن الأمم الدارجة قبل نزول هذا الخطاب لاحظ لها فيه لاختصاص الأوامر والنواهي بمن يتصور منه الامتثال

ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r1.claim: Some include earlier peoples in the address and in the coming command in God’s eternal speech, though its Arabic form is incidental to this community; the author objects that the discussion concerns Quranic rulings after revelation, or all direct address would be metaphorical.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r1.anchor: وجوز بعضهم كون الخطاب عاما بحيث يندرجون فيه ثم قال : ولا يبعد

ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r2.claim: The word الناس includes males and females by agreement, but whether a masculine plural command such as اتقوا ربكم includes women is disputed; most say it does not apparently, unlike the Hanbalis.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r2.anchor: وفي شمول نحو قوله تعالى : ( أتقوا ربكن ( خلاف

ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r3.speaker: أم سلمة
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r3.claim: Umm Salama reports that women asked why God mentioned only men, after which a verse mentioning women was revealed; the majority infer that women were not already included in the apparent wording.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r3.anchor: عن أم سلمة أنها قالت : يارسول الله إن النساء قلن

ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r4.claim: The majority also argue that Arabic grammarians classify this form as masculine plural and that adding women in the Quranic phrase المسلمين والمسلمات would be redundant if women were already included in its apparent sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r4.anchor: وبأنه قد أجمع أرباب العربية على أن نحو هذه الصيغة جمع مذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r5.claim: Those who include women argue that Arabic convention lets the masculine dominate when the sexes are combined; otherwise women would miss many shared legal rulings, and a bequest to men and women followed by “I bequeathed to them” includes both.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r5.anchor: المعروف من أهل اللسان تغليبهم المذكر على المؤنث

ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r6.claim: The report from Umm Salama only proves that the wording can be used for everyone when that is intended; the majority call that figurative, so it does not establish universal apparent meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r6.anchor: فبأنه إنما يدل على أن الإطلاق صحيح إذا قصد الجميع والجمهور يقولون به لكنه يكون مجازا

ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r7.claim: The argument from shared legal rulings fails: women can participate through separate evidence, as they do not enter rules for jihad or Friday prayer without such evidence.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r8.claim: The bequest example does not establish immediate inclusion without context, because the preceding bequest itself signals the intended referent.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r8.anchor: فإن الوصية المتقدمة قرينة دالة على الإرادة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r9.claim: The author concludes that women are not included in the apparent meaning of the masculine form, though here it is preferable to include them through grammatical predominance.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r9.anchor: فالحق عدم دخول الإناث ظاهرا نعم الأولى هنا القول بدخولهن باعتبار التغليب

ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r10.claim: A view that the command addresses men alone and includes women only through external evidence would require restricting الناس, which the author says sound taste rejects.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r10.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن لا تغليب بل الأمر للرجال فقط كما يقتضيه ظاهر الصيغة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r11.claim: The command to practice taqwa may broadly mean avoiding disbelief, sins, and vices while honoring both human and divine rights.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p179#2/r11.anchor: والمأمور به إما الإتقاء بحيث يشمل ما كان بإجتناب الكفر والمعاصي

ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r1.claim: Alternatively, taqwa means protecting the rights owed among people; this specifically fits the surah’s concerns with orphans, kinship, marital justice, and inheritance, while the broader reading fits only generally.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r1.anchor: وأما الإتقاء في الإخلال بما يجب حفظه من الحقوق فيما بين العباد

ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r2.claim: Calling God “your Lord” supports the command and reinforces the duty to obey.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r2.anchor: وفي التعرض لعنوان الربوبية مع الإضافة إلى ضمير المخاطبين ما لا يخفى من تأييد الأمر

ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r3.claim: Describing God as the one who created the addressees from one soul functions as a reason for the command; it points either to immense power or great favor, prompting piety through fear or gratitude.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r3.anchor: لأن ما ذكر يدل على القدرة العظيمة أو النعمة الجسيمة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r4.claim: Creation from one origin especially makes piety compelling if the description is understood as a reminder of favor and the gratitude owed for it.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r4.anchor: وإيجاب الخلق من أصل واحد للإتقاء على الإحتمال الثاني ظاهر جدا

ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r5.claim: The description also reminds the addressees that they know these facts that call for piety, and rebukes anyone who nevertheless neglects it.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r5.anchor: وفي الوصف المذكور تنبيه على أن المخاطبين عالمون بما ذكر مما يستدعي التحلي بالتقوى

ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r6.claim: The one soul is Adam, whom the mainstream jurists and traditionists regard as the sole first human and father of humankind.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r6.anchor: والمراد من النفس الواحدة آدم عليه السلام والذي عليه الجماعة من الفقهاء والمحدثين

ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r7.speaker: صاحب جامع الأخبار
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r7.claim: A report in Jamiʿ al-Akhbar says God created thirty Adams, with a thousand years between each, followed by fifty thousand years of desolation, fifty thousand years of habitation, and then our father Adam.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r7.anchor: ذكر صاحب جامع الأخبار من الإمامية في الفصل الخامس عشر خبرا طويلا نقل فيه أن الله تعالى خلق قبل أبينا آدم ثلاثين آدم

ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r8.speaker: الصادق
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r8.claim: A long report in Ibn Babawayh’s al-Tawhid quotes al-Sadiq saying God created a million Adams and that this humanity is the last of them.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r8.anchor: وروى إبن بابويه في كتاب التوحيد عن الصادق

ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r9.speaker: محمد بن علي الباقر
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r9.claim: Al-Maytham’s commentary on the Nahj quotes Muhammad al-Baqir saying a million or more Adams preceded our father Adam.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r9.anchor: ونقل عن محمد بن علي الباقرأنه قال : قد إنقضى قبل آدم

ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r10.speaker: ابن عربي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r10.claim: The author says Ibn Arabi’s Futuhat appears to imply that another Adam existed forty thousand years before ours.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r10.anchor: وذكر الشيخ الأكبر قدس سره في فتوحاته ما يقتضي بظاهره أن قبل آدم بأربعين ألف سنة آدم غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r11.speaker: الصادق
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r11.claim: A report in al-Khasaʾis quotes al-Sadiq saying God has twelve thousand worlds, each larger than seven heavens and seven earths, and each unaware of the other worlds.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r11.anchor: عن الصادق أنه قال : إن لله تعالى إثني عشر ألف عالم

ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r12.claim: The author suggests such reports may belong to esoteric or imaginal material; if they are sound, multiple Adams there need not mean multiple Adams in this world.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r12.anchor: ولعل هذا وأمثاله من أزض السمسمة وجابر ساوجا بلقا إن صح محمول على عالم المثال

ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r13.speaker: زين العرب
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r13.claim: The author says Sunnis reject literal multiple Adams; Zayn al-Arab even declared a believer in multiple Adams an unbeliever.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r13.anchor: بل قد صرح زين العرب بكفر من يعتقد التعدد

ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r14.claim: Our Adam was preceded by other creations such as angels, jinn, and many animals, but not other humans like him; humanity began in time, contrary to philosophers who claim its species is eternal.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r14.anchor: آدمنا هدا عليه السلام مسبوق بخلق آخرين كالملائكة والجن

ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r15.claim: Many Sunnis held that six thousand years elapsed before the Prophet and that the world lasts seven thousand years, relying on many reports.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r15.anchor: وذهب الكثير منا إلى أنه منذ كان إلى زمن البعثة ستة آلاف سنة وأن عمر الدنيا سبعة آلاف سنة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r16.claim: The author holds that the world began after not existing and will end; when it began and ends is known only to God, and the reports on its timing are too contradictory to rely on.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p180/r16.anchor: والحق عندي أنه كان بعد أن لم يكن ولا يكون بعد أن كان

ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r1.claim: The author rejects as neither sound creed nor certainty the claim that a universal soul judges individual souls every seven thousand years and that the Hour follows the thousandth resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r1.anchor: مما لا أزتضيه دينا ولا أختاره يقينا

ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r2.claim: ربكم and خلقكم address those commanded; extending them to earlier nations while the earlier address excluded them needlessly splits the syntax, since God’s lordship and creation of the addressees already encompass their ancestors.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r2.anchor: للمأمورين وتعميمه بحيث يشمل الأمم السالفة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r3.claim: Mentioning the addressees’ creation through Adam and their intervening parents also implicitly recognizes all those ancestral links, as does mentioning God’s lordship over them.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r3.anchor: لأن خلقه تعالى للمأورين من نفس آدم عليه السلام حيث كانوا

ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r4.claim: The phrase وخلق منها زوجها coordinates with خلقكم inside the relative clause; repeating the verb distinguishes derivation from the original from creating a mate out of material.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r4.anchor: وهو عطف على ( خلقكم ) داخل معه في حيز الصلة وأعيد الفعل

ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r5.claim: The mate is Eve, created from Adam’s left rib, as reported from Ibn Umar and others.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r5.anchor: فإن المراد من الزوج حواء وهي قد خلقت من ضلع آدم عليه السلام الأيسر كما روى ذلك عن ابن عمر وغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r6.speaker: النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r6.claim: The two Sahih collections transmit the Prophet’s counsel to treat women well because they were created from a rib; its upper part is most crooked, and trying to straighten it breaks it while leaving it preserves its crookedness.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r6.anchor: وروى الشيخان استوصوا بالنساء خيرا فإنهن خلقن من ضلع وإن أعوج شيء من الضلع أعلاه

ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r7.speaker: أبو مسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r7.claim: Abu Muslim denies that Eve was created from Adam’s rib, arguing that God could create her from dust and interpreting منها as “of the same kind,” like the phrase in 16:72.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r7.anchor: وأنكر أبو مسلم خلقها من الضلع لأنه سبحانه قادر على خلقها من التراب

ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r8.claim: Some agree with Abu Muslim, saying the rib interpretation would mean Adam had intercourse with part of himself, which they find repugnant.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r8.anchor: ووافقه على ذلك بعضهم مدعيا أن القول بما ذكر يجر إلى القول بأن آدم عليه السلام كان ينكح بعضه بعضا

ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r9.claim: Another view says Eve was a heavenly maiden created from the same substance as houris after Adam entered the Garden.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r9.anchor: وزعم بعض أن حواء كانت حورية خلقت مما خلق منه الحور بعد أن أسكن آدم الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r10.claim: The author rejects the houri view because no Quranic verse or hadith even hints at it; if houris were made from Paradise saffron, Eve would differ in kind from Adam, and if from Adam’s substance, the claim collapses into Abu Muslim’s position.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r10.anchor: أما الثاني فلأنه ليس في الآيات ولا الأحاديث ما يتوهم منه الإشارة إليه أصلا

ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r11.claim: The author rejects Abu Muslim’s view because then humanity would come from two souls instead of the single soul stated here, and it conflicts with authentic Prophetic reports; this also undermines the houri view.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p181/r11.anchor: وأما الأول فلأنه لو كان الأمر كما ذكر فيه لكان الناس مخلوقين من نفسين لا من نفس واحدة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p182/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p182/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p182/r1.claim: Creating Eve from Adam demonstrates that God can create a living being from another living being, just as He creates from lifeless matter; human generation likewise occurs although Adam could have been created directly from earth.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p182/r1.anchor: إظهار أنه سبحانه قادر على أن يخلق حيا من حي لا على سبيل التوالدكما أنه قادر على أن يخلق حيا من جماد كذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v4p182/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p182/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p182/r2.claim: The alleged impropriety of Eve's rib-origin is only a groundless intuition: the part's original identity disappeared, and the wisdom of this particular union supports it.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p182/r2.anchor: هذا التشخص الخاص الحاصل لذلك الجزء بحيث لم يبق من تشخصه الأصلي شيء ظاهر يدفع الإستهجان الذي لا مقتضى له إلا الوهم الخالص

ALUSI-FULL:v4p182/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p182/r3.speaker: الشيخ الأكبر
ALUSI-FULL:v4p182/r3.claim: The Shaykh al-Akbar describes Eve's separation as leaving a void filled by sexual desire: Adam sought its airy occupant, found Eve, and their union began procreation; human union also mirrors the higher cosmic pairing of the First Intellect and Universal Soul.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p182/r3.anchor: فقد ذكر الشيخ الأكبر قدس سره أن حواء لما أنفصلت من آدم عمر موضعها منه بالشهوة النكاحية التي بها وقع الغشيان

ALUSI-FULL:v4p182#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p182#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p182#2/r1.claim: The preceding discussion suggests this manner of creation was unique to Adam and Eve rather than other animal pairs, but the author has found no fully satisfying evidence on that question.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p182#2/r1.anchor: ويفهم من كلامهم أن هذا الخلق لم يقع هكذا إلا بين هذين الزوجين دون سائر أزواج الحيوانات ولم أظفر في ذلك بما يشفى الغليل

ALUSI-FULL:v4p182#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p182#2/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v4p182#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that Iblis's wife was created from his left rear rib; al-Ḍaḥḥāk explains the relevant term as the shortest ribs of the side.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p182#2/r2.anchor: نعم أخرج عبد بن حميد وإبن المنذر عن إبن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنهما أن زوج إبليس عليهما اللعنة خلقت من خلفه الأيسر

ALUSI-FULL:v4p182#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p182#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p182#2/r3.claim: The verse mentions the addressees' creation first because that reminder more directly prompts obedience; fronting “from it” emphasizes Adam as Eve's origin and creates suspense, while “spouse” prepares for reproduction.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p182#2/r3.anchor: وإنما أخر بيان خلق الزوج عن بيان خلق المخاطبين لما أن تذكير خلقهم أدخل في تحقيق ما هو المقصود

ALUSI-FULL:v4p182#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p182#2/r4.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v4p182#2/r4.claim: Some critical scholars allow the clause about the spouse to coordinate with an implied clause: God first created the single soul, then created its spouse; the implied clause may stand independently or describe that soul.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p182#2/r4.anchor: وذهب بعض المحققين إلى جواز عطف هذه الجملة على مقدر ينبيء عنه السوق لأن تفريع الفروع من أصل واحد يستدعي إنشاء ذلك الأصل

ALUSI-FULL:v4p182#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p182#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p182#2/r5.claim: Some require the implied clause if the address is universal, to avoid redundancy and the false suggestion that men and women alone were created from both sources; the author considers the objection remote and the added clause unnecessary.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p182#2/r5.anchor: وأوجب بعضهم هذا التقدير على تقدير جعل الخطاب فيما تقدم عاما في الجنس

ALUSI-FULL:v4p182#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p182#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p182#2/r6.claim: “He spread from both” means He propagated and dispersed many men and women from the single soul and its spouse through reproduction.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p182#2/r6.anchor: وبث منهما ( أي نشر وفرق من تلك النفس وزوجها على وجه التناسل والتوالد

ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r1.claim: The indefinite “men” and “women” conveys abundance, and “many” modifies “men,” reinforcing that abundance; the author rejects as strained taking it as an adjective for an omitted verbal noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r1.anchor: والتلوين في ( رجالا ونساءا ) للتكثير و ( كثيرا ) نعت ل ( رجالا ) مؤكد لما أفاده التنكير والإفراد

ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r2.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ analyzes “many” as an adjective for an omitted verbal noun, meaning “a great propagation”; the author calls the alternative adjective analysis contrived.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r2.anchor: ونقل أبو البقاء أنه نعت المصدر محذوف أي بثا ( كثيرا )

ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r3.claim: “Men and women” means males and females of any age, not only adults; using the gendered terms may intensify the sense of great numbers by portraying each propagated individual as a source of another.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r3.anchor: وليس المراد بالرجال والنساء البالغين والبالغات بل الذكور والإناث مطلقا تجوزا

ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r4.speaker: الخطيب
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r4.claim: Al-Khaṭīb explains why abundance is stated only for men: wisdom requires women to be more numerous, since a man may have more than one wife whereas a woman cannot have multiple husbands.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r4.anchor: إذ للرجل أن يزيد في عصمته على واحدة بخلاف المرأة قاله الخطيب

ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r5.claim: Some infer from the verse that every originated thing must arise from prior matter and that creation from absolute nonbeing is impossible; the author rejects this generalization because the verse only identifies the origins of humanity and its mate.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r5.anchor: واحتج بعضهم بالآية على أن الحادث لا يحدث إلا عن مادة سابقة وأن خلق الشيء عن العدم المحض والنفي الصرف محال

ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r6.claim: A case in which matter is used for a particular wise purpose does not establish that all creation requires matter; this verse says only that humans and their mate were created from the stated origins.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r6.anchor: وأجيب بأنه لا يلزم من إحداث شيء في صورة واحدة من المادة لحكمة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r7.claim: A reading with “creating” and “spreading” treats the words as coordinated clauses with an omitted subject, since they continue the relative clause; the author contrasts this with coordination of a participle after a finite verb.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r7.anchor: وقريءوخالق وباثعلى حذف المبتدأ لأنه صلة لعطفه

ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r8.claim: “Fear God” repeats and confirms the opening command. The author takes both addresses as directed to the Prophet's original audience; alternatives make both addresses specific to Arabs or the second alone specific to them, but he finds that scope-shift incoherent.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r8.anchor: ( وأتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به ( تكرير للأمر الأول وتأكيد له والمخاطب من بعث إليهم صلى الله عليه وسلم أيضا كما مر

ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to identify the addressees in both commands as Arabs because they habitually invoked one another by God.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r9.anchor: وقيل : المخاطب هنا وهناك هم العرب كما روى عن إبن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r10.claim: Using the majestic name “Allah” instead of a pronoun moves from the attribute of lordship to all attributes of perfection, reinforcing the command to fear Him as creator and deserving of every perfection.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183/r10.anchor: ووضع الأسم الجليل موضع الضمير للإشارة إلى جميع صفات الكمال ترقيا بعد صفة الربوبية

ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r1.claim: Calling on one another by God in supplication and entreaty itself calls for fearing violation of His commands and prohibitions.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r1.anchor: فإن قول القائل لصاحبه : أسألك بالله وأنشدك الله تعالى على سبيل الإستعطاف يقتضي الإتقاء من مخالفة أوامره ونواهيه

ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r2.claim: The common reading “you ask one another” can be reciprocal; the form can also carry the meaning “you ask,” since a form with multiple agents may function like the basic verb.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r2.anchor: و ( تساءلون ) إما بمعنى يسأل بعضكم بعضا فالمفاعلة على ظاهرها

ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r3.claim: The standard form originally has two successive tāʾs, one omitted for ease; Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, and the other Kūfan readers assimilate the first tāʾ into the nearby sīn.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r3.anchor: وأصله على القراءة المشهورة تتساءلونبتاءين فحذفت إحداهما للثقل

ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r4.claim: One accusative analysis coordinates “kinship” with the grammatical position of “by Him”; it is supported by the reading “by Him and by kinship,” and reports that people paired kinship with God in pleas, as Mujāhid relates.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r4.anchor: والأرحام بالنصب وهو معطوف إما على محل الجار والمجرور إن كان المحل لهما

ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r5.claim: Mujāhid reports that people used to couple kinship with God when asking and adjuring one another, saying they asked by God and by the womb/kinship.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r5.anchor: كما أخرج ذلك غير واحد عن مجاهد وهو إختيار الفارسي وعلي بن عيسى

ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r6.claim: Another accusative analysis coordinates “kinship” with the name Allah: fear God and maintain kinship; this is reported from Mujāhid, al-Ḍaḥḥāk from Ibn ʿAbbās, and ʿIkrima, and preferred by al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r6.anchor: وإما معطوف على الأسم الجليل أي أتقوا الله تعالى والأرحام وصلوها ولا تقطعوها

ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r7.speaker: الواحدي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r7.claim: Al-Wāḥidī allows the accusative as an exhortation: hold fast to kinship and maintain it.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r7.anchor: وجوز الواحدي النصب على الإغراء أي والزموا الأرحام وصلوها

ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r8.speaker: حمزة
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r8.claim: Ḥamza reads “kinship” in the genitive, conventionally parsed as coordinated with the attached genitive pronoun; most grammarians weaken that construction because the pronoun is tightly bound to its preposition.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p183#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ حمزة بالجر وخرجت في المشهور على العطف على الضمير المجرور وضعف ذلك أكثر النحويين

ALUSI-FULL:v4p184/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p184/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p184/r1.claim: Ḥamza received this reading through recognized Qurʾān transmitters, was a trusted and learned imam, and was among the seven whose readings leading authorities judged mutawātir; other early authorities also read it, so attacking him is gravely improper.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p184/r1.anchor: وقد قال الإمام أبو حنيفة والثوري ويحيى بن آدم في حقه غلب حمزة الناس على القراءة والفرائض

ALUSI-FULL:v4p184/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p184/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p184/r2.claim: The author reports that Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, Qatāda, Mujāhid, and others also read the genitive form.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p184/r2.anchor: بل قرأ به جماعة من غير السبعة كإبن مسعود وإبن عباس وإبراهيم النخعي والحسن البصري وقتادة ومجاهد وغيرهم

ALUSI-FULL:v4p184/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p184/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p184/r3.claim: The objection that a genitive attachment cannot follow a preposition-bound pronoun merely reflects Basran grammar; the author rejects binding readers to that school and cites Abū Ḥayyān, the Kūfans, and Ibn Mālik for its grammatical legitimacy in Arabic prose and verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p184/r3.anchor: وماذكر من إمتناع العطف على الضمير المجرور هو مذهب البصريين ولسنا متعبدين بإتباعهم

ALUSI-FULL:v4p184/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p184/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p184/r4.claim: Mentioning kinship does aid the command to fear God: if taqwā means care for human rights, maintaining family ties is among them; if it is general, kinship is included within it.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p184/r4.anchor: لأن التقوى إن أريد بها تقوى خاصة وهي التي في حقوق العباد التي من جملتها صلة الرحم فالتساؤل بالأرحام مما يقتضيه بلا ريب

ALUSI-FULL:v4p184/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p184/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v4p184/r5.claim: Some answer the objection based on the prohibition of swearing by other than God by limiting that prohibition to oaths made with a belief that fulfillment is obligatory; they cite the report “He prospers, by his father, if truthful.”
ALUSI-FULL:v4p184/r5.anchor: فقد قيل في جوابها : لا نسلم أن الحلف بغير الله تعالى مطلقا منهى عنه بل المنهي عنه ما كان مع إعتقاد وجوب البر

ALUSI-FULL:v4p184/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p184/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p184/r6.claim: Some distinguish a plea asking another “by kinship” as mere entreaty from swearing “by kinship, I will do it”; they say the former is not covered by the prohibition, and reject the claim that the verse merely reports a pre-Islamic practice.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p184/r6.anchor: وقد ذكر بعضهم أن قول الشخص لآخر : أسألك بالرحم أن تفعل كذا ليس الغرض منه سوى الإستعطاف

ALUSI-FULL:v4p184/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p184/r7.speaker: إبن جني
ALUSI-FULL:v4p184/r7.claim: Ibn Jinnī offers a further grammatical analysis of Ḥamza's reading based on an omitted element that context makes understood; the next passage develops the proposal.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p184/r7.anchor: وقد خرج إبن جني هذه القراءة على تخريج آخر فقال في الخصائص : باب في أن المحذوف إذا دلت الدلالة عليه كان في حكم الملفوظ به

ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r1.claim: Following Ibn Jinnī's principle that a contextually evident omission counts as spoken, the author illustrates an omitted “rubb” in a line about a house trace and omitted “bi-khayr” in a greeting; on this analysis Ḥamza's reading omits a preposition already mentioned.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r1.anchor: أي رب رسم دار وكان رؤبو

ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also uses omission of the previously mentioned preposition to explain this reading; the author reports al-Kashf's judgment that this is closer for many Basrans because preposition omission is established in comparable expressions.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r2.anchor: وفي شرح المفصل أن الباء في هذه القراءة محذوفة لتقدم ذكرها وقد مشى على ذلك أيضا الزمخشري في أحاجيه

ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r3.claim: Another analysis makes the conjunction an oath, as in “Fear God, for by God He watches over me”; omitting the explanatory fāʾ leaves the stronger independent resumption, a good analysis according to the author.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r3.anchor: ونقل عن بعضهم أن الواو للقسم على نحوأتق الله تعالى فوالله إنه مطلع عليكوترك الفاء

ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r4.speaker: إبن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd reads “kinship” in the nominative as a subject with an omitted predicate: kinship is likewise to be guarded against severance, or is likewise invoked in mutual requests.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r4.anchor: وقرأ إبن زيد ( والأرحام ) بالرفع على أنه مبتدأ محذوف الخبر أي ( والأرحام ) كذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya supplies “worthy of being maintained” as the omitted predicate, while Ibn Jinnī says “among what you must maintain and protect”; the author finds the clause parenthetical on this reading and the coordination somewhat obscure.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r5.anchor: وقدره إبن عطية أهل لأن توصلو

ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r6.speaker: النبي ﷺ
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r6.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that the Prophet said the womb sought refuge from severance after creation, and God promised to join whoever maintains kinship and sever whoever cuts it; al-Bukhārī and Muslim transmit it.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم : إن الله تعالى خلق الخلق حتى إذا فرغ منهم قامت الرحم

ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r7.speaker: البزار
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r7.claim: Al-Bazzār transmits with a good chain a report portraying kinship as clinging to the Throne and praying for connection or severance; God answers that He is the Merciful and reciprocates, since He derived kinship from His name.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r7.anchor: وأخرج البزار بإسناد حسن الرحم حجنة متمسكة بالعرش تكلم بلسان زلق اللهم صل من وصلني

ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r8.speaker: أحمد
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r8.claim: A report that Aḥmad transmits with a sound chain calls unjust aggression a form of usury, describes kinship as a branch of the All-Merciful, and says God bars Paradise to whoever severs it.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r8.anchor: وأخرج الإمام أحمد بإسناد صحيح إن من أربى الربا الإستطالة بغير حق وإن هذه الرحم شجنة من الرحمن

ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r9.claim: Kinship covers relatives connected by lineage, however distant, and can refer particularly to maternal relatives; restricting the duty of maintaining it to relatives through the mother's womb is unacceptable because commands to treat relatives well are general.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r9.anchor: والمراد بالرحم الأقارب ويقع على كل من يجمع بينك وبينه نسب وإن بعد

ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r10.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r10.claim: Mujāhid explains “watchful over you” as “preserving you”; al-Rāghib derives the expression from watching in the sense of guarding.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r10.anchor: إن الله كان عليكم رقيبا 1 أي حفيظا قاله مجاهد

ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r11.speaker: إبن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r11.claim: The word may also mean one who observes or knows: Ibn Zayd interprets it as “knowing,” by analogy with a high lookout from which a place is observed; grammatically it is an active participle.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r11.anchor: ومن هنا فسره إبن زيد بالعالم وعلى كل فهو فعيل بمعنى فاعل

ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r12.claim: The closing clause explains why the command and compliance are obligatory; naming God explicitly reinforces that rationale, and fronting the prepositional phrase maintains the verse's rhyme.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p185/r12.anchor: والجملة في موضع التعليل للأمر ووجوب الإمتثال وإظهار الأسم الجليل لتأكيده وتقديم الجار لرعاية الفواصل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p158#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p158#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p158#2/r1.claim: The one soul from which humanity was created is Adam, and his spouse is Eve.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p158#2/r1.anchor: يعني: آدم عليه السلام، {وخلق منها زوجها} يعني: حواء،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p158#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p158#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p158#2/r2.claim: The verb describing their descendants means that God spread and brought them forth.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p158#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p158#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p158#2/r3.claim: The phrase تساءلون means that people ask one another by God; Kufans lighten the sīn by deleting one of the two tāʾs, as in 5:2.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p158#2/r3.anchor: الذي تساءلون به} أي: تتساءلون به، وقرأ أهل الكوفة بتخفيف السين على حذف إحدى التاءين،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p158#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p158#2/r4.speaker: قراءة العامة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p158#2/r4.claim: The general reading puts al-arḥām in the accusative, commanding care for kinship ties so they are not severed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p158#2/r4.anchor: ، {والأرحام} قراءة العامة بالنصب، أي: واتقوا الأرحام أن تقطعوها،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p158#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p158#2/r5.speaker: حمزة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p158#2/r5.claim: Hamza reads al-arḥām in the genitive, coordinating it with the pronoun in the sense of swearing by God and kinship.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p158#2/r5.anchor: ، وقرأ حمزة بالخفض، أي: به وبالأرحام كما يقال: سألتك بالله والأرحام،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p158#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p158#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p158#2/r6.claim: The accusative reading is more eloquent because Arabs rarely coordinate an overt noun with a pronoun without repeating the preposition, though it is allowed rarely.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p158#2/r6.anchor: والقراءة الأولى أفصح لأن العرب لا تكاد تنسق بظاهر على مكنى، إلا أن تعيد الخافض

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p158#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p158#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p158#2/r7.claim: Raqīb means a guardian or watcher.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p158#2/r7.anchor: ، {إن الله كان عليكم رقيبا} أي: حافظا.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r1.claim: “People” is an address encompassing all the children of Adam.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r2.claim: The one soul from which humanity was created is Adam.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r3.claim: His spouse was created from him: Eve was made from one of Adam’s ribs.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r3.anchor: وخلق منه أمكم حواء من ضلع من أضلاعه

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r4.claim: Alternatively, an omitted clause means “from one soul He created, and from it He created its spouse,” reaffirming humanity’s single origin.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r4.anchor: أو محذوف تقديره من نفس واحدة خلقها وخلق منها زوجها

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r5.claim: The spreading of many men and women explains how they descend from the original pair; the verse mentions many men without repeating “many” for women because wisdom requires women to be more numerous.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r5.anchor: ونشر من تلك النفس والزوج المخلوقة منها بنين وبنات كثيرة

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r6.claim: The masculine plural “many” follows the collective construction.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r7.claim: The origin story grounds the command to fear God in His overwhelming power and abundant blessing, which call for fear and obedience.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r7.anchor: لما فيها من الدلالة على القدرة القاهرة التي من حقها أن تخشى

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r8.claim: Alternatively, the command prepares people for piety in the rights of household members and fellow human beings discussed in the following verses.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r8.anchor: تمهيد الأمر بالتقوى فيما يتصل بحقوق أهل منزله وبني جنسه

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r9.claim: A reading has khāliqun and bāththun with an omitted subject, estimated as “and He is creator and spreader.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r9.anchor: وقرىء «وخالق» «وباث» على حذف مبتدأ تقديره وهو خالق وباث.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r10.claim: Tasaʾalūn derives from tata-sāʾalūn, with the second tāʾ assimilated into the sīn.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r10.anchor: وأصله تتساءلون فأدغمت التاء الثانية في السين

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r11.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r11.claim: They omit one of the two tāʾs in the verb.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r12.claim: Al-arḥām can be accusative by coordination with the understood object of the preposition, or with God as the object of “fear”: fear God and maintain kinship.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r12.anchor: والأرحام } بالنصب عطف على محل الجار والمجرور

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r13.claim: The author interprets the second accusative construction as commanding people to maintain kinship and not sever it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r13.anchor: أي اتقوا الله واتقوا الأرحام فصلوها ولا تقطعوها

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r14.speaker: حمزة
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r14.claim: Hamza reads al-arḥām in the genitive, coordinated with the pronoun after the preposition; the construction is weak because it is like a part of a word.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r14.anchor: وقرأ حمزة بالجر عطفا على الضمير المجرور وهو ضعيف

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r15.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r15.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r15.claim: A nominative reading treats al-arḥām as a subject with an omitted predicate: it too is something to be guarded or invoked by.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r15.anchor: وقرىء بالرفع على أنه مبتدأ محذوف الخبر تقديره

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r16.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r16.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r16.claim: By pairing kinship with His honored name, God indicates that maintaining family ties is owed for His sake.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r16.anchor: إذ قرن الأرحام باسمه الكريم على أن صلتها بمكان منه

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r17.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r17.speaker: النبي
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r17.claim: A Prophetic report depicts kinship as suspended from the Throne, asking God to join whoever maintains it and sever whoever cuts it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1/r17.anchor: الرحم معلقة بالعرش تقول ألا من وصلني وصله الله

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1#2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1#2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:1#2/r1.claim: God is a guardian over people, preserving and observing them.

SULAMI:v1p138/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p138/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p138/r1.claim: One view interprets the address to people as calling the children of forgetfulness and ignorance.
SULAMI:v1p138/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : ﴿ يا أيها الناس ﴾ يا بني النسيان والجهل .

SULAMI:v1p138/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p138/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p138/r2.claim: Al-Wasiti addresses people as children of lifespans, deeds, and hopes, urging them not to disappear into the past or be absent from the present.
SULAMI:v1p138/r2.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله : يا بني الأعمار والأعمال والآمال ، لا تذهبون فيما سبق ولا تغيبون عما أنتم فيه .

SULAMI:v1p138/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p138/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p138/r3.claim: Ibn Ata interprets the address as calling people to be among those intimate with God and estranged from everything besides Him.
SULAMI:v1p138/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء رحمه الله : ﴿ يا أيها الناس ﴾ كونوا مع الناس الذين آنسوا بالله واستوحشوا ممن سواه .

SULAMI:v1p138/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p138/r4.speaker: جعفر الصادق
SULAMI:v1p138/r4.claim: Jaafar al-Sadiq calls people to be among the truly human and never neglect God; those singled out by Him rise above seeking stations, with God as their end and divine knowledge and inspiration elevating their aspiration.
SULAMI:v1p138/r4.anchor: وقال جعفر الصادق رحمه الله : ﴿ يا أيها الناس ﴾ كونوا من الناس الذين هم الناس ، ولا تغفلوا عن الله فمن عرف أنه من الناس الذين خص خلقه ما خص به

SULAMI:v1p138/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p138/r5.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p138/r5.claim: One view distinguishes addresses: people are the general audience, servants the elect, and Prophet or Messenger the elect of the elect.
SULAMI:v1p138/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم : ﴿ يا أيها الناس ﴾ خطاب العام ، و ' يا عبادي ' خطاب الخاص ، وخطاب خاص الخاص ﴿ يا أيها النبي ﴾

SULAMI:v1p138#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r1.claim: The Prophet is reported to have advised a man who asked for counsel to fear God, saying that this gathers all good.
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r1.anchor: روى الليث عن مجاهد عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه أن رجلا جاء إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال له : أوصني قال : ' اتق الله فإنه جماع كل خير ' .

SULAMI:v1p138#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r2.claim: One view says the root of piety is God's describing and meeting a person in the manner fitting that person.
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم : أصل التقوى أنه وصفك وقابلك بما يليق بك .

SULAMI:v1p138#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r3.speaker: النصر آباذي
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r3.claim: Al-Nasrabadhi defines piety as attaining God and cites the verse that God receives piety rather than sacrificial flesh or blood.
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r3.anchor: قال سمعت النصر آباذي رحمه الله يقول : التقوى نيل الحق ، قال الله عز وجل : ﴿ لن ينال الله لحومها ولا دماؤها ولكن يناله التقوى منكم ﴾

SULAMI:v1p138#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r4.claim: One view defines piety as abandoning every act of opposition to God.
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r4.anchor: قال بعضهم : التقوى ترك المخالفات أجمع .

SULAMI:v1p138#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r5.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r5.claim: Sahl says piety requires leaving every sin and anything that brings a fault, including forbidden acts and indecencies.
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r5.anchor: وقال سهل رحمه الله : من أراد التقوى فليترك الذنوب كلها وكل شيء يقع فيه خلل فيدخل عليه التقوى

SULAMI:v1p138#2/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r6.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r6.claim: One view identifies piety with following the Prophet.
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r6.anchor: وقال بعضهم رحمه الله : التقوى الاقتداء بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم .

SULAMI:v1p138#2/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r7.claim: One view says piety in commands is avoiding delay, in prohibitions resisting desire, in exhortation keeping noble manners, in encouragement concealing one's inner state, and in threats not persisting in ignorance.
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم : التقوى في الأمر ترك التسويف والتقوى في النهى ترك الفكرة والقيام عليه . والتقوى أداب مكارم الأخلاق

SULAMI:v1p138#2/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r8.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r8.claim: One view defines piety from God as avoiding everything besides God.
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم رحمه الله : التقوى من الله الاجتناب من كل شيء سوى الله .

SULAMI:v1p138#2/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r9.speaker: الجريري
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r9.claim: Al-Jurayri says without piety and vigilance in one's relation to God, one cannot attain unveiling and direct vision.
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r9.anchor: وقال الجريري رحمه الله : من لم يحكم فيما بينه وبين الله تعالى بالتقوى والمراقبة لا يصل إلى الكشف والمشاهدة .

SULAMI:v1p138#2/r10.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r10.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r10.claim: Al-Wasiti gives four levels of piety: avoiding shirk for commoners, sins for the elect, reliance on deeds for saintly elect, and turning from God toward Him for prophets.
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r10.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله : التقوى على أربعة أوجه : للعامة تقوى الشرك ، وللخاص تقوى المعاصي ، وللخاص من الأولياء تقوى التوسل بالأفعال

SULAMI:v1p138#2/r11.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r11.speaker: أبو يزيد
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r11.claim: Abu Yazid says complete piety means speaking and intending for God alone, without turning back to another.
SULAMI:v1p138#2/r11.anchor: وقال أبو يزيد رحمه الله : كل التقوى من إذا قال لله ولم يقل لغيره ، وإذا نوى نوى لله ولم يتب لغيره

SULAMI:v1p139/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p139/r1.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p139/r1.claim: One view says only God's active power and effective will could bring the first soul into existence.
SULAMI:v1p139/r1.anchor: قيل : من أوجد النفس الأولى إلا القدرة الجارية والمشيئة النافذة .

SULAMI:v1p139/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p139/r2.speaker: عمرو بن عثمان
SULAMI:v1p139/r2.claim: Amr ibn Uthman describes the universe as a harmonious, gapless order whose diverse forms are joined by divine governance and interests; God displayed His power in creating Adam and spreading his descendants under His will.
SULAMI:v1p139/r2.anchor: وقال عمرو بن عثمان : إن الله عز وجل خلق العالم فهيأه باتساقه نظما وذكرا من أطرافه وأكنافه وأوله وآخره وبدؤه ومنتهاه

SULAMI:v1p139/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p139/r3.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p139/r3.claim: Al-Wasiti says God created people with prior knowledge, arranged their composition, clothed them in signs of His attributes, and brought forth breaths He had kept stored; what He manifests is what He conceals.
SULAMI:v1p139/r3.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله في قوله تعالى : ﴿ خلقكم من نفس واحدة ﴾ قال : خلقهم بعلم سابق ودبرهم بالتركيب وألبسهم شواهد النعت

SULAMI:v1p141/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p141/r1.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p141/r1.claim: One view says God watches one's secret; a person should not be found busy with anything besides Him, lest He cut the person off and erase him.
SULAMI:v1p141/r1.anchor: قيل : هو المراقب بسرك والناظر إليك ، فاجتهد أن لا ينظر إليك فيراك مشتغلا بغيره فيقطعك ويمحقك .

SULAMI:v1p141/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p141/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p141/r2.claim: Ibn Ata says God knows what one conceals in the heart and in one's thoughts, so one should remain watchful before the Watcher.
SULAMI:v1p141/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء رحمه الله : في قوله تعالى : ﴿ إن الله كان عليكم رقيبا ﴾ قال : عالما بما تغمره في سرك وما تخفيه من خواطرك

BIQAI-FULL:v2p204/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p204/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p204/r1.claim: The surah is named Women because kinship ties, commonly mediated by women, are central to social cohesion; observing women's rights secures chastity and justice, whose core is monotheism.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p204/r1.anchor: ولأن بالاتقاء فيهم تتحقق العفة والعدل الذي لبابه التوحيد

BIQAI-FULL:v2p204/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p204/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p204/r2.claim: In the basmala, Allah gathers scattered matters through gracious pairing, the All-Merciful makes wombs a general mercy, and the Especially Merciful grants chosen people the complete blessing of religious connection.
