BIQAI-FULL:v2p204/r2.anchor: { بسم الله } الجامع لشتات الأمور بإحسان التزاوج في لطائف المقدور { الرحمن } الذي جعل الأرحام رحمة عامة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p204/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p204/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p204/r3.claim: After the Book and monotheism were established as the path and foundation, this surah calls people to assemble through connection, mutual care, and mercy.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p204/r3.anchor: فجاءت هذه السورة داعية إلى الاجتماع والتواصل والتعاطف والتراحيم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p204/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p204/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p204/r4.claim: The surah opens with a universal address to all people, following Aal Imran's closing address to believers.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p204/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p204/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p204/r5.claim: Ethics identifies four chief virtues: knowledge, courage, justice, and chastity; Aal Imran especially called to the first two.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p204/r5.anchor: لما كانت أمهات الفضائل - كما تبين في علم الأخلاق - أربعا : العلم والشجاعة والعدل والعفة ,

BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r1.claim: The Battle of Uhud left orphans whose heirs died for God's sake, while pre-Islamic custom denied such orphans inheritance; this surah addresses justice and chastity alongside knowledge and courage.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r1.anchor: وكانت قصة أحد قد أسفرت عن أيتام استشهد موروثهم في حب الله ,

BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r2.claim: The remaining virtues, justice and chastity, are reinforced with knowledge and courage to produce benevolent connection and social repair in obedience to God.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r2.anchor: من الفضيلتين الباقيتين , وهما العفة والعدل مع تأكيد الخصلتين الأخريين حسبما تدعو إليه المناسبة ,

BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r3.claim: The surah's chief purpose is gathering people around religion by following the clear Book.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r3.anchor: فمقصودها الأعظم الاجتماع على الدين بالاقتداء بالكتاب المبين

BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r4.claim: The surah's broad opening deliberately follows Aal Imran's specific closing exhortation to believers to persevere.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r4.anchor: وما أحسن ابتداءها بعموم : { ياأيها الناس } بعد اختتام تلك بخصوص ( ياأيها الذين آمنوا اصبروا وصابروا الآية .

BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r5.claim: The many duties include caring for the weak in matters people were habituated to neglect, making them difficult; the surah's opening and close stress this concern.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r5.anchor: على أنواع كثيرة من التكاليف , منها التعطف على الضعاف بأمور كانوا قد مرنوا على خلافها , فكانت في غاية المشقة على النفوس ,

BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r6.claim: Calling God their Lord means their Master and benefactor who nurtured them after bringing them into existence; fearing Him creates a shield from displeasure and hardship.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r6.anchor: { اتقوا ربكم } أي سيدكم ومولاكم المحسن إليكم بالتربية بعد الإيجاد , بأن تجعلوا بينكم وبين سخطه وقاية ,

BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r7.claim: The single soul is Adam; recalling this origin displays God's power, deters disobedience, encourages obedience, and prepares for the inheritance laws.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r7.anchor: أنه { خلقكم من نفس واحدة } هي أبوكم آدم عليه الصلاة والسلام مذكرا بعظيم قدرته ترهيبا للعاصي وترغيبا للطائع توطئة للأمر بالإرث ,

BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r8.claim: The command to fear God opens both this surah, fourth in the first half, and al-Hajj, fourth in the second; this surah points to the beginning of creation and al-Hajj vividly depicts the return.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r8.anchor: وقد جعل سبحانه الأمر بالتقوى مطلعا لسورتين : هذه وهي رابعة النصف الأول , والحج وهي رابعة النصف الثاني ,

BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r9.claim: The creation and return disclose wisdom: the universe was made so God's beautiful names and exalted attributes could appear as fully as humans can apprehend.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r9.anchor: ما خلق الوجود إلا لأجله , لتظهر الأسماء الحسنى والصفات العلى أتم ظهور يمكن البشر الاطلاع عليه ,

BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r10.claim: The prior debate about Jesus leads into this verse: Adam, Eve, Jesus, and ordinary humans represent the four rational modes of human origin, from neither parent, both, father alone, or mother alone.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r10.anchor: وكانت حقيقة حاله أنه ذكر يولد من أنثى فقط بلا وساطة ذكر ؛

BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r11.claim: The phrase about creating the spouse links her origin to Adam's and helps complete the fourfold account of human creation.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p205/r11.anchor: وخلق منها زوجها } أي مثله في ذلك أيضا كمثل كل من أبيه وأمه : آدم فإنها أنثى تولدت من ذكر بلا واسطة أنثى ,

BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r1.claim: The creation wording is more fitting than making because it stresses originating causes and arranging effects, a stronger warning than merely arranging effects upon existing causes.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r1.anchor: فكان بالخلق الذي هو أعظم في إظهار الاقتداء - لأنه اختراع الأسباب وترتيب المسببات عليها - أحق من الجعل الذي هو ترتيب المسببات

BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r2.claim: Because the verse speaks of creation, it calls God Lord, a title that conveys nurturing.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r2.anchor: ولما ذكر تعالى الإنشاء عبر بلفظ الرب الذي هو من التربية

BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r3.claim: The many men and women were dispersed through procreation from the single soul; the indefinite wording also signals that God brought them from nonexistence.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r3.anchor: { وبث منهما } أي فرق ونشر من التوالد , ولما كان المبثوث قبل ذلك عدما

BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r4.claim: Although women may be more numerous, the verse names men first to indicate their degree, greater visible strength, and public presence, while women are concealed.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r4.anchor: ووصف الرجال دونهن مع أنهن أكثر منهم إشارة إلى أن لهم عليهن درجة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r5.claim: The second command to fear God invokes His intrinsic perfection as well as the particular care and nurture mentioned first, and warns against severing kinship ties.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r5.anchor: { واتقوا الله } أي عموما لما له من إحاطة الأوصاف كما اتقيتموه خصوصا لما له إليكم من الإحسان والتربية ,

BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r6.claim: People ask one another by God's name because invoking that sacred name seeks mercy, kindness, and compassion.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r6.anchor: { الذين تساءلون } أي يسأل بعضكم بعضا { به } فإنه لا يسأل باسمه الشريف المقدس إلا الرحمة والبر والعطف ,

BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r7.claim: The phrase about wombs commands people to fear severing kinship, as in the appeal, I adjure you by God and kinship.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r7.anchor: { والأرحام } أي واتقوا قطيعة الأرحام التي تساءلون بها , فإنكم تقولون : ناشدتك بالله والرحم !

BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r8.claim: God's watchfulness over hidden and public conduct threatens those who act as though He does not see them; the preposition ala adds force to the threat.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r8.anchor: { إن الله } أي المحيط علما وقدرة { كان عليكم } وفي أداة الاستعلاء ضرب من التهديد { رقيبا * }

BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r9.claim: Hamza reads al-arham in the genitive as an oath, honoring kinship and emphasizing its rights; either grammatical reading shows its high standing.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r9.anchor: وخفض حمزة ( الأرحام ) المقسم بها تعظيما لها وتأكيدا للتنبيه على أنهم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r10.claim: Muslims agree that maintaining kinship is obligatory; the child has the strongest claim, and the first duty is choosing a lawful place for conception.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r10.anchor: واتفق المسلمون على أن صلى الرحم واجبة , وأحقهم بالصلة الولد , وأول صلته أن يختار له الموضع الحلال .

BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r11.claim: The conjunction reading also accords with the command that God and parents be worshipped and treated well.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p206/r11.anchor: كما شرحته آية { وقضى ربك أن لا تعبدوا إلا إياه } [ الإسراء : 23 ]

BIQAI-FULL:v2p382/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p382/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p382/r7.claim: The surah's opening treats humanity as one community; its end likewise gives women and men inheritance through kinship, though their shares differ, and warns that rejecting any divine ruling brings punishment without a helper.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p382/r7.anchor: لأن أولها مشير إلى أن الناس كلهم كشيء واحد

BIQAI-FULL:v2p382/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p382/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p382/r8.claim: The end's comprehensive knowledge corresponds to the opening's complete power, because perfect knowledge entails encompassing power.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p382/r8.anchor: وما أشد مناسبة ختامها بإحاطة العلم لما دل عليه أولها من تمام القدرة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p382/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p382/r9.speaker: الإمام
BIQAI-FULL:v2p382/r9.claim: The two attributes of knowledge and power establish lordship, divinity, majesty, and might, requiring servants to obey commands and prohibitions and submit to all duties.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p382/r9.anchor: وهذان الوصفان هما اللذان بهما ثبتت الربوية والإلهية والجلال والعزة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p382/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p382/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p382/r10.claim: He closes by turning to the phrase that ends the surah first verse, as a further link between its ending and opening.

DURR-FULL:v2p422/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Surat al-Nisa was revealed in Medina.
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: نزلت سورة النساء بالمدينة

DURR-FULL:v2p422/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r2.claim: Qatada likewise says Surat al-Nisa was revealed in Medina.
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r2.anchor: عن قتادة قال: نزل بالمدينة النساء

DURR-FULL:v2p422/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r3.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r3.claim: Aisha says neither Surat al-Baqara nor Surat al-Nisa was revealed until she was with the Prophet.
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r3.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: ما نزلت سورة البقرة والنساء إلا وأنا عنده

DURR-FULL:v2p422/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r4.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r4.claim: Aisha reports the Prophet said that whoever takes the seven long suras is a learned scholar.
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r4.anchor: عن عائشة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال من أخذ السبع فهو حبر

DURR-FULL:v2p422/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r5.speaker: واثلة بن الأسقع
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r5.claim: Wathila reports the Prophet saying that the seven long suras were given in place of the Torah, the hundred-verse suras are al-mi'un, and suras below one hundred but above al-mufassal are al-mathani.
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r5.anchor: عن واثلة بن الأسقع قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أعطيت مكان التوراة السبع الطول والمئين كل سورة بلغت مائة فصاعدا

DURR-FULL:v2p422/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r6.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r6.claim: Anas reports that after a painful night the Prophet said he was well by God's grace and had recited the seven long suras.
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r6.anchor: عن أنس قال: وجد رسول الله ذات ليلة شيئا فلما أصبح قيل: يا رسول الله إن أثر الوجع عليك لبين

DURR-FULL:v2p422/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r7.speaker: حذيفة
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r7.claim: Hudhayfa says that during a night prayer with the Prophet, he recited the seven long suras across seven rak'as.
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r7.anchor: عن حذيفة قال: قمت مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة فقرأ السبع الطوال في سبع ركعات

DURR-FULL:v2p422/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r8.speaker: بعض أهل النبي
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r8.claim: A member of the Prophet's household reports that he performed his nighttime ablution, washed his hands three times, and recited all seven long suras in one rak'a.
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r8.anchor: عن بعض أهل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه بات معه فقام النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من الليل فقضى حاجته ثم جاء القربة

DURR-FULL:v2p422/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas invites people to ask him about Surat al-Nisa because he had read the Quran while young.
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r9.anchor: عن أبي مليكة سمع ابن عباس يقول: سلوني عن سورة النساء فإني قرأت القرآن وأنا صغير

DURR-FULL:v2p422/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says that whoever recites Surat al-Nisa and knows which heirs are excluded from inheritance and which are not understands the laws of inheritance.
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: من قرأ سورة النساء فعلم ما يحجب مما لا يحجب علم الفرائض

DURR-FULL:v2p422/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the one soul as Adam and its mate as Eve, created from a short rib of Adam.
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {خلقكم من نفس واحدة} قال: من آدم {وخلق منها زوجها} قال: خلق حواء من قصيراء أضلاعه

DURR-FULL:v2p422/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r12.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r12.claim: Mujahid likewise identifies the one soul as Adam and his mate as Eve, created from Adam's short rib while he slept.
DURR-FULL:v2p422/r12.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {خلقكم من نفس واحدة} قال: آدم {وخلق منها زوجها} قال: حواء من قصيراء آدم وهو نائم

DURR-FULL:v2p423/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r1.claim: The opening lexical note says that امرأة means “woman” in Nabataean.
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r1.anchor: بالنبطية امرأة وأخرج عبد بن حميد

DURR-FULL:v2p423/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r2.speaker: ابن عمرو
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r2.claim: Ibn Amr reports that Eve was created from Adam’s left back and Satan’s wife from his left back.
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمرو قال خلقت حواء من خلف آدم الأيسر وخلقت امرأة إبليس من خلفه الأيسر

DURR-FULL:v2p423/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r3.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak says Eve was created from Adam, from a rib at the back, the lowest of the ribs.
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك {وخلق منها زوجها} قال: خلق حواء من آدم من ضلع الخلف وهو أسفل الأضلاع

DURR-FULL:v2p423/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says woman was created from man and made desirous of men, so men should restrain their wives; man was created from earth and desires it.
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: خلقت المرأة من الرجل فجعلت نهمتها في الرجال فاحبسوا نساءكم وخلق الرجل من الأرض

DURR-FULL:v2p423/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Adam had forty children: twenty sons and twenty daughters.
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: ولد لآدم أربعون ولدا: عشرون غلاما وعشرون جارية

DURR-FULL:v2p423/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r6.speaker: أرطاة بن المنذر
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r6.claim: Arta reports that Eve bore Seth, Adam’s third child, after a severe labor; angels took him for forty days, taught him signs, then returned him.
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r6.anchor: عن أرطاة بن المنذر قال: بلغني أن حواء حملت بشيث حتى نبتت أسنانه وكانت تنظر إلى وجهه من صفاء في بطنها

DURR-FULL:v2p423/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses “by whom you ask one another” as “you transact by Him.”
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس {واتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به} قال: تعاطون به

DURR-FULL:v2p423/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r8.speaker: الربيع
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r8.claim: Al-Rabiʿ explains that people make covenants and pledges by God.
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r8.anchor: عن الربيع في الآية يقول: اتقوا الله الذي به تعاقدون وتعاهدون

DURR-FULL:v2p423/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r9.claim: Mujahid reads the phrase as a person saying, “I ask you by God and by kinship.”
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد {تساءلون به والأرحام} قال: يقول: أسألك بالله وبالرحم

DURR-FULL:v2p423/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r10.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r10.claim: Al-Hasan gives the expression as “I adjure you by God and by kinship.”
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r10.anchor: عن الحسن في الآية قال: هو قول الرجل: أنشدك بالله والرحم

DURR-FULL:v2p423/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r11.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r11.claim: Ibrahim reports the genitive reading al-arhām and explains it with the expression “I ask you by God and by kinship.”
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r11.anchor: عن إبراهيم {تساءلون به والأرحام} خفض قال: هو قول الرجل: أسألك بالله وبالرحم

DURR-FULL:v2p423/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r12.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r12.claim: Al-Hasan says that one who asks by God should be given, and likewise one who asks by kinship.
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r12.anchor: عن الحسن أنه تلا هذه الآية قال: إذا سئلت بالله فأعطه وإذا سئلت بالرحم فأعطه

DURR-FULL:v2p423/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the verse as commanding fear of God and observance and maintenance of kinship ties.
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r13.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {واتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به والأرحام} يقول: اتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به واتقوا الأرحام وصلوها

DURR-FULL:v2p423/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r14.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r14.claim: In a report through ʿIkrima from Ibn Abbas, God commands maintaining kinship, which prolongs worldly life and benefits people in the hereafter.
DURR-FULL:v2p423/r14.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله {الذي تساءلون به والأرحام} قال: قال ابن عباس: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: يقول الله تعالى: صلوا أرحامكم فإنه أبقى لكم

DURR-FULL:v2p424/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p424/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p424/r1.claim: Qatada reports the Prophet’s command to fear God and maintain kinship; one version says this prolongs life in this world and benefits the hereafter.
DURR-FULL:v2p424/r1.anchor: عن قتادة قال: ذكر لنا أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقول: اتقوا الله وصلوا الأرحام فإنه أبقى لكم في الدنيا وخير لكم في الآخرة

DURR-FULL:v2p424/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p424/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p424/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to read al-arhām and explain it as a command not to sever kinship ties.
DURR-FULL:v2p424/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك إن ابن عباس كان يقرأ {والأرحام} يقول: اتقوا الله لا تقطعوها

DURR-FULL:v2p424/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p424/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p424/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj transmits Ibn Abbas’s injunction to observe kinship ties.
DURR-FULL:v2p424/r3.anchor: من طريق ابن جريج قال: قال ابن عباس: اتقوا الأرحام

DURR-FULL:v2p424/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p424/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p424/r4.claim: Mujahid takes al-arhām as accusative and reads the phrase as a command not to cut kinship ties.
DURR-FULL:v2p424/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد {الذي تساءلون به والأرحام} قال: اتقوا الله واتقوا الأرحام أن تقطعوها نصب الأرحام

DURR-FULL:v2p424/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p424/r5.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v2p424/r5.claim: Ikrima glosses the command as “fear kinship ties, lest you sever them.”
DURR-FULL:v2p424/r5.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله {والأرحام} قال: اتقوا الأرحام أن تقطعوها

DURR-FULL:v2p424/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p424/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p424/r6.claim: Mujahid glosses raqīban as a guardian or preserver.
DURR-FULL:v2p424/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد {إن الله كان عليكم رقيبا} قال: حفيظا

DURR-FULL:v2p424/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p424/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v2p424/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says God watches people’s deeds, knowing and recognizing them.
DURR-FULL:v2p424/r7.anchor: عن ابن زيد قال: رقيبا على أعمالكم يعلمها ويعرفها

DURR-FULL:v2p424/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p424/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v2p424/r8.claim: Ibn Masud says the Prophet taught the prayer and need sermons; the latter includes praise, supplication, testimony, three Qurʾanic verses, then the speaker states the need.
DURR-FULL:v2p424/r8.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: علمنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خطبة الصلاة وخطبة الحاجة فأما خطبة الصلاة فالتشهد

AKHFASH:v1p243/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p243/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p243/r1.claim: The light form تساءلون deletes the final tāʾ from تساؤلهم; this deletion is common in Arabic, as in تكلمون, and a heavy form with assimilation is also possible.
AKHFASH:v1p243/r1.anchor: قال تعالى {تسآءلون به} خفيفة لأنها من تساؤلهم فانههم "يتساءلون" فحذف التاء الأخيرة، وذلك كثير في كلام العرب نحو {تكلمون} وان شئت ثقلت فادغمت.

AKHFASH:v1p243/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p243/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p243/r2.claim: He parses والأرحام as accusative, “and fear the ties of kinship,” because an explicit noun should not be coordinated with a genitive attached pronoun without repeating the preposition.
AKHFASH:v1p243/r2.anchor: قال الله تعالى {والأرحام} منصوبة أي: اتقوا الأرحام. وقال بعضهم {والأرحام} جر. والأول أحسن لأنك لا تجري الظاهر المجرور على المضمر المجرور.

AKHFASH:v1p243/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p243/r3.speaker: بعضهم
AKHFASH:v1p243/r3.claim: Some parse والأرحام as genitive, coordinated with the pronoun in تساءلون به; al-Akhfash prefers the accusative analysis.

AKHFASH:v1p243/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p243/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p243/r4.claim: The verb family of رقيب includes رقب يرقب رقبا ورقوبا.

IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the address ‘O people’ includes both unbelievers and hypocrites.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس : يا ايها الناس اي : للفريقين جميعا من الكفار والمنافقين

IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r2.claim: Muqatil ibn Hayyan glosses fearing your Lord as worshiping Him.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r2.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان قوله : اتقوا ربكم : واعبدوه

IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r3.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the single soul from which people were created as Adam; Mujahid, Abu Malik, Qatada, and Muqatil are also reported to agree.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r3.anchor: عن السدي قوله : يا ايها الناس اتقوا ربكم الذي خلقكم من نفس واحدة : اما خلقكم من نفس واحدة ، فمن ادم صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddi explains ‘and He created’ as ‘and He made.’
IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r4.anchor: به عن السدي قوله : وخلق منها زوجها قال : وجعل

IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the female created from the single soul as Eve.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r5.anchor: وبه عن السدي قوله وخلق منها زوجها قال حواء

IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r6.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak says Eve was created from Adam, from a back rib among the lower ribs.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r6.anchor: عن الضحاك : وخلق منها زوجها قال : خلق حواء من ادم ، من ضلع الخلف ، وهو من اسفل الاضلاع

IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r7.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says woman was made from man and desires men, while man was made from earth and desires the earth; it concludes, ‘restrain your women.’
IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r7.anchor: عن قتادة عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما يعني قوله : وخلق منها زوجها قال : خلقت المراة من الرجل

IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r8.claim: Mujahid says Eve came from Adam’s short rib while he slept; on waking he said ‘atha,’ a Nabataean word for woman. Al-Suddi, Qatada, and Muqatil also identify her as Eve.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p852#2/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : وخلق منها زوجها قال : حواء من قصير ادم وهو نائم ، فاستيقظ ، فقال : اثا ، بالنبطية ، اي امراة

IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r1.claim: Al-Suddi glosses ‘and He dispersed from the two’ as ‘created’; Muqatil ibn Hayyan is reported similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r1.anchor: عن السدي قوله : وبث منهما قال : بث : خلق

IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r2.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r2.claim: Muqatil ibn Hayyan says God created many men and women from Adam and Eve.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r2.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان قوله : وبث منهما : من ادم وحواء : يقول : خلق منهما رجالا كثيرا ونساء

IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r3.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the command to fear God is a warning addressed to believers.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله : اتقوا الله يعني : المؤمنين يحذرهم

IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r4.claim: Mujahid explains asking by God and kinship as saying, ‘I ask you by Allah and by the kinship.’
IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : واتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به قال : يقول اسالك بالله وبالرحم

IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says that when someone asks by God one should give, and when someone asks by kinship one should give because of the bond between them.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r5.anchor: تلا الحسن هذه الاية : واتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به والارحام : فاذا سئلت بالله فاعط ، واذا سئلت بالرحم فاعط

IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r6.speaker: الربيع
IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r6.claim: Al-Rabi' interprets the phrase as the One by whom people make commitments and affirmations; Ibrahim and Ikrima are reported to share Mujahid’s interpretation.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r6.anchor: عن الربيع في قوله : اتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به والارحام قال : الذي تعهدون وتعتقدون به

IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says to fear God by whom people ask one another and to maintain kinship; al-Dahhak agrees, while Muqatil and Ikrima say not to sever it.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : واتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به والارحام قال : اتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به ، واتقوا الارحام وصلوها

IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r8.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r8.claim: Mujahid glosses God as ever watchful as ‘guardian’; Qatada, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and al-Thawri are reported similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p853/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد : قوله : ان الله كان عليكم رقيبا قال : حفيظا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r1.claim: The relative clause ‘created you from one soul’ draws attention to wondrous creation and invites reflection; humanity’s common father supports Islam’s universal call, unlike laws restricted to particular peoples.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r1.anchor: ووصل { خلقكم } بصلة { من نفس واحدة } إدماج للتنبيه على عجيب هذا الخلق وحقه بالاعتبار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r2.claim: The verse implies that Muhammad is especially entitled to the polytheists’ allegiance because he is their kinsman.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r2.anchor: وفي الآية تعريض للمشركين بأن أولى الناس بأن يتبعوه هو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم لأنه من ذوي رحمهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r3.claim: The common origin prepares for the surah’s later rules that depend on descent and kinship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r3.anchor: وفي الآية تمهيد لما سيبين في هذه السورة من الأحكام المرتبة على النسب والقرابة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r4.claim: The single soul is Adam and the spouse is Hawwa; the apparent meaning of ‘from it’ is that Hawwa was brought forth from Adam’s rib.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r4.anchor: والنفس الواحدة : هي آدم . والزوج : حواء ، فإن حواء أخرجت من آدم . من ضلعه ، كما يقتضيه ظاهر قوله : { منها }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r5.claim: Min is partitive: Hawwa was created from part of Adam, either from the remnant of his clay or, as the apparent hadith in the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections says, from a rib.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r5.anchor: و ( من ) تبعيضية . ومعنى التبعيض أن حواء خلقت من جزء من آدم . قيل : من بقية الطينة التي خلق منها آدم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r6.claim: The claim that ‘from it’ merely means ‘from its kind’ adds nothing, since the female of every species belongs to that species.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r6.anchor: ومن قال : إن المعنى وخلق زوجها من نوعها لم يأت بطائل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r7.claim: The clauses ‘created her spouse’ and ‘spread from them’ are second and third relative qualifications: the wondrous creator merits reverence, and common descent confirms humanity’s connection despite descending through pairs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r7.anchor: وعطف قوله : { وخلق منها زوجها } على { خلقكم من نفس واحدة } ، فهو صلة ثانية . وقوله : { وبث منهما } صلة ثالثة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r8.claim: The three clauses detail how people were created from one soul; the order first states the creation generally, then details its wonder as the context requires.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r8.anchor: وقد حصل من ذكر هذه الصلات تفصيل لكيفية خلق الله الناس من نفس واحدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r9.claim: Hadith says Hawwa was created from Adam’s rib; on this account min marks the point of origin, meaning her creation was brought forth from his rib.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r9.anchor: وقد ورد في الحديث : أن حواء خلقت من ضلع آدم ، فلذلك يكون حرف ( من ) في قوله : { وخلق منها } للابتداء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r10.claim: ‘Spouse’ here is the first woman from whom humanity descended; each partner can conventionally be called zawj, although the word originally names the pair together.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r10.anchor: والزوج هنا أريد به الأنثى الأولى التي تناسل منها البشر ، وهي حواء . وأطلق عليها اسم الزوج لأن الرجل يكون منفردا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r11.speaker: الأصمعي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r11.claim: Al-Asma‘i strongly rejected the feminine form zawja and considered it a language error, although the author explains that customary usage made zawj apply to either sex.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p215/r11.anchor: ولذلك استوى فيه الرجل والمرأة لأنه من الوصف بالجامد ، فلا يقال للمرأة ( زوجة ) ، ولم يسمع في فصيح الكلام ، ولذلك عده بعض أهل اللغة لحنا . وكان الأصمعي ينكره أشد الإنكار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r1.speaker: الأصمعي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r1.claim: When confronted with Dhu al-Rumma’s use of zawja, al-Asma‘i dismissed him as colloquial, saying he had long eaten salted food and greens in grocers’ shops.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r1.anchor: فقال : إن ذا الرمة طالما أكل المالح والبقل في حوانيت البقالين ، يريد أنه مولد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r2.speaker: ذو الرمة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r2.claim: Dhu al-Rumma’s cited hemistich uses zawja for ‘wife,’ the example raised against al-Asma‘i’s rejection of that feminine form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r2.anchor: أذو زوجة بالمصر أم ذو خصومة أراك لها بالبصرة العام ثاويا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r3.speaker: الفرزدق
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r3.claim: Al-Farazdaq’s verse likewise uses zawjati for ‘my wife,’ providing another poetic example of the form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r3.anchor: وقال الفرزدق : وإن الذي يسعى ليفسد زوجتي كساع إلى أسد الشرى يستبيلها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r4.claim: The feminine form became common among jurists as a useful way to distinguish men and women when discussing legal rules.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r4.anchor: وشاع ذلك في كلام الفقهاء ، قصدوا به التفرقة بين الرجل والمرأة عند ذكر الأحكام ، وهي تفرقة حسنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r5.claim: The usage of spouse recalls the earlier account of Adam and his spouse in the surah of al-Baqara.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r5.anchor: وتقدم عند قوله تعالى : { وقلنا يا آدم اسكن أنت وزوجك الجنة في سورة البقرة ( 35 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r6.claim: The creation of a spouse from one origin is wondrous and varies in form and traits; men and women are each beneficiaries of the other’s creation, and the species receives the gift of offspring.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r6.anchor: وقد شمل وخلق منها زوجها } العبرة بهذا الخلق العجيب الذي أصله واحد ، ويخرج هو مختلف الشكل والخصائص

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r7.claim: Bathth means spreading and dispersing many things; the scattered people compared to moths illustrate the word.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r8.claim: The singular adjective kathīr describes the plural rijāl because kathīr has the same form with singular and plural; a parallel is the many devotees with a prophet.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r8.anchor: ووصف الرجال ، وهو جمع ، بكثير ، وهو مفرد ، لأن كثير يستوي فيه المفرد والجمع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r9.claim: The verse omits ‘many’ after women because the adjective after men and the verb ‘spread’ already indicate that the women are numerous.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r9.anchor: واستغنى عن وصف النساء بكثير لدلالة وصف الرجل به ما يقتضيه فعل البث من الكثرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r10.claim: The renewed command to fear God begins the surah’s legislation, especially for Muslims retaining Jahili habits of neglecting relatives’ and orphans’ rights.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r10.anchor: شروع في التشريع المقصود من السورة ، وأعيد فعل { اتقوا } : لأن هذه التقوى مأمور بها المسلمون خاصة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r11.claim: Using God’s proper name after ‘your Lord’ instills awe appropriate to legislation; the earlier address ‘fear your Lord’ served encouragement.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r11.anchor: واستحضر اسم الله العلم هنا دون ضمير يعود إلى ربكم لإدخال الروع في ضمائر السامعين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r12.claim: ‘You ask one another by Him’ means invoking God when swearing; such mutual invocation signifies utmost reverence, so people should all the more fear Him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p216/r12.anchor: ومعنى { تساءلون به } يسأل بعضكم بعضا به في القسم فالمسايلة به تؤذن بمنتهى العظمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r1.claim: Most readers pronounce tusāʾalūn with a doubled sīn by assimilating the second tāʾ into sīn because they are close in articulation and share voicelessness; Hamza, Asim, al-Kisai, and Khalaf use a light sīn after dropping tāʾ for ease.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r1.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { تساءلون } بتشديد السين لإدغام التاء الثانية ، وهي تاء التفاعل في السين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r2.claim: Most readers put al-arḥām in the accusative, coordinated with God’s name; Hamza reads it in the genitive, coordinated with the attached pronoun.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r2.anchor: { والأرحام } قرأه الجمهور بالنصب عطفا على اسم الله . وقرأه حمزة بالجر عطفا على الضمير المجرور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r3.claim: On the majority’s accusative reading, kinship is to be revered by observing its rights; the construction elides ‘rights,’ and the verse begins legislation connected to the preceding creation account.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r3.anchor: فعلى قراءة الجمهور يكون الأرحام مأمورا بتقواها على المعنى المصدري أي اتقائها ، وهو على حذف مضاف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r4.claim: Hamza’s genitive reading exalts kinship, as in the Arab oath ‘I adjure you by God and kin’; the report says Utba was awed while hearing the Prophet recite 41:13 and invoked both.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r4.anchor: وعلى قراءة حمزة يكون تعظيما لشأن الأرحام أي التي يسأل بعضكم بعضا بها ، وذلك قول العرب : ( ناشدتك الله والرحم )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r5.speaker: المبرد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r5.claim: Al-Mubarrad objects to coordinating a noun with an attached genitive pronoun without repeating the preposition, saying he would leave prayer if an imam recited it that way.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r5.anchor: حتى قال المبرد : ( لو قرأ الإمام بهاته القراءة لأخذت نعلي وخرجت من الصلاة )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r6.speaker: ابن مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r6.claim: Ibn Malik rightly permits coordination with a genitive pronoun without repeating its preposition; the author calls al-Mubarrad’s rejection narrow-minded and overconfident.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r6.anchor: ولقد أصاب ابن مالك في تجويزه العطف على المجرور بدون إعادة الجار ، فتكون تعريضا بعوائد الجاهلية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r7.claim: The genitive reading criticizes Jahili Arabs who invoked kinship in oaths yet neglected its rights and wronged orphan relatives; they also harmed Muhammad despite his kinship and claim to their care.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r7.anchor: إذ يتساءلون بينهم بالرحم وأواصر القرابة ثم يهملون حقوقها ولا يصلونها ، ويعتدون على الأيتام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r8.claim: On Hamza’s reading, the kinship clause continues the preceding verse’s meaning about humanity’s shared creation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p217/r8.anchor: وعلى قراءة حمزة يكون معنى الآية تتمة لمعنى التي قبلها

FARRA:v1p252/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p252/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p252/r1.claim: واحدة is feminine because نفس is grammatically feminine, though واحد would also be valid by reference to the male, Adam.
FARRA:v1p252/r1.anchor: قال (واحدة) لأن النفس مؤنثة، فقال: واحدة لتأنيث النفس

FARRA:v1p252/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p252/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p252/r2.claim: بث منهما means God spread the creatures; Arabic also uses أبث الله الخلق and both بثثتك and أبثثتك for telling someone what is within oneself.
FARRA:v1p252/r2.anchor: العرب تقول: بث الله الخلق: أي نشرهم

FARRA:v1p252/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p252/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p252/r3.claim: He parses الأرحام accusatively as an additional object of “fear”: fear God and kinship ties, lest you sever them.
FARRA:v1p252/r3.anchor: فنصب الأرحام يريد واتقوا الأرحام أن تقطعوها

FARRA:v1p252/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p252/r4.speaker: إبراهيم
FARRA:v1p252/r4.claim: Ibrāhīm read الأرحام in the genitive, comparing بالله والرحم.
FARRA:v1p252/r4.anchor: عن الأعمش عن إبراهيم أنه خفض الأرحام

FARRA:v1p252/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p252/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p252/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ calls the genitive reading awkward because Arabic does not coordinate a genitive already represented by a pronoun; he permits this construction in poetry under metrical constraint.
FARRA:v1p252/r5.anchor: وفيه قبح لأن العرب لا ترد مخفوضا على مخفوض وقد كنى عنه

FARRA:v1p252/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p252/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p252/r6.claim: An unnamed poet uses the genitive construction in نعلق في مثل السواري سيوفنا … والكعب; al-Farrāʾ says poetic constraint licenses it.

FARRA:v1p252/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p252/r7.speaker: بعضهم
FARRA:v1p252/r7.claim: Some read تسائلون as تتساءلون with the first tāʾ assimilated into the sīn.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r1.claim: The opening is parsed as vocative: yā is the call particle, ayy the singular vocative, and hāʾ an attention particle; al-nās modifies ayy or is its complement per al-Akhfash.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r1.anchor: «يا» حرف نداء، و «أي» منادى مفرد- و «ها»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r2.claim: Al-rabb means owner; the verse points to the Creator and origin of existence, and urges kinship because this lineage is sacred even at a distance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r2.anchor: «والرب» : المالك، وفي الآية تنبيه على الصانع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r3.claim: Wāḥida is feminine because nafs is grammatically feminine, supported by the cited verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r3.anchor: وقال: واحدة على تأنيث لفظ النفس، وهذا كقول الشاعر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r4.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة، ومجاهد، وقتادة وغيرهما
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads “one person” without feminine hāʾ, matching the intended meaning Adam, as Mujāhid, Qatāda, and others explain.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة- «من نفس واحد» - بغير هاء، وهذا على مراعاة المعنى، إذ المراد بالنفس آدم صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r5.claim: Creation means originating; the spouse is Eve, and zawj can mean a man’s wife or zawja, as in Abū Firās’s verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r5.anchor: والخلق في الآية: بمعنى الاختراع، ويعني بقوله: زوجها حواء، والزوج في كلام العرب: امرأة الرجل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس، ومجاهد، والسدي، وقتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r6.claim: They report that God created Adam alone in the Garden, then removed a short rib from his left side while asleep (some say right) and created Eve.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد والسدي وقتادة: إن الله تعالى خلق آدم وحشا في الجنة وحده، ثم نام فانتزع الله أحد أضلاعه القصيرى من شماله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r7.claim: A sound hadith says woman was created from a rib and straightening her breaks her; the break is explained as divorce.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r7.anchor: ويعضد هذا القول الحديث الصحيح في قوله عليه السلام: «إن المرأة خلقت من ضلع، فإن ذهبت تقيمها كسرتها»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r8.speaker: بعضهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r8.claim: Some read “from it” as “from its kind”; the phrase can cover this or bodily substance from Adam’s rib with the soul from the same kind.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم: معنى منها من جنسها، واللفظ يتناول المعنيين، أو يكون لحمها وجواهرها من ضلعه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r9.claim: Bathth means spread, as in the dispersed moths of 101:4.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r9.anchor: وبث معناه: نشر، كقوله تعالى: كالفراش المبثوث [القارعة: 4]

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r10.claim: Naming offspring as men and women implies the intersex condition is not a third kind.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r10.anchor: وحصره ذريتها إلى نوعين الرجال والنساء مقتض أن الخنثى ليس بنوع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r11.claim: Even if an intersex person’s outward status is unclear, in reality they return to one of the two kinds.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r11.anchor: وأنه وإن فرضناه مشكل الظاهر عندنا، فله حقيقة ترده إلى أحد هذين النوعين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r12.claim: Repeating the command to be mindful of God reinforces it and alerts the addressees.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r12.anchor: وفي تكرار الأمر بالاتقاء تأكيد وتنبيه لنفوس المأمورين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r13.claim: The relative pronoun occupies the accusative as an adjective.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r13.anchor: والذي في موضع نصب على النعت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r14.claim: Tasāʾalūn means mutual concern, as when one asks another to act by God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p3#2/r14.anchor: وتسائلون معناه: تتعاطفون به، فيقول أحدكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r1.speaker: طائفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r1.claim: One group interprets the phrase as asking for rights by God and making God the means for claims.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r1.anchor: وقالت طائفة معناه: تسائلون به حقوقكم وتجعلونه مقطعا لها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r2.claim: The form derives from tatasāʾalūn, with the second tāʾ changed to sīn and assimilated; Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, and one Ibn ʿAmr transmission read that way.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r2.anchor: وأصله: «تتساءلون» ، فأبدلت التاء الثانية سينا وأدغمت في السين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r3.claim: Other readers lighten the sīn by deleting the second tāʾ; the readings reflect assimilation or deletion among neighboring sounds.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r3.anchor: وقرأ الباقون- «تساءلون» - بسين مخففة وذلك لأنهم حذفوا التاء الثانية تخفيفا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r4.speaker: أبو علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r4.claim: Abū ʿAlī explains that neighboring sounds are eased by deletion, assimilation, or substitution, giving ṭast as an example.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r4.anchor: قال أبو علي: وإذا اجتمعت المتقاربة خففت بالحذف والإدغام والإبدال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r5.speaker: العجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r5.claim: Al-ʿAjjāj’s line supplies poetic evidence for the sound form being discussed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r5.anchor: قال العجاج: [الرجز] لو عرضت لأيبلي قس ... أشعث في هيكله مندس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads tasʾalūn without the long alif.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r6.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود- «تسألون» - خفيفة بغير ألف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r7.claim: The seven except Ḥamza read wa-al-arḥām accusative, either coordinated with bihi’s accusative position or, more clearly, governed by an implied “be mindful of kinship, lest you sever it.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r7.anchor: والأرحام نصب على العطف على موضع به لأن موضعه نصب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r8.claim: They explain the accusative reading as a command to be mindful of kinship and not sever it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r8.anchor: وهذه قراءة السبعة إلا حمزة، وعليها فسر ابن عباس وغيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r9.speaker: عبد الله بن يزيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r9.claim: He reads wa-al-arḥām nominative, with an implied predicate that kinship deserves connection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r9.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله بن يزيد- والأرحام- بالرفع وذلك على الابتداء والخبر مقدر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r10.speaker: حمزة وجماعة من العلماء، والحسن، وإبراهيم النخعي، ومجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r10.claim: They read wa-al-arḥām genitive, coordinating with the suffixed pronoun and understanding invocation by God and kinship.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r10.anchor: وقرأ حمزة وجماعة من العلماء- «والأرحام» - بالخفض عطفا على الضمير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r11.speaker: رؤساء نحويي البصرة، والزجاج عن المازني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r11.claim: Basran grammarians disallow coordinating an overt noun with a genitive pronoun; al-Zajjāj reports al-Māzinī’s argument that the terms must be interchangeable.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r11.anchor: وهذه القراءة عند رؤساء نحويي البصرة لا تجوز، لأنه لا يجوز عندهم أن يعطف ظاهر على مضمر مخفوض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r12.speaker: سيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r12.claim: Sībawayh calls the construction poor and permits it only in poetry, citing two lines.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r12.anchor: وأما سيبويه فهي عنده قبيحة لا تجوز إلا في الشعر، كما قال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r13.speaker: بعض النحويين، وأبو علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r13.claim: Some grammarians approved the genitive construction, but Abū ʿAlī judges it weak by analogy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p4/r13.anchor: واستهلها بعض النحويين، قال أبو علي: ذلك ضعيف في القياس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r1.claim: A suffixed genitive pronoun is inseparable like part of a word, so an overt noun cannot be coordinated with it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r1.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: المضمر المخفوض لا ينفصل فهو كحرف من الكلمة، ولا يعطف على حرف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r2.claim: He rejects the genitive reading semantically: invoking kinship does not advance the command to fear God and disrupts the sentence’s eloquence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r2.anchor: ويرد عندي هذه القراءة من المعنى وجهان: أحدهما أن ذكر الأرحام فيما يتساءل به لا معنى له في الحض على تقوى الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r3.claim: The reading also appears to endorse swearing by kinship, conflicting with the sound hadith to swear by God or be silent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r3.anchor: والوجه الثاني أن في ذكرها على ذلك تقريرا للتساؤل بها والقسم بحرمتها، والحديث الصحيح يرد ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r4.speaker: طائفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r4.claim: Some take the genitive as God swearing by His creatures, with “God is watching over you” as the answer; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says this conflicts with the sentence’s order.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r4.anchor: وقالت طائفة: إنما خفض- «والأرحام» - على جهة القسم من الله على ما اختص به لا إله إلا هو

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r5.claim: Kāna here does not confine the statement to the past; it means God was and continues to be watching.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r5.anchor: وكان في هذه الآية ليست لتحديد الماضي فقط، بل المعنى: كان وهو يكون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r6.claim: Raqīb is the active participle of raqaba: close observation by sight or insight to verify a matter, with preservation, witnessing, and knowledge.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r6.anchor: والرقيب: بناء الاسم الفاعل من رقب يرقب إذا أحد النظر بالبصر أو بالبصيرة إلى أمر ما ليتحققه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r7.claim: “Over you” carries a warning; “for you” could suggest watching on your behalf what others do.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r7.anchor: وفي قوله عليكم ضرب من الوعيد، ولم يقل «لكم» للاشتراك الذي كان يدخل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r8.claim: A person watching an arrow leave the bow in the qidāḥ game is also called a raqīb.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r8.anchor: ومما ذكرناه قيل للذي يرقب خروج السهم من ربابة الضريب في القداح رقيب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r9.speaker: أبو دؤاد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r9.claim: Abū Duʾād’s verse likens observers to watchers at the shooting game.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p5/r9.anchor: ومنه قول أبي دؤاد: [مجزوء الكامل] كمقاعد الرقباء للضرباء أيديهم نواهد

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p118#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p118#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p118#2/r1.claim: Batha means that God spread people across the earth.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p118#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p118#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p118#2/r2.claim: With accusative al-arḥāma, the command is to fear God and also fear severing family ties.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p118#2/r2.anchor: من نصب أراد: اتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به واتقوا الأرحام أن تقطعوها.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p118#2/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p118#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p118#2/r3.claim: With genitive al-arḥāmi, the phrase means asking by God and by kinship, like swearing by God and kinship.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p118#2/r3.anchor: ومن خفض أراد: الذي تساءلون به وبالأرحام (1) . وهو مثل قول الرجل: نشدتك بالله وبالرحم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r1.speaker: عطية عن ابن عباس، الحسن، مجاهد، جابر بن زيد، قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r1.claim: One view says this verse was revealed in Mecca; it is transmitted by Atiyya from Ibn Abbas and held by Hasan, Mujahid, Jabir ibn Zayd, and Qatada.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r1.anchor: أنها مكية رواه عطية عن ابن عباس وهو قول الحسن ومجاهد وجابر بن زيد وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r2.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس، مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r2.claim: A second view says it was revealed in Medina; this is transmitted by Ata from Ibn Abbas and held by Muqatil.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r2.anchor: إنها مدنية رواه عطاء عن ابن عباس وهو قول مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r3.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r3.claim: A qualified view says the sura is Medinan except 4:58, revealed at Mecca when Muhammad sought the Kaaba keys from Uthman ibn Talha to give them to al-Abbas.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r3.anchor: إلا آية نزلت بمكة في عثمان بن طلحة حين أراد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r4.claim: The command to be mindful of the Lord means obedience.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r4.anchor: أحدهما أنه بمعنى الطاعة قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r5.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r5.claim: Alternatively, being mindful of the Lord means fear.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r6.claim: The one soul is Adam and his spouse is Eve.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r7.speaker: الجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r7.claim: The majority take min in created from it as partitive: Eve was created from Adam himself.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r7.anchor: ﴿ وخلق منها ﴾ للتبعيض في قول الجمهور

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r8.speaker: ابن بحر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r8.claim: Ibn Bahr instead understands created from it to mean created from the same kind.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r8.anchor: ابن بحر منها أي من جنسها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r9.claim: One report says Eve was created after Adam entered the Garden.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r9.anchor: أحدهما أنها خلقت بعد دخوله الجنة قاله ابن مسعود و ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r10.speaker: كعب الأحبار ووهب وابن إسحاق
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r10.claim: Another report says Eve was created before Adam entered the Garden.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r10.anchor: قبل دخوله الجنة قاله كعب الأحبار ووهب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas relates that God put Adam to sleep and created Eve from his left rib without causing him pain; after waking, Adam identified her as Hawwaʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p1/r11.anchor: لما خلق الله آدم ألقى عليه النوم فخلق حواء من ضلع من أضلاعه اليسرى فلم تؤذه بشيء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r1.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r1.claim: Baththa means to spread; Arabs also say abaththa for God spreading creation and use the verb for disclosing what is within oneself.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r1.anchor: قال الفراء بث نشر ومن العرب من يقول أبث الله الخلق ويقولون بثثتك ما في نفسي و أبثثتك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r2.claim: A number of named readers and transmitters read tasaʾalūn with a doubled sīn; other listed readers and transmitters read it lightly.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r2.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير و نافع و ابن عامر و البرجمي عن أبي بكر عن عاصم واليزيدي و شجاع و الجعفي و عبد الوارث عن أبي عمرو تساءلون بالتشديد و قرأ عاصم و حمزة و الكسائي و كثير من أصحاب أبي عمرو عنه بالتخفيف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r3.claim: The original form is tatasāʾalūn; the doubled reading assimilates tāʾ into the nearby sīn.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r3.anchor: الأصل تتساءلون فمن قرأ بالتشديد أدغم التاء في السين لقرب مكان هذه من هذه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r4.claim: The light reading deletes the second tāʾ because two tāʾs would otherwise meet.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r5.claim: One interpretation of asking one another by God is that people show mutual affection through the oath.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r5.anchor: أحدها تتعاطفون به قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r6.speaker: الضحاك والربيع
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r6.claim: Another interpretation is that people make covenants and agreements by God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r6.anchor: تتعاقدون و تتعاهدون به قاله الضحاك والربيع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r7.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r7.claim: A third interpretation is that people seek their rights by invoking God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r7.anchor: والثالث تطلبون حقوقكم به قاله الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r8.speaker: الجمهور، ابن عباس، مجاهد، عكرمة، السدي، ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r8.claim: The majority read al-arḥām in the accusative, construing it as a command to fear severing kin ties; Ibn Abbas and the named exegetes explain it this way.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r8.anchor: فالجمهور على نصب الميم على معنى واتقوا الأرحام أن تقطعوها و فسرها على هذا ابن عباس و مجاهد وعكرمة والسدي و ابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r9.speaker: الحسن وعطاء والنخعي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r9.claim: Hasan, Ata, and Nakhaʿi interpret the genitive reading as coordinated with the pronoun in by which you ask.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r9.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وقتادة و الأعمش و حمزة بخفض الميم على معنى تساءلون به وبالأرحام و فسرها على هذا الحسن و عطاء و النخعي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r10.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r10.claim: Al-Zajjaj rejects the genitive grammatically except in poetic necessity and theologically because the Prophet forbade swearing by fathers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r10.anchor: خطأ في العربية لا يجوز إلا في اضطرار الشعر وخطأ في الدين لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لا تحلفوا بآبائكم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r11.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r11.claim: Al-Farraʾ takes a view like al-Zajjaj's objection to the genitive reading.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r12.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r12.claim: Ibn al-Anbari understands Hamza as describing a former customary oath: people used to invoke God and kinship in pre-Islamic times.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r12.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري إنما أراد حمزة الخبر عن الأمر القديم الذي جرت عادتهم به فالمعنى الذي كنتم تساءلون به وبالأرحام في الجاهلية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r13.speaker: أبو علي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r13.claim: Abu Ali parses the genitive as coordinated with the pronoun governed by bi, but calls it weak and rare, so avoiding it is better.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r13.anchor: قال أبو علي من جر عطف على الضمير المجرور بالباء وهو ضعيف في القياس قليل في الاستعمال فترك الأخذ به أحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r14.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r14.claim: Al-raqīb means the guardian or keeper, according to Ibn Abbas and Mujahid.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r14.anchor: فقال ابن عباس ومجاهد الرقيب الحافظ

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r15.speaker: الخطابي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r15.claim: Al-Khattabi describes al-raqīb as a guardian from whom nothing is absent; among people it is one assigned to protect something vigilantly without heedlessness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p2/r15.anchor: هو الحافظ الذي لا يغيب عنه شيء وهو في نعوت الآدميين الموكل بحفظ الشيء المترصد له المتحرز عن الغفلة فيه

MAJAZ:v1p113/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p113/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p113/r1.claim: Al-arḥām is accusative in “fear God and the kinship ties”; those who read it genitive connect it to the preposition bi- in tasāʾalūna bih.
MAJAZ:v1p113/r1.anchor: [ «واتقوا الله الذي] تسائلون به والأرحام» (1) : اتقوا الله والأرحام نصب، ومن جرها فإنما يجرها بالباء.

MAJAZ:v1p113/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p113/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p113/r2.claim: Raqīban means a guardian or keeper.
MAJAZ:v1p113/r2.anchor: «كان عليكم رقيبا» (1) : حافظا، وقال أبو دؤاد الإيادى:

MAJAZ:v1p113/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p113/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p113/r3.claim: Abū Duʾād al-Iyādī’s line compares guards’ hands to those of the dice throwers, whose hands are stretched out.
MAJAZ:v1p113/r3.anchor: كمقاعد الرقباء للضرباء أيديهم نواهد الضريب الذي يضرب بالقداح نهدت أيديهم أي مدوها.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#2/r1.claim: God brought forth Adam and Eve’s many descendants and spread them through the world with diverse peoples, traits, colors, and languages, to return to Him at resurrection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#2/r1.anchor: أي: وذرأ منهما، أي: من آدم وحواء رجالا كثيرا ونساء، ونشرهم في أقطار العالم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#2/r2.speaker: إبراهيم ومجاهد والحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#2/r2.claim: Ibrahim, Mujahid, and al-Hasan explain asking one another by God and kinship as saying, ‘I ask you by God and by kinship.’
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#2/r2.anchor: قال إبراهيم ومجاهد والحسن: {الذي تساءلون به} أي: كما يقال: أسألك بالله وبالرحم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#2/r3.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#2/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak reads the wording as invoking God by whom people make covenants and pledges.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#2/r3.anchor: وقال الضحاك: واتقوا الله الذي به تعاقدون وتعاهدون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وعكرمة والحسن والضحاك والربيع
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#2/r4.claim: The command concerning kinship means not to sever ties but to honor and maintain them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#2/r4.anchor: واتقوا الأرحام أن تقطعوها، ولكن بروها وصلوها، قاله ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وعكرمة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#2/r5.claim: Some readers pronounce al-arḥām in the genitive, coordinating it with the pronoun in ‘by Him,’ so people ask by God and kinship.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ (3) بعضهم: {والأرحام} بالخفض على العطف على الضمير في به

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#3/r1.claim: God watches all deeds and circumstances, as also stated at 85:9.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#3/r1.anchor: هو مراقب لجميع أعمالكم وأحوالكم كما قال: {والله على كل شيء شهيد} [البروج: 9]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#3/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#3/r2.claim: A sound hadith commands worship with awareness that God sees the worshipper, even when the worshipper does not see Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#3/r2.anchor: وفي الحديث الصحيح: "اعبد الله كأنك تراه، فإن لم تكن تراه فإنه يراك"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#3/r3.claim: Mentioning humanity’s one father and mother should foster mutual affection and compassion toward the weak.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#3/r3.anchor: ولهذا ذكر تعالى أن أصل الخلق من أب [واحد] (5) وأم واحدة؛ ليعطف بعضهم على بعض، ويحننهم (1) على ضعفائهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#3/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#3/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#3/r4.claim: After Mudar’s poor, scantily clothed delegation arrived, the Prophet recited 4:1 and 59:18 in a sermon, then urged people to give charity.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#3/r4.anchor: من حديث جرير بن عبد الله البجلي؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حين قدم عليه أولئك النفر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#3/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#3/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#3/r5.claim: The report of Ibn Mas‘ud’s sermon of need says the Prophet recited three verses, including 4:1.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p206#3/r5.anchor: وهكذا رواه (6) الإمام أحمد وأهل السنن عن ابن مسعود في خطبة الحاجة (7)

NAHHAS:v1p430/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p430/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p430/r1.claim: يا is a vocative particle that may be omitted when the addressee is already known; أي is a singular vocative and ها signals attention.
NAHHAS:v1p430/r1.anchor: ( يا ) حرف ينادى به وقد يجوز أن يحذف إذا كان المنادى يعلم بالنداء و ( أي ) نداء مفرد و ها تنبيه

NAHHAS:v1p430/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p430/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p430/r2.claim: الناس is an adjective of أي, not accusative in its underlying position except under al-Māzinī’s analysis; al-Akhfash instead treats أي as a relative pronoun whose clause is its adjective.
NAHHAS:v1p430/r2.anchor: ( الناس ) نعت لأي لا يجوز نصبه على الموضع لأن الكلام لا يتم قبله إلا على قول المازني وزعم الأخفش أن أيا موصولة بالنعت

NAHHAS:v1p430/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p430/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p430/r3.claim: اتقوا is an imperative, which accounts for deletion of its nūn; الذي is accusative as an adjective of ربكم.
NAHHAS:v1p430/r3.anchor: ( اتقوا ربكم ) أمر فلذلك حذفت منه النون ( الذي خلقكم ) في موضع نصب على النعت

NAHHAS:v1p430/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p430/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p430/r4.claim: نفس is feminine by form, though masculine من نفس واحد is also possible in ordinary speech.
NAHHAS:v1p430/r4.anchor: ( من نفس واحدة ) أنثت على اللفظ ويجوز في الكلام من نفس واحد

NAHHAS:v1p430/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p430/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p430/r5.claim: Masculine and feminine dual forms share the same marker, unlike plurals, which differ.
NAHHAS:v1p430/r5.anchor: المذكر والمؤنث في التثنية على لفظ واحد في العلامة وليس كذا الجمع لاختلافه

NAHHAS:v1p430/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p430/r6.speaker: أهل المدينة
NAHHAS:v1p430/r6.claim: Medinan readers assimilate the first tāʾ of تساءلون into sīn; Kūfans delete one of the two tāʾs because they meet and the meaning remains clear.
NAHHAS:v1p430/r6.anchor: هذه قراءة أهل المدينة بإدغام التاء في السين وقراءة أهل الكوفة ( تساءلون ) بحذف التاء

NAHHAS:v1p430/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p430/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p430/r7.claim: This deletion has a parallel in إذ تلقونه بألسنتكم.

NAHHAS:v1p430/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p430/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p430/r8.claim: الأرحام is coordinated with اتقوا الله: fear God and kinship ties by not severing them.
NAHHAS:v1p430/r8.anchor: ( والأرحام ) عطف أي واتقوا الأرحام أن تقطعوها

NAHHAS:v1p430/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p430/r9.speaker: إبراهيم وقتادة وحمزة
NAHHAS:v1p430/r9.claim: Ibrāhīm, Qatāda, and Ḥamza read الأرحام in the genitive; Basran leaders call it an inadmissible solecism, while Kūfans call it ugly without explaining why.
NAHHAS:v1p430/r9.anchor: وقرأ إبراهيم وقتادة وحمزة ( والأرحام ) بالخفض وقد تكلم النحويون في ذلك

NAHHAS:v1p430/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p430/r10.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v1p430/r10.claim: Sībawayh says a noun governed by a preposition cannot be coordinated with a pronoun governed by a preposition, since the pronoun is like nunation.
NAHHAS:v1p430/r10.anchor: وقال سيبويه لم يعطف على المضمر المخفوض لأنه بمنزلة التنوين

NAHHAS:v1p430/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p430/r11.speaker: أبو عثمان المازني
NAHHAS:v1p430/r11.claim: Abū ʿUthmān al-Māzinī argues that a coordinated term and its antecedent are partners: what applies to one must apply to the other.
NAHHAS:v1p430/r11.anchor: قال أبو عثمان المازني المعطوف والمعطوف عليه شريكان لا يدخل في أحدهما إلا ما دخل في الآخر

NAHHAS:v1p430/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p430/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p430/r12.claim: Two poems demonstrate coordination after a prepositional pronoun: one has بك والأيام and another بينها والكعب; the excerpt does not name either poet.
NAHHAS:v1p430/r12.anchor: فاذهب فما بك والأيام من عجب ) وكما قال ( وما بينها والكعب غوط نفانف

NAHHAS:v1p430/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p430/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p430/r13.claim: The claim that الأرحام is an oath is wrong in meaning and grammar; a Prophetic address instead supports the accusative as an exhortation to maintain kinship.
NAHHAS:v1p430/r13.anchor: وقال بعضهم والأرحام قسم وهذا خطأ من المعنى والإعراب لأن الحديث عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يدل على النصب

NAHHAS:v1p430/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p430/r14.speaker: جرير
NAHHAS:v1p430/r14.claim: Jarīr reports that the Prophet, moved by the poverty of a barefoot group, urged people to fear God and kinship and then gave a charity appeal.
NAHHAS:v1p430/r14.anchor: عن المنذر بن جرير عن أبيه قال كنت عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى جاء قوم من مصر حفاة عراة

NAHHAS:v1p430/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p430/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p430/r15.claim: If الأرحام were an oath, the omitted wording would have to be “by the wombs”; such ellipsis is not permitted unless the sentence requires it.
NAHHAS:v1p430/r15.anchor: فلو كان قسما كان قد حذف منه لأن المعنى ويقولون بالأرحام أي ورب الأرحام ولا يجوز الحذف

NAHHAS:v1p430/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p430/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p430/r16.claim: A sound Prophetic report says an oath is to be sworn by God; by analogy, one can adjure only by God, refuting “I ask you by God and by kinship.”
NAHHAS:v1p430/r16.anchor: وأيضا فقد صح عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من كان حالفا فليحلف بالله فكما لا يجوز أن تحلف إلا بالله

NAHHAS:v1p430/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p430/r17.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v1p430/r17.claim: Abū Isḥāq explains تساءلون به as seeking rights through God and says this sense gives no basis for the genitive reading.
NAHHAS:v1p430/r17.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق معنى تساءلون به تطلبون حقوقكم به ولا معنى للخفض على هذا

NAHHAS:v1p430/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p430/r18.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p430/r18.claim: The noun رحم is feminine and is attested in four vocalized forms.
NAHHAS:v1p430/r18.anchor: والرحم مؤنثة ويقال رحم ورحم ورحم ورحم

NAHHAS:v1p430/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p430/r19.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v1p430/r19.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses رقيب as حفيظ, a vigilant guardian.

NAHHAS:v1p430/r20.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p430/r20.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p430/r20.claim: The verb رقب is used in the sense “to watch,” with the verbal nouns رقبة and رقبان.
NAHHAS:v1p430/r20.anchor: يقال رقب الرجل وقد رقبته رقبة ورقبانا

JISHUMI:v2p1441/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1441/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1441/r1.claim: The surah is Medinan; its verse count differs by region: 176 in Kufa, 175 in the Hijaz and Basra, and 177 in Syria.
JISHUMI:v2p1441/r1.anchor: وهي مدنية. مائة وست وسبعون آية في الكوفي، وخمس في الحجازي والبصري

JISHUMI:v2p1441/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1441/r2.speaker: ابن كعب
JISHUMI:v2p1441/r2.claim: A report from Ibn Kaʿb says the Prophet promised a reader of Surat al-Nisa reward like charity to every believer, an inheritance, freeing a person, and deliverance from associating partners with God.
JISHUMI:v2p1441/r2.anchor: وعن ابن كعب عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أنه قال: من قرأ سورة النساء فكأنما تصدق على كل مؤمن ومؤمنة

JISHUMI:v2p1441/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1441/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1441/r3.claim: The prior surah ended with a command to fear God, and this one opens with the same command, extending obedience across both surahs.
JISHUMI:v2p1441/r3.anchor: ولما ختم السورة المتقدمة بالأمر بالتقوى افتتح هذه السورة بالأمر بالتقوى

JISHUMI:v2p1441/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1441/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1441/r4.claim: One reading of the transition is that the former surah addressed believers, while this opening commands all morally responsible people to fear God.
JISHUMI:v2p1441/r4.anchor: وقيل: أمر هناك بالتقوى للمؤمنين وأمر ههنا لجميع المكلفين بالتقوى

JISHUMI:v2p1441/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1441/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1441/r5.claim: Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisai read تساءلون with a light sīn by deleting a tāʾ; others double the sīn through assimilation.
JISHUMI:v2p1441/r5.anchor: قرأ تساءلون بتخفيف السين عاصم وحمزة والكسائي، والباقون بالتشديد

JISHUMI:v2p1441/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1441/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1441/r6.claim: Hamza alone, with al-Nakhaʿi, Qatada, and al-Aʿmash, reads الأرحام in the genitive; the others read it with fatḥa.
JISHUMI:v2p1441/r6.anchor: وقرأ حمزة وحده والأرحام بخفض الميم، وهي قراءة النخعي وقتادة والأعمش، وقرأ الباقون بفتح الميم

JISHUMI:v2p1441/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1441/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1441/r7.claim: He prefers the fatḥa: it means fear severing kinship ties, and Arabic normally avoids coordinating an explicit noun with a preposition attached to a pronoun unless repeating the preposition.
JISHUMI:v2p1441/r7.anchor: فوجه ذلك: واتقوا الأرحام أن تقطعوها

JISHUMI:v2p1441/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1441/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1441/r8.claim: An unnamed poet supplies a rare precedent for coordinating an explicit noun with a preposition attached to a pronoun.
JISHUMI:v2p1441/r8.anchor: قال الشاعر: فاليوم أصبحت تهجونا وتشتمنا

JISHUMI:v2p1441/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1441/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1441/r9.claim: Some read الأرحام nominative as a new subject after ending the previous clause; al-Akhfash says the genitive reading implies an omitted preposition.
JISHUMI:v2p1441/r9.anchor: وعن بعضهم والأرحام بالرفع على الابتداء، كأنه نوى تمام الكلام عند قوله: تساءلون به

JISHUMI:v2p1441/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1441/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1441/r10.claim: Most readers pronounce qāf and kāf distinctly in خلقكم; some assimilate qāf into kāf because they share an articulation point.
JISHUMI:v2p1441/r10.anchor: والقراء على إظهار القاف والكاف في قوله: خلقكم ومنهم من يدغم القاف في الكاف؛ لأنه من مخرجها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p491/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p491/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p491/r1.claim: People means the children of Adam; humanity descends from one root, Adam, their father.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p491/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p491/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p491/r2.claim: One parse coordinates created its spouse with an omitted verb: God began Adam's creation from clay and created Eve from one of his ribs.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p491/r2.anchor: فيه وجهان أحدهما أن يعطف على محذوف كأنه قيل من نفس واحدة أنشأها أو ابتدأها وخلق منها زوجها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p491/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p491/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p491/r3.claim: On that parse, God made humanity branch from Adam, created Eve from clay from one of his ribs, and dispersed humankind from the pair.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p491/r3.anchor: والمعنى شعبكم من نفس واحدة هذه صفتها وهي أنه أنشأها من تراب وخلق زوجها حواء من ضلع من أضلاعها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p491/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p491/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p491/r4.claim: An alternative parse coordinates created her spouse with created you, addressing the people to whom the Prophet was sent: they descend from Adam, their mother Eve was made from him, and humanity spread from both.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p491/r4.anchor: والثاني أن يعطف على خلقكم ويكون الخطاب فى ﴿ يا أيها الناس ﴾ للذين بعث اليهم رسول الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p491#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p491#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p491#2/r1.claim: The many men and women are other human communities, too numerous to count.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p491#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p491#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p491#2/r2.claim: The creation account warrants piety because it displays immense power: one able to create this can punish sinners, so people should fear His punishment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p491#2/r2.anchor: لأن ذلك مما يدل على القدرة العظيمة ومن قدر على نحوه كان قادرا على كل شيء ومن المقدورات عقاب العصاة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p491#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p491#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p491#2/r3.claim: Creation also demonstrates abundant blessing, so people owe God piety rather than ingratitude and neglect of their duty to thank Him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p491#2/r3.anchor: ولأنه يدل على النعمة السابغة عليهم فحقهم أن يتقوه في كفرانها والتفريط فيما يلزمهم من القيام بشكرها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p491#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p491#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p491#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, piety here means preserving mutual rights and not cutting obligatory ties, since God joined people as branches of one root; this fits the sura's themes.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p491#2/r4.anchor: أو أراد بالتقوى تقوى خاصة وهي أن يتقوه فيما يتصل بحفظ الحقوق بينهم فلا يقطعوا ما يجب عليهم وصله
