SAMIN-DURR:4:1#3/r5.claim: Hamza reads والأرحام in the genitive; one analysis coordinates it with the genitive pronoun in به without repeating the preposition, a construction Basrans reject and previously debated with 2:217.
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#3/r5.anchor: وقرأ حمزة " والأرحام " بالجر، وفيها قولان، أحدهما: أنه عطف على الضمير المجرور في " به " من غير إعادة الجار

SAMIN-DURR:4:1#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#3/r6.speaker: الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#3/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj and others criticized Hamza's reading of the genitive coordination.
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#3/r6.anchor: وقد طعن جماعة على هذه القراءة كالزجاج وغيره

SAMIN-DURR:4:1#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#3/r7.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#3/r7.claim: Al-Farra, despite allowing such coordination, calls it ugly and reports Ibrahim's comparison: أسألك بالله والرحم, since Arabs do not coordinate onto a genitive represented by a pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#3/r7.anchor: حتى يحكى عن الفراء الذي مذهبه جواز ذلك أنه قال: " حدثني شريك بن عبد الله عن الأعمش عن إبراهيم

SAMIN-DURR:4:1#3/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#3/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#3/r8.claim: A second genitive analysis treats the و as an oath particle and the kinship term as the object of oath, answered by إن الله كان عليكم رقيبا.
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#3/r8.anchor: والثاني: أنه ليس معطوفا على الضمير المجرور بل الواو للقسم وهو خفض بحرف القسم مقسم به، وجواب القسم: " إن الله كان عليكم رقيبا "

SAMIN-DURR:4:1#3/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#3/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#3/r9.claim: The oath analysis is weak because the accusative reading and the reading with an explicit preposition point elsewhere, and reports prohibit swearing by anything besides God.
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#3/r9.anchor: وضعف هذا بوجهين، أحدهما: أن قراءتي النصب وإظهار حرف الجر في " بالأرحام " يمنعان من ذلك، والأصل توافق القراءات. والثاني: أنه نهي أن يحلف بغير الله تعالى والأحاديث مصرحة بذلك

SAMIN-DURR:4:1#3/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#3/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#3/r10.claim: Some supply an omitted رب, reading رب الأرحام; Abu al-Baqa says the preceding mention of God already supplies it.
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#3/r10.anchor: وقدر بعضهم مضافا فرارا من ذلك فقال: " تقديره: ورب الأرحام: قال أبو البقاء: وهذا قد أغنى عنه ما قبله "

SAMIN-DURR:4:1#3/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#3/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#3/r11.claim: The author answers that God may swear by whatever He chooses, including created things such as the sun, star, and night, although people are forbidden to do so; semantically the verse is not an oath.
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#3/r11.anchor: إن لله تعالى أن يقسم بما شاء كما أقسم بمخلوقاته كالشمس والنجم والليل، وإن كنا نحن منهيين عن ذلك

SAMIN-DURR:4:1#3/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#3/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#3/r12.claim: Because the intended meaning is not an oath, the author prefers coordination with the pronoun and disregards criticism of Hamza's reading, whose high standing precludes transmitting a weak reading.
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#3/r12.anchor: إلا أن المقصود من حيث المعنى ليس على القسم، فالأولى حمل هذه القراءة على العطف على الضمير، ولا التفات إلى طعن من طعن فيها

SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r1.claim: In Abdullah's nominative reading, Ibn Atiyya makes والأرحام a subject with the omitted predicate أهل أن توصل, worthy of being joined.
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r1.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله أيضا: " والأرحام " رفعا وهو على الابتداء، والخبر محذوف فقدره ابن عطية: " أهل أن توصل "

SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari supplies the predicate مما يتقى or مما يتساءل به; the author prefers this because it fits both wording and meaning, unlike Ibn Atiyya's semantic-only fit.
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r2.anchor: وقدره الزمخشري: و " الأرحام مما يتقى، أو: مما يتساءل به " ، وهذا أحسن للدلالة اللفظية والمعنوية

SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqa supplies محترمة as the predicate: kinship ties are sacrosanct and their respect is obligatory.
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r3.anchor: وقدره أبو البقاء: " والأرحام محترمة " أي: واجب حرمتها

SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r4.claim: The statement that God is ever watchful over people functions as the reason for the command.
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r4.anchor: وقوله: { إن الله كان عليكم رقيبا } جار مجرى التعليل. والرقيب: فعيل للمبالغة

SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r5.claim: Raqīb is an intensive adjective from raqaba and related forms, meaning God's vigilant preservation or guardianship.
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r5.anchor: والرقيب: فعيل للمبالغة من رقب يرقب رقبا ورقوبا ورقبانا

SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r6.claim: An anonymous poem uses الرقباء for watchmen, supporting the vigilant sense of raqīb.

SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r7.claim: Raqīb also names a kind of snake.

SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r8.claim: Raqīb also names the third arrow in the game of maysir.
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r8.anchor: والرقيب: السهم الثالث من سهام الميسر

SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:1#4/r9.claim: The verbal noun irtiqāb means waiting or expectation.

STUDYQURAN:4:1/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r1.claim: The single-soul creation is also cited at 6:98, 7:189, 31:28, and 39:6; creation of its mate is also cited at 7:189 and 39:6.
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r1.anchor: That God created human beings from a single soul is also mentioned in 6:98; 7:189; 31:28; 39:6

STUDYQURAN:4:1/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r2.claim: Other verses present making human mates as a divine gift for which humanity should be grateful and stand in awe.
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r2.anchor: Elsewhere, God’s having made for human beings “mates from among themselves” or “in pairs” is considered a Divine gift

STUDYQURAN:4:1/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r3.claim: The verse moves from singularity, reflecting God's oneness, to duality and then the multiplicity of humanity.
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r3.anchor: The present verse indicates a progression in human creation from singularity

STUDYQURAN:4:1/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r4.speaker: most commentators
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r4.claim: The single soul is widely identified as Adam and its mate as Eve (Ḥawwāʾ).
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r4.anchor: The single soul is widely understood to refer to Adam, and its mate to Eve (Ḥawwāʾ).

STUDYQURAN:4:1/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r5.speaker: most commentators
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r5.claim: Although nafs is grammatically feminine and zawj masculine, this grammatical mismatch does not trouble the Adam-and-Eve identification for most commentators.
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r5.anchor: does not necessarily make the correlation to Adam and Eve, respectively, problematic for most commentators

STUDYQURAN:4:1/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r6.claim: The interwoven masculine and feminine references suggest reciprocity between the sexes in human relations and marriage, also implied at 2:187 and 30:21.
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r6.anchor: The interweaving of masculine and feminine references suggests a reciprocity of the masculine and feminine in human relations and marriage

STUDYQURAN:4:1/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r7.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r7.claim: Commentators typically connect the verse with Eve's creation from Adam's rib as recounted in Genesis 2:21–23.
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r7.anchor: Commentators typically understand this verse as a reference to the story of Eve’s creation from Adam’s rib as found in Genesis 2:21–23

STUDYQURAN:4:1/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r8.speaker: some modern commentators
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r8.claim: Some modern commentators are skeptical of the rib association because it relies too heavily on Biblical tradition.
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r8.anchor: although some modern commentators are skeptical of this association, feeling it relies too heavily on the Biblical tradition.

STUDYQURAN:4:1/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r9.claim: Canonical hadith references Eve's creation from Adam's rib, but the Quran never explicitly recounts Eve's creation.
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r9.anchor: The story of Eve’s creation from Adam’s rib is referenced in the canonical Ḥadīth, but the Quran nowhere explicitly recounts Eve’s creation.

STUDYQURAN:4:1/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r10.claim: Minhā may mean Eve was made of the same nature as Adam; min anfus can mean of the same type or character, as at 3:164, 9:128, and 16:72.
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r10.anchor: the mate (Eve) was created of the same nature as the original

STUDYQURAN:4:1/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r11.speaker: Muḥammad al-Bāqir
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r11.claim: The fifth Shiite Imam reportedly said Eve was created from the same superior clay as Adam.
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r11.anchor: The fifth Shiite Imam, Muhammad al-Bāqir (d. ca. 114/732), reportedly said that Eve was created from the same superior clay as Adam

STUDYQURAN:4:1/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r12.claim: Common parentage is meant to encourage love among all people and discourage boasting about ancestry.
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r12.anchor: The statement regarding humanity’s common origin from a single soul and its mate could also be meant to engender brotherly and sisterly love between all human beings

STUDYQURAN:4:1/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r13.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r13.claim: The wording about invoking God and family relations may allude to the pre-Islamic Arab practice of swearing by both.
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r13.anchor: Reverence God, through Whom you demand your rights of one another, and family relations may be related to the pre-Islamic Arab practice of swearing upon “God and family relations.”

STUDYQURAN:4:1/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r14.speaker: most commentators
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r14.claim: Most favor reading the passage as commanding obedience to God and good relations with one's family.
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r14.anchor: However, most favor the view that this passage instructs men to reverence God through obedience to His commands and to reverence family relations by maintaining good relations with family members.

STUDYQURAN:4:1/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r15.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r15.claim: Arḥām means family relations; its singular raḥim primarily means womb and shares a root with mercy and the Divine Name al-Raḥmān.
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r15.anchor: Family relations translates arḥām; the singular is raḥim, the primary meaning of which is “womb,” derived from the same root as raḥmah

STUDYQURAN:4:1/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r16.speaker: a ḥadīth
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r16.claim: A hadith says the Compassionate created the womb, maintaining its ties earns God's ties, and severing them brings God's severance.

STUDYQURAN:4:1/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r17.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r17.claim: Other passages pair worship of God with commands to treat family well.
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r17.anchor: Elsewhere, the imperative to worship God is paired with commands to be good to family

STUDYQURAN:4:1/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r18.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r18.claim: The verse's first part establishes kinship among all humanity and its latter part commands care for relatives, together making responsibility to all people a divine imperative.
STUDYQURAN:4:1/r18.anchor: The first part of this verse indicates the kinship of all human beings, as they are created from the same soul and mate, while the latter part commands reverence for one’s relatives.

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r48.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r48.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r48.claim: The Bible’s rib account appears in Hadith; many commentators read 4:1 as an oblique reference to Eve’s creation from Adam, understood here as primordial and androgynic humanity.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r48.anchor: The Biblical story of Eve’s creation from Adam’s rib (Genesis 2:21–22), however, is referenced in the Ḥadīth

TAB-FULL:v6p339#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p339#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p339#2/r1.claim: People must fear their Lord by obeying commands and avoiding prohibitions, lest a punishment beyond their power befall them.
TAB-FULL:v6p339#2/r1.anchor: الناس ربكم في أن تخالفوه فيما أمركم، وفيما نهاكم، فيحل بكم من عقوبته ما لا قبل لكم به

TAB-FULL:v6p339#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p339#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p339#2/r2.claim: Because all people descend from one man and one woman, they are kin and owe one another the care and rights of siblings; this should produce justice, compassion, and protection of the weak.
TAB-FULL:v6p339#2/r2.anchor: لاجتماعهم في النسب إلى أب واحد وأم واحدة، وأن الذي يلزمهم من رعاية بعضهم حق بعض

TAB-FULL:v6p339#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p339#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p339#2/r3.anchor: فقال: {الذي خلقكم من نفس واحدة} [النساء: 1] يعني من آدم

TAB-FULL:v6p339#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p339#2/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v6p339#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddī says that the one soul from which people were created is Adam.
TAB-FULL:v6p339#2/r4.anchor: عن السدي: أما {خلقكم من نفس واحدة} [النساء: 1] «فمن آدم صلى الله عليه وسلم»

TAB-FULL:v6p339#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p339#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v6p339#2/r5.claim: Qatāda identifies the one soul as Adam.
TAB-FULL:v6p339#2/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {يا أيها الناس اتقوا ربكم الذي خلقكم من نفس واحدة} [النساء: 1] يعني: «آدم صلى الله عليه وسلم»

TAB-FULL:v6p339#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p339#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v6p339#2/r6.claim: Mujāhid identifies the one soul as Adam.
TAB-FULL:v6p339#2/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد: {خلقكم من نفس واحدة} [النساء: 1] قال: «آدم»

TAB-FULL:v6p339#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p339#2/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p339#2/r7.claim: The feminine form nafs refers to a male; a poet's use of feminine khalīfah for a male illustrates this semantic and grammatical distinction.
TAB-FULL:v6p339#2/r7.anchor: أبوك خليفة ولدته أخرى … وأنت خليفة ذاك الكمال

TAB-FULL:v6p339#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p339#2/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p339#2/r8.claim: The noun is feminine in form, while its meaning is one man; using masculine wāḥid to agree with the meaning would also be correct.
TAB-FULL:v6p339#2/r8.anchor: {من نفس واحدة} [النساء: 1] لتأنيث النفس والمعنى، من رجل واحد ولو قيل: من نفس واحد، وأخرج اللفظ على التذكير للمعنى كان صوابا

TAB-FULL:v6p342/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p342/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v6p342/r1.claim: Mujāhid says Eve was made from Adam's short rib while he slept; on waking he called her “woman” in Nabataean.
TAB-FULL:v6p342/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {وخلق منها زوجها} [النساء: 1] قال: " حواء من قصيرى آدم وهو نائم، فاستيقظ فقال: «أثا» بالنبطية امرأة "

TAB-FULL:v6p342/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p342/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v6p342/r2.claim: Qatāda says Eve was created from one of Adam's ribs.
TAB-FULL:v6p342/r2.anchor: عن قتادة: {وخلق منها زوجها} [النساء: 1] يعني حواء خلقت من آدم من ضلع من أضلاعه

TAB-FULL:v6p342/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p342/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v6p342/r3.claim: Al-Suddī recounts that Adam felt alone in Paradise, slept, and awoke to a woman created from his rib so that he could find comfort with her.
TAB-FULL:v6p342/r3.anchor: عن السدي، قال: " أسكن آدم الجنة، فكان يمشي فيها وحشا ليس له زوج يسكن إليها؛ فنام نومة

TAB-FULL:v6p342/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p342/r4.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v6p342/r4.claim: Ibn Isḥāq, relaying the People of the Book and Ibn ʿAbbās, says Eve was shaped as a woman from Adam's left rib while he slept; Adam later recognized her as his flesh, blood, and wife.
TAB-FULL:v6p342/r4.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال: " ألقي على آدم صلى الله عليه وسلم السنة فيما بلغنا عن أهل الكتاب من أهل التوراة وغيرهم من أهل العلم، عن عبد الله بن العباس وغيره

TAB-FULL:v6p342/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p342/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p342/r5.claim: God spread many men and women from Adam and Eve.
TAB-FULL:v6p342/r5.anchor: فإنه يعني ونشر منهما يعني من آدم وحواء {رجالا كثيرا ونساء} [النساء: 1] قد رآهم

TAB-FULL:v6p342/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p342/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p342/r6.claim: The spreading is likened to scattered moths; the verb baththa and its variant both mean to scatter creation.
TAB-FULL:v6p342/r6.anchor: كما قال جل ثناؤه: {كالفراش المبثوث} [القارعة: 4] يقال منه: بث الله الخلق وأبثهم

TAB-FULL:v6p342#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p342#2/r1.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v6p342#2/r1.anchor: عن السدي: {وبث منهما رجالا كثيرا ونساء} [النساء: 1] " وبث: خلق "

TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r1.speaker: قراء أهل المدينة والبصرة
TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r1.claim: Most Medinan and Basran readers pronounce tasaʾalūn with a doubled sīn, reflecting assimilation of one of the two tāʾs.
TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r1.anchor: فقرأه عامة قراء أهل المدينة والبصرة

TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r2.speaker: بعض قراء الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r2.claim: Some Kufan readers use the lighter form on the tafāʿalūn pattern.
TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r2.anchor: وقرأه بعض قراء الكوفة: {تساءلون} [النساء: 1] بالتخفيف على مثال تفاعلون

TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r3.claim: Both readings are established, eloquent dialects and equally correct because their meaning does not differ.
TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r3.anchor: وهما قراءتان معروفتان، ولغتان فصيحتان، أعني التخفيف والتشديد في قوله: {تساءلون به} [النساء: 1]

TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r4.claim: The phrase means people invoke God when asking one another, saying “I ask you by God,” “I adjure you by God,” or similar expressions.
TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r4.anchor: وأما تأويله: {واتقوا الله} [البقرة: 189] أيها الناس، الذي إذا سأل بعضكم بعضا سأل به، فقال السائل للمسئول: أسألك بالله، وأنشدك بالله

TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r5.claim: As people treat a broken promise made in God's name as grave, they should honor God through obedience and avoiding what He forbids.
TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r5.anchor: فكما تعظمون أيها الناس ربكم بألسنتكم، حتى تروا أن من أعطاكم عهده فأخفركموه، فقد أتى عظيما

TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r6.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk interprets invoking God as making contracts and covenants by Him.
TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r6.anchor: عن الضحاك، في قوله: {واتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به} [النساء: 1] قال: يقول: «اتقوا الله الذي تعاقدون وتعاهدون به»

TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r7.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r7.claim: Al-Rabīʿ likewise explains the phrase as making contracts and covenants by God.
TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r7.anchor: عن الربيع: {واتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به} [النساء: 1] يقول: «اتقوا الله الذي به تعاقدون وتعاهدون»

TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the phrase as people showing mutual affection through God.
TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r8.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: قال ابن عباس: {تساءلون به} [النساء: 1] قال: «تعاطفون به»

TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r9.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r9.claim: One interpretation takes wa-l-arḥām as people asking one another by God and by kinship.
TAB-FULL:v6p342#3/r9.anchor: فقال بعضهم: معناه: واتقوا الله الذي إذا سألتم بينكم، قال السائل للمسئول: أسألك به وبالرحم

TAB-FULL:v6p346/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p346/r1.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v6p346/r1.claim: Ibrāhīm interprets the phrase as asking someone by God and by kinship.
TAB-FULL:v6p346/r1.anchor: عن إبراهيم، قال: " هو كقول الرجل: أسألك بالله، أسألك بالرحم "

TAB-FULL:v6p346/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p346/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v6p346/r2.claim: Mujāhid says people ask by God and by kinship.
TAB-FULL:v6p346/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد: {واتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به والأرحام} [النساء: 1] قال: يقول: «أسألك بالله وبالرحم»

TAB-FULL:v6p346/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p346/r3.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v6p346/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan paraphrases the expression as “I adjure you by God and kinship.”
TAB-FULL:v6p346/r3.anchor: عن الحسن، قال: " هو قول الرجل: أنشدك بالله والرحم "

TAB-FULL:v6p346/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p346/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p346/r4.claim: On this interpretation, genitive al-arḥām coordinates with the attached pronoun in bihi; al-Ṭabarī says overt nouns should not coordinate with a genitive attached pronoun in ordinary Arabic prose, except poetic necessity.
TAB-FULL:v6p346/r4.anchor: فعطف بظاهر على مكني مخفوض، وذلك غير فصيح من الكلام عند العرب؛ لأنها لا تنسق بظاهر على مكني في الخفض إلا في ضرورة شعر

TAB-FULL:v6p345/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p345/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p345/r1.claim: A cited poetic line coordinates the overt noun al-kaʿb with the hidden dual pronoun in baynahā, an exception to the prose norm.
TAB-FULL:v6p345/r1.anchor: نعلق في مثل السواري سيوفنا … وما بينها والكعب غوط نفانف

TAB-FULL:v6p345/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p345/r2.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v6p345/r2.claim: Another interpretation commands people to fear their kinship ties by not severing them.
TAB-FULL:v6p345/r2.anchor: {واتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به} [النساء: 1] واتقوا الأرحام أن تقطعوها

TAB-FULL:v6p345/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p345/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v6p345/r3.claim: Al-Suddī explains the command as fearing God and not severing kinship ties.
TAB-FULL:v6p345/r3.anchor: عن السدي، في قوله: {واتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به والأرحام} [النساء: 1] يقول: «اتقوا الله، واتقوا الأرحام لا تقطعوها»

TAB-FULL:v6p345/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p345/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v6p345/r4.claim: Qatāda reports that the Prophet urged fearing God and maintaining kinship, which preserves good in this world and is better in the next.
TAB-FULL:v6p345/r4.anchor: عن قتادة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «اتقوا الله وصلوا الأرحام»

TAB-FULL:v6p345/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p345/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v6p345/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says to fear God in matters of kinship and maintain those ties.
TAB-FULL:v6p345/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قول الله: {واتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به والأرحام} [النساء: 1] يقول: «اتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به، واتقوا الله في الأرحام فصلوها»

TAB-FULL:v6p345/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p345/r6.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v6p345/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan says to fear God and fear Him regarding kinship ties.
TAB-FULL:v6p345/r6.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {واتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به والأرحام} [النساء: 1] قال: «اتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به، واتقوه في الأرحام»

TAB-FULL:v6p345/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p345/r7.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v6p345/r7.claim: ʿIkrimah explains the command as not severing kinship ties.
TAB-FULL:v6p345/r7.anchor: عن عكرمة، في قول الله: {الذي تساءلون به والأرحام} [النساء: 1] قال: «اتقوا الأرحام أن تقطعوها»

TAB-FULL:v6p345/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p345/r8.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v6p345/r8.claim: In a separate report, al-Ḥasan understands the wording as someone adjuring another by God and kinship.
TAB-FULL:v6p345/r8.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {واتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به والأرحام} [النساء: 1] قال: " هو قول الرجل: أنشدك بالله والرحم "

TAB-FULL:v6p350/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p350/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v6p350/r1.claim: Mujāhid explains wa-l-arḥām as a command not to sever kinship ties.
TAB-FULL:v6p350/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد: {الذي تساءلون به والأرحام} [النساء: 1] قال: «اتقوا الأرحام أن تقطعوها»

TAB-FULL:v6p350/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p350/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v6p350/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says to fear God regarding kinship and maintain those ties.
TAB-FULL:v6p350/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك، في قوله: {الذي تساءلون به والأرحام} [النساء: 1] قال: يقول: «اتقوا الله في الأرحام فصلوها»

TAB-FULL:v6p350/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p350/r3.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v6p350/r3.claim: Al-Rabīʿ says to fear God regarding kinship and maintain those ties.
TAB-FULL:v6p350/r3.anchor: عن الربيع: {واتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به والأرحام} [النساء: 1] قال: يقول: «واتقوا الله في الأرحام فصلوها»

TAB-FULL:v6p350/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p350/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v6p350/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reportedly recited al-arḥām and glossed it as a command not to sever kinship; another report from him says simply to fear the kinship ties.
TAB-FULL:v6p350/r4.anchor: أن ابن عباس، كان يقرأ: {والأرحام} [النساء: 1] يقول: «اتقوا الله لا تقطعوها»

TAB-FULL:v6p350/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p350/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v6p350/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says not to sever kinship ties and cites the description of those who join what God commanded to be joined.
TAB-FULL:v6p350/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {واتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به} [النساء: 1] «واتقوا الأرحام أن تقطعوها» وقرأ: {والذين يصلون ما أمر الله به أن يوصل} [الرعد: 21]

TAB-FULL:v6p350/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p350/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p350/r6.claim: For the “do not sever kinship” interpretation, al-Ṭabarī prefers the accusative reading wa-l-arḥāma, coordinated with the name of God; this is the only reading he permits, since genitive coordination on an attached pronoun is ungrammatical outside poetry.
TAB-FULL:v6p350/r6.anchor: القراءة التي لا نستجيز للقارئ أن يقرأ غيرها في ذلك النصب

TAB-FULL:v6p350#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p350#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p350#2/r1.claim: Arabic shifts to second-person plural when the report includes both those being addressed and other people who are absent.
TAB-FULL:v6p350#2/r1.anchor: الكلام على الخطاب، فتقول إذا خاطبت رجلا واحدا أو جماعة فعلت هي وآخرون غيب معهم فعلا: فعلتم كذا، وصنعتم كذا

TAB-FULL:v6p350#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p350#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p350#2/r2.claim: Raqīban means a guardian who records and monitors people's deeds, including how they honor, maintain, neglect, or sever kinship ties.
TAB-FULL:v6p350#2/r2.anchor: ويعني بقوله: {رقيبا} [النساء: 1] حفيظا، محصيا عليكم أعمالكم، متفقدا رعايتكم حرمة أرحامكم وصلتكم إياها، وقطعكموها وتضييعكم حرمتها

TAB-FULL:v6p350#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p350#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v6p350#2/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد: {إن الله كان عليكم رقيبا} [النساء: 1] «حفيظا»

TAB-FULL:v6p350#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p350#2/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v6p350#2/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says God watches people's deeds, knows them, and recognizes them.
TAB-FULL:v6p350#2/r4.anchor: سمعت ابن زيد، في قوله: {إن الله كان عليكم رقيبا} [النساء: 1] «على أعمالكم، يعلمها ويعرفها»

TAB-FULL:v6p350#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p350#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p350#2/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī cites a verse by Abū Duwād al-Iyādī as lexical evidence for raqīb as a watchman.
TAB-FULL:v6p350#2/r5.anchor: ومنه قول أبي دواد الإيادي: [البحر الكامل]

TABATABAI:4:1/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1/r1.claim: The sūrah's main concerns are marriage and inheritance laws, with additional rulings on prayer, jihad, testimony, trade, and the People of the Book.
TABATABAI:4:1/r1.anchor: غرض السورة كما يلوح إليه هذا الصدر بيان أحكام الزواج كعدد الزوجات ومحرمات النكاح وغير ذلك وأحكام المواريث

TABATABAI:4:1/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1/r2.claim: Its contents show it is Medinan and apparently revealed in installments, although most verses remain connected to one another.
TABATABAI:4:1/r2.anchor: وظاهرها أنها نزلت نجوما لا دفعة واحدة وإن كانت أغلب آياتها غير فاقدة للارتباط فيما بينها

TABATABAI:4:1/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1/r3.claim: This verse and those following about orphans and women introduce inheritance and forbidden-marriage rules; the number of wives in 4:3 enters incidentally through this preliminary discussion.
TABATABAI:4:1/r3.anchor: وأما هذه الآية في نفسها فهي وعدة من الآيات التالية لها المتعرضة لحال اليتامى والنساء كالتوطئة لما سيبين من أمر المواريث

TABATABAI:4:1/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1/r4.claim: The call to all people to fear their Lord rests on shared human nature: men must not oppress women, nor adults wrong children, in the society and laws that secure collective and individual well-being.
TABATABAI:4:1/r4.anchor: وهم ناس متحدون في الحقيقة الإنسانية من غير اختلاف فيها بين الرجل منهم والمرأة والصغير والكبير والعاجز والقوي

TABATABAI:4:1/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1/r5.claim: Addressing all people rather than only believers, and calling God their Lord, fits the universal human scope and His role in governing and perfecting them.
TABATABAI:4:1/r5.anchor: ومن هناك تظهر نكتة توجيه الخطاب إلى الناس دون المؤمنين خاصة وكذا تعليق التقوى بربهم

TABATABAI:4:1/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1/r6.claim: Nafs lexically means a thing itself; the human self comprises spirit and body in this life, and only spirit in the barzakh, as discussed earlier.
TABATABAI:4:1/r6.anchor: فالنفس على ما يستفاد من اللغة عين الشيء يقال جاءني فلان نفسه وعينه

TABATABAI:4:1#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#2/r1.claim: The single soul and its spouse are Adam and his wife, the parents of all people alive today, as the Qur'an's presentation indicates.
TABATABAI:4:1#2/r1.anchor: وظاهر السياق أن المراد بالنفس الواحدة آدم عليه السلام ومن زوجها زوجته وهما أبوا هذا النسل الموجود

TABATABAI:4:1#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#2/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:4:1#2/r2.claim: Some exegetes take the single soul and spouse generically as every human's male and female parents, making the verse equivalent to the statement that all descend from human parents.
TABATABAI:4:1#2/r2.anchor: وأما ما احتمله بعض المفسرين أن المراد بالنفس الواحدة وزوجها في الآية مطلق الذكور والإناث من الإنسان

TABATABAI:4:1#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#2/r3.claim: The generic-parent reading confuses the aims of 4:1 and 49:13: 49:13 denies status distinctions among people, while 4:1 says the many men and women branch from one original source.
TABATABAI:4:1#2/r3.anchor: ففيه فساد ظاهر وقد فاته أن بين الآيتين أعني آية النساء وآية الحجرات فرقا بينا

TABATABAI:4:1#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#2/r4.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:4:1#2/r4.claim: Al-Rāghib says zawj can name either member of an animal male-female pair, a pair generally, and anything joined to another as its likeness or opposite; zawja is poor usage.
TABATABAI:4:1#2/r4.anchor: قال الراغب يقال لكل واحد من القرينين من الذكر والأنثى في الحيوانات المتزاوجة زوج

TABATABAI:4:1#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#2/r5.claim: The phrase about creating the spouse from the soul indicates a corresponding mate of the same kind; min here marks origination, not creation from Adam's rib.
TABATABAI:4:1#2/r5.anchor: وظاهر الجملة أعني قوله { وخلق منها زوجها } أنها بيان لكونه زوجها من نوعها بالتماثل

TABATABAI:4:1#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r1.claim: Verses about spouses made from humans and animals support same-kind pairs; the claim that Eve was made from Adam's rib lacks evidence in this verse, despite some tafsir and reports.
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r1.anchor: أن الله خلق زوجة آدم من ضلع من أضلاعه مما لا دليل عليه من الآية

TABATABAI:4:1#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r2.claim: Bathth means dispersal by stirring or the like, as in the description of dust blown apart.
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r2.anchor: البث هو التفريق بالإثارة ونحوها قال تعالى فكانت هباء منبثا

TABATABAI:4:1#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r3.claim: The Qur'anic phrase for grief as bathth uses the word for something dispersed and spread, hence its meaning here is grief and sorrow.
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r3.anchor: قال إنما أشكوا بثي وحزني إلى الله

TABATABAI:4:1#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r4.claim: The verse's wording indicates that all existing human descendants trace back to Adam and his wife alone, without another source contributing.
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r4.anchor: وظاهر الآية أن النسل الموجود من الإنسان ينتهي إلى آدم وزوجته من غير أن يشاركهما فيه غيرهما

TABATABAI:4:1#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r5.claim: The many men and women means Adam and his wife's descendants, with or without intervening generations; the verse effectively addresses people as spread from the pair.
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r5.anchor: أفراد البشر من ذريتهما بلا واسطة أو مع واسطة فكأنه قيل وبثكم منهما

TABATABAI:4:1#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r6.claim: If Adam and his wife alone began the lineage, their immediate sons and daughters must have married one another.
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r6.anchor: أن الازدواج في الطبقة الأولى بعد آدم وزوجته أعني في أولادهما بلا واسطة إنما وقع بين الإخوة والأخوات

TABATABAI:4:1#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r7.claim: Sibling marriage in that first generation would be a changeable legislative ruling: God could allow it temporarily and prohibit it later.
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r7.anchor: فإنه حكم تشريعي راجع إلى الله سبحانه فله أن يبيحه يوما ويحرمه آخر

TABATABAI:4:1#3/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r8.claim: Mutual asking by God means one person asks another in God's name, which is an oath and shows that God is revered and loved among them.
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r8.anchor: المراد بالتساؤل سؤال بعض الناس بعضا بالله يقول أحدهم لصاحبه أسألك بالله أن تفعل كذا وكذا هو إقسام به تعالى

TABATABAI:4:1#3/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r9.claim: The apparent syntax joins al-arham to God's name, commanding people to revere and observe kinship ties.
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r9.anchor: وأما قوله { والأرحام } ، فظاهره أنه معطوف على لفظ الجلالة والمعنى واتقوا الأرحام

TABATABAI:4:1#3/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r10.claim: An alternative parses al-arham with the pronoun governed by bi; the genitive reading attributed to Hamza is cited in support, though grammarians criticize it.
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r10.anchor: وربما أيدته قراءة حمزة " والأرحام " بالجر عطفا على الضمير المتصل المجرور - وإن ضعفه النحاة -

TABATABAI:4:1#3/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r11.claim: The alternative either leaves the relative clause without its required pronoun or makes God and kinship equal in majesty, contrary to Qur'anic decorum.
TABATABAI:4:1#3/r11.anchor: فإن قوله " والأرحام " إن جعل صلة مستقلة للذي وكان تقدير الكلام واتقوا الله الذي تسألون بالأرحام كان خاليا من الضمير

TABATABAI:4:1#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#4/r1.claim: Tabatabai cites Qur'anic commands to fear a Day, the Fire, and a trial as examples of taqwa directed toward things other than God.
TABATABAI:4:1#4/r1.anchor: واتقوا يوما ترجعون فيه إلى الله

TABATABAI:4:1#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#4/r2.claim: The second clause narrows the opening command: first fear God as Lord and creator of humanity's shared nature, then fear Him in His majesty and preserve the kinship unity He created.
TABATABAI:4:1#4/r2.anchor: فهذا الشطر من الكلام بمنزلة التقييد بعد الإطلاق والتضييق بعد التوسعة بالنسبة إلى الشطر السابق عليه

TABATABAI:4:1#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#4/r3.claim: Repeating the command to fear God adds a special emphasis on the duty owed to kinship ties.
TABATABAI:4:1#4/r3.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر وجه تكرار الأمر بالتقوى وإعادته ثانيا في الجملة الثانية فإن الجملة الثانية في الحقيقة تكرار للجملة الأولى

TABATABAI:4:1#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#4/r4.claim: Rahim originally means a woman's womb; by a container-content relation it came to mean relatives who share descent from one womb.
TABATABAI:4:1#4/r4.anchor: والرحم في الأصل رحم المرأة وهي العضو الداخلي منها المعبأ لتربية النطفة وليدا ثم استعير للقرابة بعلاقة الظرف والمظروف

TABATABAI:4:1#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#4/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#4/r5.claim: The Qur'an treats kinship as a small community and a people as a larger one, each a real social entity with properties and effects grounded in existence.
TABATABAI:4:1#4/r5.anchor: وقد اعتنى القرآن بأمر المجتمع وعده حقيقة ذات خواص وآثار كما اعتنى بأمر الفرد من الإنسان وعده حقيقة ذات خواص وآثار

TABATABAI:4:1#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#5/r1.claim: Other verses show the Qur'an's concern for kinship rights, severing family ties, and the care owed to children who might be left vulnerable.
TABATABAI:4:1#5/r1.anchor: وأولوا الأرحام بعضهم أولى ببعض في كتاب الله الأنفال 75، وقال تعالى فهل عسيتم إن توليتم أن تفسدوا في الأرض وتقطعوا أرحامكم

TABATABAI:4:1#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#5/r2.claim: Raqib means guardian, and muraqaba means guarding; the word may derive from the neck, as a keeper watches over dependents or stretches out his neck to observe.
TABATABAI:4:1#5/r2.anchor: الرقيب الحفيظ والمراقبة المحافظة وكأنه مأخوذ من الرقبة بعناية

TABATABAI:4:1#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#5/r3.claim: Raqib is more than general preservation: it means watching the observed person's actions and stillness to correct or contain faults, with knowledge and attention.
TABATABAI:4:1#5/r3.anchor: وليس الرقوب مطلق الحفظ بل هو الحفظ على أعمال المرقوب من حركاته وسكناته لإصلاح موارد الخلل والفساد

TABATABAI:4:1#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#5/r4.claim: God is the watcher because He keeps account of servants' deeds in order to requite them, as other verses say He is their preserver and watches over them.
TABATABAI:4:1#5/r4.anchor: والله سبحانه رقيب لأنه يحفظ على العباد أعمالهم ليجزيهم بها

TABATABAI:4:1#5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#5/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#5/r5.claim: God's surveillance powerfully warns against violating humanity's shared unity; threats against oppression, corruption, and transgression serve the aim of protecting that unity from collapse.
TABATABAI:4:1#5/r5.anchor: وهو وقاية الوحدة الإنسانية من الفساد والسقوط

TABATABAI:4:1#6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#6/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#6/r1.claim: Jewish historical tradition places humanity's age near seven thousand years; a rough demographic model, even with extreme calamity losses, yields over 2.5 billion after seventy centuries, near the contemporary world estimate.
TABATABAI:4:1#6/r1.anchor: أن عمر هذا النوع لا يزيد على ما يقرب من سبعة آلاف سنة والاعتبار يساعده

TABATABAI:4:1#6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#6/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#6/r2.claim: Geologists estimate humanity is millions of years old and cite human fossils, bodies, and artifacts they date to more than half a million years ago.
TABATABAI:4:1#6/r2.anchor: لكن علماء الجيولوجي علم طبقات الأرض ذكروا أن عمر هذا النوع يزيد على مليونات من السنين وقد وجدوا من الفسيلات الإنسانية

TABATABAI:4:1#6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#6/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#6/r3.claim: Such evidence does not prove uninterrupted descent between ancient peoples and the present; humanity could have appeared, grown, disappeared, and arisen again in multiple cycles.
TABATABAI:4:1#6/r3.anchor: غير أنه لا دليل معهم يقنع الإنسان ويرضي النفس باتصال النسل بين هذه الأعقاب الخالية والأمم الماضية من غير انقطاع

TABATABAI:4:1#6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#6/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#6/r4.claim: The Qur'an does not explicitly say whether humanity appeared only in the present cycle or passed through multiple cycles.
TABATABAI:4:1#6/r4.anchor: وأما القرآن الكريم فإنه لم يتعرض تصريحا لبيان أن ظهور هذا النوع هل ينحصر في هذه الدورة التي نحن فيها أو أن له أدوارا متعددة

TABATABAI:4:1#6/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#6/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#6/r5.claim: A prior human cycle may perhaps be inferred from a Qur'anic statement, though the Qur'an does not explicitly settle the matter.
TABATABAI:4:1#6/r5.anchor: وإن كان ربما يستشم من قوله تعالى

TABATABAI:4:1#6/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#6/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#6/r6.claim: The demographic estimate assumes catastrophic mortality as high as 999 deaths per 1,000 in each century, leaving one survivor per thousand.
TABATABAI:4:1#6/r6.anchor: وبالغنا في ذلك حتى أخذنا الفناء يعم الأفراد بنسبة تسعمائة وتسعة وتسعين إلى الألف

TABATABAI:4:1#7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#7/r1.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:4:1#7/r1.claim: Some argue that differences in skin color and blood require separate ancestry for each race, with at least four original couples for four color groups.
TABATABAI:4:1#7/r1.anchor: ربما قيل إن اختلاف الألوان في أفراد الإنسان وعمدتها البياض كلون أهل النقاط المعتدلة من آسيا واوروبا

TABATABAI:4:1#7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#7/r2.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:4:1#7/r2.claim: Another argument says the people of the Americas, isolated from the Eastern Hemisphere, could not plausibly descend from the same original parents.
TABATABAI:4:1#7/r2.anchor: وربما يستدل عليه بأن قارة أمريكا انكشفت ولها أهل وهم منقطعون عن الإنسان القاطن في نصف الكرة الشرقي

TABATABAI:4:1#7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#7/r3.claim: The color argument is weak because modern natural science assumes species can evolve, so differences in blood and color could arise through development within a species; scientists also give the differences little weight.
TABATABAI:4:1#7/r3.anchor: أما مسألة اختلاف الدماء باختلاف الألوان فلأن الأبحاث الطبيعية اليوم مبنية على فرضية التطور في الأنواع

TABATABAI:4:1#7/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#7/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#7/r4.claim: The Americas argument relies only on improbability: human history may extend millions of years, and geological changes could have separated continents before recorded history.
TABATABAI:4:1#7/r4.anchor: وما هو أعظم من ذلك كتبدل القطبين والمنطقة على ما يشرحه علوم طبقات الأرض والهيئة والجغرافيا فلا يبقى لهذا المستدل إلا الاستبعاد فقط

TABATABAI:4:1#7/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#7/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#7/r5.claim: The Qur'an's near-explicit meaning is that present humanity ultimately descends from one male and one female, the parents of everyone.
TABATABAI:4:1#7/r5.anchor: وأما القرآن فظاهره القريب من النص أن هذا النسل الحاضر المشهود من الإنسان ينتهي بالارتقاء إلى ذكر وأنثى هما الأب والأم لجميع الأفراد

TABATABAI:4:1#7/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#7/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#7/r6.claim: The Qur'an names the father Adam but does not name his wife; narrations call her Eve, as does the extant Torah.
TABATABAI:4:1#7/r6.anchor: أما الأب فقد سماه الله تعالى في كتابه بآدم وأما زوجته فلم يسمها في كتابه ولكن الروايات تسميها حواء كما في التوراة الموجودة

TABATABAI:4:1#8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#8/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#8/r1.claim: The cited creation verses show that ordinary human lineage continues through semen, while Adam was initially created from clay; thus the present line plainly ends in Adam and his wife, though reinterpretation remains possible.
TABATABAI:4:1#8/r1.anchor: فإن الآيات - كما ترى - تشهد بأن سنة الله في بقاء هذا النسل أن يتسبب إليه بالنطفة لكنه أظهره حينما أظهره بخلقه من تراب

TABATABAI:4:1#8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#8/r2.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:4:1#8/r2.claim: Some say Adam in creation and prostration verses means humanity as a type, rather than a particular individual, because humanity's creation traces to earth and reproduces.
TABATABAI:4:1#8/r2.anchor: وربما قيل إن المراد بآدم في آيات الخلقة والسجدة آدم النوعي دون الشخصي كأن مطلق الإنسان من حيث انتهاء خلقه إلى الأرض

TABATABAI:4:1#8/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#8/r3.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:4:1#8/r3.claim: Supporters of type-Adam read the plural creation and formation in 7:11 as suggesting the angels prostrated to a humanity prepared through creation and formation.
TABATABAI:4:1#8/r3.anchor: فإنه لا يخلو عن إشعار بأن الملائكة إنما أمروا بالسجدة لمن هيأه الله لها بالخلق والتصوير

TABATABAI:4:1#8/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#8/r4.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:4:1#8/r4.claim: They also point to the creation account's shift from a singular created figure to plural descendants as evidence that Adam can signify the human type.
TABATABAI:4:1#8/r4.anchor: حيث أبدل ما ذكره مفردا أولا من الجمع ثانيا

TABATABAI:4:1#9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#9/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#9/r1.claim: The command to Adam's children says Satan expelled their two parents from the Garden, making Adam a particular person rather than a human type.
TABATABAI:4:1#9/r1.anchor: فظهور الآية في شخصية آدم مما لا ينبغي أن يرتاب فيه

TABATABAI:4:1#9/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#9/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#9/r2.claim: The reference to Adam's offspring and the verse under discussion likewise support the personal Adam identified as the ancestor of humanity.
TABATABAI:4:1#9/r2.anchor: وكذا قوله تعالى وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس قال أأسجد لمن خلقت طينا

TABATABAI:4:1#9/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#9/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#9/r3.claim: The Qur'an resists calling humanity Adam in one sense and Adam's children in another, or assigning clay creation to one sense and semen descent to another.
TABATABAI:4:1#9/r3.anchor: فالآيات - كما ترى - تأبى أن يسمى الإنسان آدم باعتبار وابن آدم باعتبار آخر وكذا تأبى أن تنسب الخلقة إلى التراب باعتبار وإلى النطفة باعتبار آخر

TABATABAI:4:1#9/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#9/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#9/r4.claim: If Adam were not a literal first human, the argument that Jesus' creation is an exceptional break from ordinary custom would fail.
TABATABAI:4:1#9/r4.anchor: وإلا لم يستقم استدلال الآية على كون خلقة عيسى خلقة استثنائية ناقضة للعادة الجارية

TABATABAI:4:1#10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#10/r1.speaker: زين العرب
TABATABAI:4:1#10/r1.claim: Zayn al-Arab, a Sunni scholar, holds that believing more than one Adam was created amounts to unbelief.
TABATABAI:4:1#10/r1.anchor: قول بعضهم إن القول بخلق أزيد من آدم واحد كفر. ذهب إليه زين العرب من علماء أهل السنه

TABATABAI:4:1#10/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#10/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#10/r2.claim: The creation verses establish humans as a distinct kind ending in Adam and his wife, who were created without connection to a prior similar or related kind.
TABATABAI:4:1#10/r2.anchor: فالإنسانية تنتهي إليهما وهما لا يتصلان بآخر يماثلهما أو يجانسهما وإنما حدثا حدوثا

TABATABAI:4:1#10/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#10/r3.speaker: الباحثون عن طبيعة الإنسان
TABATABAI:4:1#10/r3.claim: Researchers commonly assume that an early human individual developed into a human, and more basically that humans are animals transformed into humans, though the specific first-human theory is disputed.
TABATABAI:4:1#10/r3.anchor: لكن أصل الفرضية وهي " أن الإنسان حيوان تحول إنسانا " مما تسلموه وبنوا عليه البحث عن طبيعة الإنسان

TABATABAI:4:1#10/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#10/r4.speaker: الباحثون عن طبيعة الإنسان
TABATABAI:4:1#10/r4.claim: Their proposed sequence runs from a cooling earth and water-based life through plants, aquatic animals, amphibious and land animals, and finally humans as earlier material forms develop.
TABATABAI:4:1#10/r4.anchor: ثم حدثت تراكيب مائية وأرضية فحدثت النباتات المائية ثم حدثت بتكامل النبات واشتمالها على جراثيم الحياة السمك وسائر الحيوان المائي

TABATABAI:4:1#10/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#10/r5.speaker: الباحثون عن طبيعة الإنسان
TABATABAI:4:1#10/r5.claim: They infer evolution from the ordered increase of complexity and from experiments showing limited development within particular cases.
TABATABAI:4:1#10/r5.anchor: كل ذلك لما يشاهد من الكمال المنظم في بنيها نظم المراتب الآخذة من النقص إلى الكمال ولما يعطيه التجريب في موارد جزئية التطور

TABATABAI:4:1#10/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#10/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#10/r6.claim: The hypothesis is an explanatory supposition without specific proof; experiments have never shown an individual of one species turning into another, such as a monkey into a human.
TABATABAI:4:1#10/r6.anchor: فإن التجارب لم يتناول فردا من أفراد هذه الأنواع تحول إلى فرد من نوع آخر كقردة إلى إنسان

TABATABAI:4:1#10/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#10/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#10/r7.claim: Because the proposed evolution lacks decisive evidence and experiments concern traits rather than species themselves, the Qur'anic view of humanity as a separate kind faces no scientific contradiction.
TABATABAI:4:1#10/r7.anchor: فالحقيقة التي يشير إليها القرآن الكريم من كون الإنسان نوعا مفصولا عن سائر الأنواع غير معارضة بشيء علمي

TABATABAI:4:1#10/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#10/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#10/r8.claim: Since the verse says humanity was spread from Adam and his wife alone, their immediate sons and daughters must have intermarried; the author then asks how that second generation reproduced.
TABATABAI:4:1#10/r8.anchor: ومن المعلوم أن انحصار مبدأ النسل في آدم وزوجته يقضي بازدواج بنيهما من بناتهما

TABATABAI:4:1#11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#11/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#11/r1.claim: Sibling marriage is forbidden in Islam and reportedly in earlier laws, but it is a legislative ruling tied to benefit and harm; God could allow it in necessity and prohibit it when the need ended and immorality threatened society.
TABATABAI:4:1#11/r1.anchor: فإنما هو حكم تشريعي يتبع المصالح والمفاسد لا تكويني غير قابل للتغيير وزمامه بيد الله سبحانه يفعل ما يشاء ويحكم ما يريد

TABATABAI:4:1#11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#11/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#11/r2.claim: The objection from natural religion fails: innate disposition does not reject sibling contact itself, but rejects its social consequences—public indecency and the collapse of chastity—which did not apply when siblings alone existed and proliferation was divinely intended.
TABATABAI:4:1#11/r2.anchor: فإن الفطرة لا تنفيه ولا تدعو إلى خلافه من جهه تنفرها عن هذا النوع من المباشرة مباشرة الأخ الأخت وإنما تبغضه وتنفيه من جهة تأديته إلى شيوع الفحشاء والمنكر

TABATABAI:4:1#11/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#11/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#11/r3.claim: Historical reports of long practice among Magi, legal acceptance in Russia, and illicit prevalence in Europe are evidence against an instinctive aversion to sibling unions.
TABATABAI:4:1#11/r3.anchor: تداوله بين المجوس أعصارا طويلة على ما يقصه التاريخ وشيوعه قانونيا في روسيا على ما يحكى وكذا شيوعه سفاحا من غير طريق الازدواج القانوني في اوروبا

TABATABAI:4:1#11/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#11/r4.speaker: بعض علماء الحقوق
TABATABAI:4:1#11/r4.claim: Some legal scholars argue that natural law opposes sibling unions because household familiarity and association extinguish the innate attraction between siblings.

TABATABAI:4:1#11/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#11/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#11/r5.claim: The natural-law objection is denied, limited to cases without necessity, and relevant only where social rules do not protect needed welfare; most current laws and customs are themselves unnatural.
TABATABAI:4:1#11/r5.anchor: وفيه أنه ممنوع كما تقدم أولا ومقصور في صورة عدم الحاجة الضرورية ثانيا ومخصوص بما لا تكون القوانين الوضعية غير الطبيعية حافظة للصلاح الواجب الحفظ في المجتمع

TABATABAI:4:1#11/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#11/r6.speaker: الإمام الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:4:1#11/r6.claim: In a report in al-Tawhid, al-Sadiq says God created a million Adams and that the present people belong to the last of them.
TABATABAI:4:1#11/r6.anchor: في التوحيد عن الصادق عليه السلام في حديث قال لعلك ترى أن الله لم يخلق بشرا غيركم؟ بلى والله لقد خلق ألف ألف آدم

TABATABAI:4:1#12/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r1.speaker: الصادق
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r1.claim: A report in al-Khiṣāl says God created twelve thousand worlds, each larger than the seven heavens and earths, with each world unaware of the others.
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r1.anchor: وفي الخصال عن الصادق عليه السلام قال إن الله تعالى خلق اثنا عشر ألف عالم

TABATABAI:4:1#12/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r2.claim: A report says seven worlds inhabited earth successively before Adam; their inhabitants were not Adam's descendants and were made from earth's surface.
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r2.anchor: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام لقد خلق الله عز وجل في الأرض منذ خلقها سبعة عالمين ليس هم من ولد آدم

TABATABAI:4:1#12/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر عن أبيه عن آبائه عن رسول الله
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r3.claim: In response to the claim that Eve came from Adam's rib, the Prophet says God formed Adam from clay and formed Eve from the remaining clay.
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r3.anchor: إن الله تبارك وتعالى قبض قبضة من طين فخلطها بيمينه - وكلتا يديه يمين - فخلق منها آدم وفضلت فضلة من الطين فخلق منها حواء

TABATABAI:4:1#12/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r4.claim: Other reports and Genesis say Eve came from Adam's shortest left rib; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says this is not impossible in itself, but the Qur'an gives no evidence for it.
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r4.anchor: وهناك روايات أخر تدل على أنها خلقت من خلف آدم وهو أقصر أضلاعه من الجانب الأيسر

TABATABAI:4:1#12/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r5.speaker: السجاد
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r5.claim: In a debate, al-Sajjād says Cain married Abel's sister and Abel married Cain's sister; the Quraysh interlocutor asks whether this was their offspring.
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r5.anchor: عن السجاد عليه السلام في حديث له مع قرشي يصف فيه تزويج هابيل بلوزا أخت قابيل

TABATABAI:4:1#12/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r6.speaker: السجاد
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r6.claim: Al-Sajjād answers that Magians only practiced sibling marriage after God prohibited it, while it had been an earlier divine law for Adam's family.
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r6.anchor: إن المجوس فعلوا ذلك بعد التحريم من الله

TABATABAI:4:1#12/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r7.claim: The report that Adam's wife was created from him and permitted to him accords with the Qur'an's apparent meaning and reason; other reports say the siblings married houris or jinn.
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r7.anchor: وهذا الذي ورد في الحديث هو الموافق لظاهر الكتاب والاعتبار

TABATABAI:4:1#12/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r8.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī notes reports that Cain and Abel married women sent down from houris and jinn, but says his earlier discussion established the correct account.
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r8.anchor: وهناك روايات أخر تعارضها وهي تدل على أنهم تزوجوا بمن نزل إليهم من الحور والجان

TABATABAI:4:1#12/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r9.speaker: الباقر
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r9.claim: Al-Bāqir interprets the command concerning kinship as an instruction not to sever family ties; the author says this rests on reading the word in the accusative.
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r9.anchor: عن الباقر عليه السلام واتقوا الأرحام أن تقطعوها

TABATABAI:4:1#12/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r10.claim: The accusative reading underlies al-Bāqir's interpretation of the verse's kinship phrase.

TABATABAI:4:1#12/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r11.speaker: الصادق
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r11.claim: Al-Kāfī and al-ʿAyyāshī report that God commanded people to maintain human kinship ties and magnified them by pairing them with Himself.
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r11.anchor: وفي الكافي وتفسير العياشي هي أرحام الناس إن الله عز وجل أمر بصلتها وعظمها

TABATABAI:4:1#12/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r12.claim: The report's statement that God set kinship alongside Himself refers to their conjunction in the verse's wording.
TABATABAI:4:1#12/r12.anchor: والمراد بجعلها معه الاقتران الواقع في قوله تعالى

TABATABAI:4:1#13/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r1.speaker: النبي عن ابن عباس
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r1.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās quoting the Prophet says maintaining kinship makes life last longer in this world and brings good in the next.
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r1.anchor:
قال ابن عباس قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
" يقول الله تعالى صلوا أرحامكم فإنه أبقى لكم

TABATABAI:4:1#13/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī links the report to widely transmitted accounts that kinship ties extend life and severing them has the opposite effect.
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r2.anchor: أن صلة الرحم تزيد في العمر وقطعها بالعكس من ذلك

TABATABAI:4:1#13/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r3.claim: He suggests the promise may be supported by the coming discussion of fear for vulnerable descendants left behind.
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r3.anchor: بما سيأتي في تفسير قوله تعالى وليخش الذين لو تركوا من خلفهم ذرية ضعافا خافوا عليهم النساء 9 الآية

TABATABAI:4:1#13/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r4.claim: Alternatively, kinship may make life more enduring through its practical effects: family solidarity strengthens people against calamities, enemies, and threats to well-being.
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r4.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون المراد بكونه أبقى كون الصلة أبقى للحياة من حيث أثرها

TABATABAI:4:1#13/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r5.speaker: علي عن الأصبغ بن نباتة
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r5.claim: ʿAlī says an angry person should approach an angry relative, since contact between kin calms the bond; kinship also appeals to God for those who maintain or sever it.
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r5.anchor: سمعت أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام يقول إن أحدكم ليغضب فما يرضى حتى يدخل النار فأيما رجل منكم غضب على ذي رحمه فليدن منه

TABATABAI:4:1#13/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r6.speaker: علي عن الأصبغ بن نباتة
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r6.claim: The report depicts kinship as attached to the Throne, making a metallic ringing sound, and praying for connection or severance according to how people treat it.
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r6.anchor: وإنها متعلقة بالعرش تنقضه انتقاض الحديد فتنادي اللهم صل من وصلني واقطع من قطعني

TABATABAI:4:1#13/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r7.claim: Kinship is a real bond of shared descent through one or both parents, with genuine moral, spiritual, bodily, and innate effects that can be weakened but never erased.
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r7.anchor: والرحم كما عرفت هي جهة الوحدة الموجودة بين أشخاص الإنسان من حيث اتصال مادة وجودهم في الولادة

TABATABAI:4:1#13/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r8.claim: Because kinship is among the strongest natural bonds, kindness among relatives has greater effect than kindness among strangers, and injury to relatives likewise wounds more deeply.
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r8.anchor: فالرحم من أقوى أسباب الالتئام الطبيعي بين أفراد العشيرة

TABATABAI:4:1#13/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r9.claim: Approaching a relative honors and strengthens kinship, renewing its effects through compassion and affection.
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r9.anchor: فإن الدنو من ذي الرحم رعاية لحكمها وتقوية لجانبها

TABATABAI:4:1#13/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r10.speaker: الصادق عن أبيه
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r10.claim: A report says an angry person should change posture: stand if seated, sit if standing, and approach and touch an angry relative so kinship can calm the anger.
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r10.anchor: الصادق عن أبيه عليهما السلام أنه ذكر الغضب فقال إن الرجل ليغضب حتى ما يرضى أبدا ويدخل بذلك النار فأيما رجل غضب وهو قائم فليجلس

TABATABAI:4:1#13/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r11.claim: Changing from standing to sitting redirects attention from impulsive anger and satanic distraction to a new matter; human nature is more inclined toward mercy than anger.
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r11.anchor: وفي تغيير الحال من القيام إلى القعود صرف النفس عن شأن إلى شأن جديد

TABATABAI:4:1#13/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#13/r12.claim: He says the effect of drawing near to kin and touching them is observable and tested.

TABATABAI:4:1#14/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#14/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#14/r1.claim: Al-Ṣiḥāḥ defines inqāḍ as a small sound like tapping; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the Throne will be explained as the station of comprehensive active knowledge of events.
TABATABAI:4:1#14/r1.anchor: وفي الصحاح الإنقاض صويت مثل النقر وقد تقدم في الكلام على الكرسي

TABATABAI:4:1#14/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#14/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#14/r2.claim: The Throne is the level where scattered events, causes, and cosmic chains converge and from which they are set in motion, like a king's throne directing a kingdom.
TABATABAI:4:1#14/r2.anchor: المراد بالعرش مقام العلم الإجمالي الفعلي بالحوادث

TABATABAI:4:1#14/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#14/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#14/r3.claim: Kinship is like a spirit flowing through the forms of people joined by family relation; when oppressed, it seeks refuge in the Throne and asks for help.
TABATABAI:4:1#14/r3.anchor: والرحم كما عرفت حقيقة هي كالروح السالب في قوالب الأشخاص الذين يجمعهم جامع القرابة

TABATABAI:4:1#14/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#14/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#14/r4.claim: The image compares the kinship bond's plea to tapping iron, whose resonance and vibration spread throughout its mass, as with bells and metal bowls.
TABATABAI:4:1#14/r4.anchor: شبه فيه ما يحدث في هذا الحال بالنقر الواقع على الحديد الذي يحدث فيه رنينا

TABATABAI:4:1#14/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#14/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#14/r5.claim: The prayer for those who maintain or sever kinship conveys the substance of its appeal; many reports say maintaining ties lengthens life and cutting them shortens it.
TABATABAI:4:1#14/r5.anchor: حكاية لفحوى التجائها واستنصارها وفي الروايات الكثيرة أن صلة الرحم تزيد في العمر

TABATABAI:4:1#14/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#14/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#14/r6.claim: The cosmic order is directed toward good ends and repairs defective parts or removes them; severing kinship resists this order and, if unreformed, brings shortened life and descendants' extinction.
TABATABAI:4:1#14/r6.anchor: وقاطع الرحم يحارب الله في تكوينه فإن لم يصلح بالاستصلاح بتر الله عمره وقطع دابره

TABATABAI:4:1#14/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:1#14/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:1#14/r7.claim: People may fail to sense this reality because chronic ailments have surrounded human life and dulled its capacity to perceive pain and punishment.
TABATABAI:4:1#14/r7.anchor: لأن الأدواء قد أحاطت بجثمان الإنسانية فاختلطت وتشابهت وأزمنت

ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r1.claim: The sura opens with admonition: God's creation establishes that He is one and that He alone has the right to be feared.
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r1.anchor: ابتدأ الله السورة بالموعظة. أخبر بما يوجب أنه واحد وأن حقه

ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r2.claim: The single soul is Adam; واحدة agrees with the feminine grammatical form نفس although the referent and meaning here are masculine, and واحد would also be valid.
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r2.anchor: يعني من آدم عليه السلام، وإنما قيل في اللغة واحدة لأن لفظ النفس

ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r3.claim: His wife Eve was created from one of Adam's ribs, and God spread all human beings from the two of them.
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r3.anchor: حواء خلقت من ضلع من أضلاع آدم، وبث الله جميع خلق الناس

ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r4.claim: بث means spreading or dispersing; the Qur'anic image of scattered moths supports that meaning.
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r4.anchor: ومعنى " بث " نشر، يقال: بث الله الخلق، وقال

ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r5.claim: Some Arabs also use أبث for spreading, and both بثثتك سري and أبثثتك سري mean revealing a secret to someone.
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r5.anchor: وبعض العرب يقول أبث الله الخلق، ويقال بثثتك سري وأبثثتك سري.

ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r6.claim: The doubled reading تساءلون derives from تتساءلون, with the tāʾ assimilated into the nearby sīn.
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r6.anchor: بالتشديد، فالأصل تتساءلون. وأدغمت التاء في السين لقرب مكان هذه

ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r7.claim: In the lighter reading, the second tāʾ of the original تتساءلون is dropped because two tāʾs are cumbersome and the meaning remains clear.
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r7.anchor: ومن قرأ بالتخفيف فالأصل تتساءلون، إلا أن التاء الثانية حذفت

ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r8.claim: تساءلون به means asking one another for rights by invoking God.

ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r9.claim: The sound reading puts الأرحام in the accusative: fear kinship ties by not severing them.
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r9.anchor: القراءة الجيدة نصب الأرحام. المعنى واتقوا الأرحام أن تقطعوها

ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r10.claim: Putting الأرحام in the genitive is bad Arabic except under poetic necessity and religiously wrong, since the Prophet forbade swearing by one's fathers.
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r10.anchor: فأما الجر في الأرحام فخطأ في العربية لا يجوز إلا في اضطرار شعر

ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r11.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r11.speaker: إسماعيل بن إسحاق
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r11.claim: Abu Ishaq Ismail ibn Ishaq held that swearing by anyone besides God is a grave matter reserved to God, as the transmitted report states.
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r11.anchor: رأيت أبا إسحاق إسماعيل بن إسحاق يذهب إلى أن الحلف بغير الله أمر عظيم

ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r12.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r12.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r12.claim: Grammarians agree that a genitive pronoun cannot be coordinated with an overt noun without repeating the preposition; forms like مررت به وزيد are disfavored.
ZAJJAJ:v2p5/r12.anchor: فأما العربية فإجماع النحويين أنه يقبح أن ينسق باسم ظاهر على اسم مضمر

TABRISI:4:1/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1/r1.speaker: أهل الكوفة
TABRISI:4:1/r1.claim: The Kufan readers lighten the sin in تسألون.
TABRISI:4:1/r1.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة تسألون بتخفيف السين

TABRISI:4:1/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1/r2.speaker: الباقون
TABRISI:4:1/r2.claim: The remaining readers geminate the sin in تسألون.

TABRISI:4:1/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1/r3.speaker: حمزة
TABRISI:4:1/r3.claim: Hamza reads الأرحام in the genitive.

TABRISI:4:1/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1/r4.speaker: الباقون
TABRISI:4:1/r4.claim: The remaining readers use the accusative for الأرحام.

TABRISI:4:1/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:1/r5.claim: A noncanonical reading puts الأرحام in the nominative.

TABRISI:4:1/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:1/r6.claim: The light reading contracts تتساءلون by deleting a ta where similar letters come together; the geminated reading merges ta into sin, helped by their shared articulation and voicelessness.
TABRISI:4:1/r6.anchor: من خفف تسألون أراد تتساءلون فحذف التاء من تتفاعلون لاجتماع حروف متقاربة

TABRISI:4:1/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:1/r7.claim: The accusative الأرحام can coordinate either with the object governed by the preposition or with اتقوا, yielding a command to maintain kinship ties.
TABRISI:4:1/r7.anchor: من نصب الأرحام احتمل انتصابه وجهين

TABRISI:4:1/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:1/r8.claim: The genitive reading coordinates the noun with the pronoun governed by باء, a construction weak by analogy and rare in usage.
TABRISI:4:1/r8.anchor: وأما من جر فإنه عطف على الضمير المجرور بالباء وهذا ضعيف في القياس وقليل في الاستعمال

TABRISI:4:1/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:1/r9.claim: The attached pronoun resembles tanwin because each is a single silent element that cannot be separated from its noun; the analogy is supported by dropping the ya in vocative forms such as يا غلام.
TABRISI:4:1/r9.anchor: لأن الضمير قد صار عوضا مما كان متصلا بالاسم من التنوين

TABRISI:4:1/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:1/r10.claim: Unlike a pronoun, an overt noun can be separated from its genitive by an adverb or other material, making the two forms less alike.
TABRISI:4:1/r10.anchor: واجتماعهما في السكون ولأنه لا يوقف على الاسم منفصلا منه

TABRISI:4:1/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1/r11.speaker: سيبويه
TABRISI:4:1/r11.claim: Sibawayh cites a poem coordinating الأيام with the genitive pronoun بك, an example of poetic license.
TABRISI:4:1/r11.anchor:
أنشد سيبويه:
فاليوم قربت تهجونا وتشتمنا فاذهب فما بك والأيام من عجب

TABRISI:4:1#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:1#2/r1.claim: Another poet coordinates الكعب with the pronoun in بينها, likewise as a poetic exception.

TABRISI:4:1#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:1#2/r2.claim: Such poetic constructions do not establish a model for the Quran or eloquent speech.
TABRISI:4:1#2/r2.anchor: ومثل ذلك لا يجوز في القرآن والكلام الفصيح

TABRISI:4:1#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#2/r3.speaker: المازني
TABRISI:4:1#2/r3.claim: Al-Mazini argues that coordination requires the first term to be capable of being a counterpart to the second; thus مررت بك وزيد is not acceptable.
TABRISI:4:1#2/r3.anchor: قال المازني: وذلك لأن الثاني في العطف شريك للأول

TABRISI:4:1#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:1#2/r4.claim: The anomalous nominative reading makes الأرحام a subject with an understood predicate: kinship ties too are something one must revere.
TABRISI:4:1#2/r4.anchor: فالوجه في رفعه على الابتداء أي والأرحام مما يجب أن تتقوه

TABRISI:4:1#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:1#2/r5.claim: البث means spreading, as in the Quranic image of scattered moths; some speakers also use أبث with the same meaning.
TABRISI:4:1#2/r5.anchor: البث النشر يقال: بث الله الخلق

TABRISI:4:1#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:1#2/r6.claim: Both forms are used in the language for spreading a secret: بثثتك سري and أبثثتك سري.

TABRISI:4:1#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:1#2/r7.claim: رقيب comes from watching and waiting; it means a guardian from whom nothing is hidden, while رقبي describes each person awaiting the other’s death.
TABRISI:4:1#2/r7.anchor: وأصل الرقيب من الترقب وهو الانتطار

TABRISI:4:1#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:1#2/r8.claim: The opening address is directed to all morally responsible people.
TABRISI:4:1#2/r8.anchor: وهو خطاب للمكلفين من جميع البشر

TABRISI:4:1#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:1#2/r9.claim: One view says prior scriptures addressed people as the poor, while the Quran uses يا أيها الناس in Meccan revelation and addresses either believers or all people in Medinan revelation.
TABRISI:4:1#2/r9.anchor: وقيل: النداء إنما كان في سائر كتب الله السالفة بيا أيها المساكين

TABRISI:4:1#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#2/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:1#2/r10.claim: اتقوا ربكم means avoid disobeying or opposing God by neglecting commands and committing prohibitions.
TABRISI:4:1#2/r10.anchor: اتقوا معصية ربكم أو مخالفة ربكم بترك ما أمر به وارتكاب ما نهى عنه

TABRISI:4:1#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#2/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:1#2/r11.claim: Another interpretation is to protect God’s due from being neglected.
TABRISI:4:1#2/r11.anchor: وقيل: معناه اتقوا حقه أن تضيعوه

TABRISI:4:1#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#2/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:1#2/r12.claim: A further interpretation is to fear God’s punishment.

TABRISI:4:1#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#2/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:1#2/r13.claim: The creation of humanity from one soul and the great favor of existence make reverence due to God, its benefactor.
TABRISI:4:1#2/r13.anchor: عقاب من أنعم عليكم بأعظم النعم وهي أن خلقكم من نفس واحدة

TABRISI:4:1#2/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#2/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:1#2/r14.claim: Another explanation emphasizes God’s complete power: the One able to create humanity from one soul is even more able to punish it.
TABRISI:4:1#2/r14.anchor: وقيل: إن المراد به بيان كمال قدرته فكأنه قال الذي قدر على أن خلقكم

TABRISI:4:1#2/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#2/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:1#2/r15.claim: All exegetes identify the single soul as Adam.
TABRISI:4:1#2/r15.anchor: المراد بالنفس هنا آدم عند جميع المفسرين

TABRISI:4:1#2/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#2/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:1#2/r16.claim: The adjective uses feminine agreement because النفس is grammatically feminine, even though Adam is intended.
TABRISI:4:1#2/r16.anchor: وإنما لم يقل نفس واحد بالتذكير وإن كان المراد آدم لأن لفظ النفس مؤنث بالصيغة

TABRISI:4:1#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:1#3/r1.claim: Feminine agreement with nafs follows its grammatical form, though masculine wāḥid would also be possible; the supporting poetic fragment has no poet named in this segment.
TABRISI:4:1#3/r1.anchor: فأنث على اللفظ ولو قال من نفس واحد لجاز

TABRISI:4:1#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#3/r2.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
TABRISI:4:1#3/r2.claim: Most exegetes say Eve was created from one of Adam's ribs.
TABRISI:4:1#3/r2.anchor: ذهب أكثر المفسرين إلى أنها خلقت من ضلع من أضلاع آدم ع.

TABRISI:4:1#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#3/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:4:1#3/r3.claim: The Prophet says woman was created from Adam's rib; straightening her breaks her, while accepting her crookedness allows enjoyment of her.
TABRISI:4:1#3/r3.anchor:
ورووا عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:
" خلقت المرأة من ضلع آدم ع إن أقمتها كسرتها وإن تركتها وفيها عوج استمتعت بها "

TABRISI:4:1#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#3/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر الباقر
TABRISI:4:1#3/r4.claim: Abu Jaʿfar al-Bāqir says Eve was made from the leftover clay of which Adam was created.
TABRISI:4:1#3/r4.anchor: وروي عن أبي جعفر الباقر ع أن الله تعالى خلق حواء من فضل الطينة التي خلق منها آدم

TABRISI:4:1#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#3/r5.speaker: تفسير علي بن إبراهيم
TABRISI:4:1#3/r5.claim: The Tafsīr of ʿAlī b. Ibrāhīm says Eve was created from Adam's lower ribs.
TABRISI:4:1#3/r5.anchor: وفي تفسير علي بن إبراهيم: من أسفل أضلاعه.

TABRISI:4:1#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#3/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:1#3/r6.claim: The two original humans spread many men and women through reproduction.
TABRISI:4:1#3/r6.anchor: أي نشر وفرق من هاتين النفسين على وجه التناسل رجالا { ونساء }

TABRISI:4:1#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#3/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:1#3/r7.claim: A shared origin encourages people to show one another affection and mercy because they all return to one source.
TABRISI:4:1#3/r7.anchor: لأنه أقرب إلى أن يعطف بعضنا على بعض ويرحم بعضنا بعضا لرجوعنا إلى أصل واحد

TABRISI:4:1#3/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#3/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:1#3/r8.claim: Creation from one soul is a more compelling sign of God's power and evidence of His knowledge and wisdom.
TABRISI:4:1#3/r8.anchor: ولأن ذلك أبلغ في القدرة، وأدل على العلم والحكمة.

TABRISI:4:1#3/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#3/r9.speaker: الحسن وإبراهيم
