TABRISI:4:1#3/r9.claim: On one reading, people invoke God and kinship when asking one another; al-arḥām is coordinated with the grammatical position of bihi.
TABRISI:4:1#3/r9.anchor: عن الحسن وإبراهيم وعلى هذا يكون قوله: { والأرحام } عطفا على موضع قوله به

TABRISI:4:1#3/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#3/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:1#3/r10.claim: On that reading, as people honor God in their words, they should honor Him through obedience.
TABRISI:4:1#3/r10.anchor: والمعنى أنكم كما تعظمون الله بأقوالكم، فعظموه بطاعتكم إياه.

TABRISI:4:1#3/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#3/r11.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد والضحاك والربيع وأبو جعفر
TABRISI:4:1#3/r11.claim: They read the phrase as seeking rights and needs by God and as commanding people to fear severing kinship ties.
TABRISI:4:1#3/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد والضحاك والربيع وهو المروي عن أبي جعفر ع فعلى هذا

TABRISI:4:1#3/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#3/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:1#3/r12.claim: On this second reading, al-arḥām is accusative and coordinated with God's name; the construction supports a duty to maintain kinship ties.
TABRISI:4:1#3/r12.anchor: يكون منصوبا عطفا على اسم الله تعالى، وهذا يدل على وجوب صلة الرحم

TABRISI:4:1#3/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#3/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:4:1#3/r13.claim: In a divine report, God calls Himself al-Raḥmān, says He created kinship and named it from His own name, and promises connection to those who maintain it and severance to those who cut it.
TABRISI:4:1#3/r13.anchor: أنه قال الله تعالى: " أنا الرحمن خلقت الرحم، وشققت لها اسما من اسمي، فمن وصلها وصلته

TABRISI:4:1#3/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#3/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:1#3/r14.claim: Maintaining kinship can mean accepting one's lineage, giving financial support to relatives, and similar acts.
TABRISI:4:1#3/r14.anchor: وصلة الرحم قد تكون بقبول النسب وقد تكون بالإنفاق على ذي الرحم وما يجري مجراه

TABRISI:4:1#3/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#3/r15.speaker: أمير المؤمنين
TABRISI:4:1#3/r15.claim: ʿAlī says anger toward a relative should be calmed by touching that relative; kinship then settles and calls God to connect those who connect it and cut off those who cut it.
TABRISI:4:1#3/r15.anchor: الأصبغ بن نباتة عن أمير المؤمنين ع قال: إن أحدكم ليغضب فما يرضى حتى يدخل به النار فأيما رجل منكم غضب على ذي رحمه فليمسه

TABRISI:4:1#3/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#3/r16.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:4:1#3/r16.claim: Mujāhid explains raqīb as a protector or guardian.

TABRISI:4:1#3/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#3/r17.speaker: ابن زيد
TABRISI:4:1#3/r17.claim: Ibn Zayd explains raqīb as one who knows; the author says this and the guardian sense are close.
TABRISI:4:1#3/r17.anchor: وقيل الرقيب العالم عن ابن زيد والمعنى متقارب

TABRISI:4:1#3/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:1#3/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:1#3/r18.claim: Kana indicates God's continuing vigilance from Adam through the addressed generation; He knows all that they do and nothing escapes Him.
TABRISI:4:1#3/r18.anchor: لأنه أراد أنه كان حفيظا على من تقدم زمانه من عهد آدم وولده إلى زمان المخاطبين وعالما بما صدر منهم لم يعزب عنه من ذلك شيء.

THALABI:v3p241#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p241#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p241#2/r1.claim: The single soul is Adam, and the spouse created from it is Eve; the commentary points to parallel wording in al-Aʿrāf and al-Zumar.
THALABI:v3p241#2/r1.anchor: يعني آدم وخلق منها زوجها يعني حواء، ونظيرها في سورة الأعراف والزمر

THALABI:v3p241#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p241#2/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p241#2/r2.claim: بث means to spread, make numerous, and bring forth men and women.
THALABI:v3p241#2/r2.anchor: وبث نشر وأظهر منهما رجالا كثيرا ونساء

THALABI:v3p241#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p241#2/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p241#2/r3.claim: تسائلون به means that people ask one another by God; the Kūfans lighten it by dropping one of the two tāʾs, as in the prohibition ولا تعاونوا.
THALABI:v3p241#2/r3.anchor: واتقوا الله الذي تسائلون به تسألون به، وخففه أهل الكوفة على حذف إحدى التائين تخفيفا

THALABI:v3p241#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p241#2/r4.speaker: قراءة العامة
THALABI:v3p241#2/r4.claim: The standard reading puts الأرحام in the accusative, coordinated with اتقوا: fear God and do not sever family ties.
THALABI:v3p241#2/r4.anchor: قراءة العامة: نصب أي واتقوا الأرحام إن تقطعوها.

THALABI:v3p241#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p241#2/r5.speaker: النخعي ويحيى بن وثاب وطلحة بن مصرف وقتادة والأعمش وحمزة
THALABI:v3p241#2/r5.claim: These readers put الأرحام in the genitive, coordinating it with the pronoun governed by bi and reading the appeal as by God and by kinship.
THALABI:v3p241#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ النخعي ويحيى بن وثاب وطلحة بن مصرف وقتادة والأعمش وحمزة: بالخفض على معنى وبالأرحام

THALABI:v3p241#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p241#2/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p241#2/r6.claim: The accusative is more correct and eloquent: Arabic normally does not coordinate an explicit noun to the meaning of a preposition without repeating that preposition or using the accusative, though poetry permits the construction.
THALABI:v3p241#2/r6.anchor: والقراءة الأولى أصح وأفصح، لأن العرب لا يكلأ بنسق بظاهر على المعنى، إلا أن يعيدوا الخافض

THALABI:v3p241#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p241#2/r7.speaker: شاعر
THALABI:v3p241#2/r7.claim: An unattributed poetic example is cited as evidence that this construction can occur in poetry.
THALABI:v3p241#2/r7.anchor: كقول الشاعر: يا قوم مالي وأبي ذويب

THALABI:v3p241#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p241#2/r8.speaker: شاعر
THALABI:v3p241#2/r8.claim: A second unattributed line offers another poetic instance of the construction with والأيام.
THALABI:v3p241#2/r8.anchor: قال الشاعر: فاليوم قربت تهجونا وتشتمنا … اذهب فمالك والأيام من عجب

THALABI:v3p242/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p242/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن يزيد المقبري
THALABI:v3p242/r1.claim: He recites al-arham in the nominative, either as a new subject after the preceding clause or as an exhortation; Arabs may raise an exhortative noun.
THALABI:v3p242/r1.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله بن يزيد المقبري: (والأرحام) رفعا على الابتداء، كأنه نوى تمام الكلام عند قوله تسائلون به ثم ابتدأ

THALABI:v3p242/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p242/r2.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v3p242/r2.claim: Al-Farra cites a poem illustrating Arabic use of the nominative for an exhortation, with the repeated call to arms.
THALABI:v3p242/r2.anchor: وأنشد الفراء: أين قوما منهم عمير … وأشباه عمير ومنهم السفاح

THALABI:v3p242/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p242/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p242/r3.claim: Raqīb means guardian or watchful keeper and may carry the active sense of faʿil.
THALABI:v3p242/r3.anchor: إن الله كان عليكم رقيبا أي حافظا، قيل: بمعنى فاعل

ASAD-NOTES:4:1#n1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:1#n1/r1.speaker: the classical commentators
ASAD-NOTES:4:1#n1/r1.claim: Most classical commentators choose nafs as 'human being' and assume it refers here to Adam.
ASAD-NOTES:4:1#n1/r1.anchor: most of the classical commentators choose "human being", and assume that it refers here to Adam

ASAD-NOTES:4:1#n1/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:1#n1/r2.speaker: Muhammad 'Abduh
ASAD-NOTES:4:1#n1/r2.claim: Abduh rejects the Adam reading and prefers 'humankind' because it stresses common origin and human brotherhood without binding the verse to the Biblical creation story.
ASAD-NOTES:4:1#n1/r2.anchor: Muhammad 'Abduh, however, rejects this interpretation (Manar IV, 323 ff.) and gives, instead, his preference to "humankind"

ASAD-NOTES:4:1#n1/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:1#n1/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:4:1#n1/r3.claim: Asad renders nafs as 'living entity', following Abduh's reasoning about humanity's common origin.
ASAD-NOTES:4:1#n1/r3.anchor: My rendering of nafs, in this context, as "living entity" follows the same reasoning

ASAD-NOTES:4:1#n1/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:1#n1/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:4:1#n1/r4.claim: Zawj can denote either member of an animate pair; for humans it means either a woman's husband or a man's wife.
ASAD-NOTES:4:1#n1/r4.anchor: with reference to human beings, it signifies a woman's mate (husband) as well as a man's mate (wife).

ASAD-NOTES:4:1#n1/r5.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:1#n1/r5.speaker: Abu Muslim
ASAD-NOTES:4:1#n1/r5.claim: Abu Muslim interprets minha as 'from its own kind', meaning each sex's counterpart is created from the same kind; this supports Abduh's reading.
ASAD-NOTES:4:1#n1/r5.anchor: Abu Muslim - as quoted by Razi - interprets the phrase "He created out of it (minha) its mate" as meaning

ASAD-NOTES:4:1#n1/r6.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:1#n1/r6.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:4:1#n1/r6.claim: Asad says the literal 'out of it' points to the biological fact that both sexes originated from one living entity.
ASAD-NOTES:4:1#n1/r6.anchor: the biological fact that both sexes have originated from "one living entity".

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the address 'O people' is directed to the people of Mecca.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الخطاب لأهل مكة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#3/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#3/r1.claim: The feminine form of نفس governs agreement even though the intended person is male, Adam; a cited poem shows the same grammatical usage.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#3/r1.anchor:
أنثها على لفظ النفس وإن عنى به مذكرا كما قال:
أبوك خليفة ولدته أخرى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#3/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#3/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#3/r3.claim: His mate is Eve, created from one of Adam's ribs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#3/r3.anchor: {وخلق منها زوجها} حواء (¬1)، خلقت من (ضلع (¬2) من أضلاع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#3/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#3/r4.speaker: النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#3/r4.claim: The Prophet says woman was created from a rib; trying to straighten her breaks her, while living with her crookedness allows enjoyment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#3/r4.anchor: ولذلك قال النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: "إن المرأة خلقت من ضلع، فإن ذهبت تقيمها كسرتها، وإن تركتها وفيها عوج استمتعت بها"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#3/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#3/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#3/r5.claim: وبث منهما means dispersed and spread from the two.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#3/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#3/r6.speaker: ابن المظفر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#3/r6.claim: He defines بث as dispersing things, giving examples of scattering horses or hounds and spreading God's creation; he links it with carpets spread out in 88:16.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#3/r6.anchor: قال ابن المظفر (¬5): البث تفريقك الأشياء، يقال بثوا الخيل في الغارة، وبث الصياد كلابه، وخلق الله الخلق فبثهم في الأرض، بثث البسط إذا نشرتها (¬6)، قال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#3/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#3/r7.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#3/r7.claim: They note that some Arabs say أبث الله الخلق as well as بث الله الخلق.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#3/r7.anchor: قال الفراء، والزجاج: وبعض العرب يقول أبث (¬8) الله الخلق.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#3/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#3/r8.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#3/r8.claim: The verb for spreading a report is بث الحديث or أبثه, to circulate and disclose it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#3/r8.anchor: وبث الحديث إذا نشره وأفشاه، وكذلك أبثه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#3/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#3/r9.speaker: ذو الرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#3/r9.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's verse uses أبثه in the sense of disclosing or sharing something.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p281#3/r9.anchor:
قال ذو الرمة:
وأسقيه حتى كاد مما أبثه ... تكلمني أحجاره وملاعبه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r1.claim: تساءلون is read either with a light or doubled sīn.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r2.claim: The doubled reading derives from تتساءلون, assimilating tāʾ into sīn because their articulations are close and both are voiceless.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r2.anchor: فمن شدد أراد: تتساءلون، فأدغم التاء في السين لاجتماعهما في أنهما من حروف طرف اللسان وأصول الثنايا واجتماعهما في الهمس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r3.claim: The light reading deletes one tāʾ from تتفاعلون because adjacent similar sounds are simplified by deletion, assimilation, or substitution.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r3.anchor: ومن خفف، حذف تاء تتفاعلون لاجتماع حروف متقاربة فأعلها بالحذف، كما أعل الأول بالإدغام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r4.claim: The substitution example is طست for الطس, supported by al-Ajjaj's poetic line.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r4.anchor:
والإبدال كقولهم: طست (للطس) (¬2) أبدل من السين الثانية التاء لتقاربهما، قال العجاج:
أإن رأيت (هامتي) (¬3) كالطست

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r5.speaker: المازني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r5.claim: Al-Mazini cites poetry for الطس as an example of the same form.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r5.anchor:
وأنشد المازني في الطس:
لو عرضت لأيبلي قس ... أشعث في هيكله مندس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r6.claim: تساءلون بالله والأرحام means people ask one another for their needs and rights by invoking God and kinship.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r6.anchor: ومعنى: {تساءلون به والأرحام} أي تتساءلون فيما بينكم حوائجكم # وحقوقكم به فتقولون: أسألك بالله والرحم، وأنشدك الله والرحم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says Meccans denied resurrection but maintained kinship, and when entreating one another they invoked God and kinship; polytheists used the same appeal in letters to the Prophet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r7.anchor: يريدون أن أهل مكة لم يكونوا يؤمنون بالبعث، وكانوا يتواصلون بالأرحام، فإذا ناشد الرجل الرجل، قال: أنشدك الله والرحم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r8.claim: On Ibn Abbas's reading, الأرحام is accusative by coordination with the syntactic position of به; it means invoking kinship in their petitions.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r8.anchor: وعلى هذا التفسير انتصب {والأرحام} بالعطف على موضع {به}، كأنه قيل: وتذكرون الأرحام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r9.speaker: أبو علي وعلي بن عيسى
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r9.claim: They compare this coordination with the poetic construction فلسنا بالجبال ولا الحديدا.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r9.anchor:
قال أبو علي (¬4) وعلي بن عيسى (¬5): ويكون كقوله:
فلسنا بالجبال ولا الحديدا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r10.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد والسدي والضحاك وابن زيد والربيع والفراء والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r10.claim: Most commentators instead understand الأرحام as a command to fear violating kinship ties.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r10.anchor: وقال أكثر المفسرين: معنى {والأرحام} أي: واتقوا الأرحام أن تقطعوها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r11.claim: On this common interpretation, الأرحام coordinates with the command اتقوا: observe relatives' rights, maintain ties, and do not sever them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p283/r11.anchor: وعلى هذا التفسير انتصب الأرحام بالعطف على قوله أي: اتقوا الله واتقوا الأرحام، أي: اتقوا حق الأرحام فصلوها ولا تقطعوها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r1.claim: On the kinship interpretation, الأرحام can also be an exhortation: preserve and maintain family ties.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r1.anchor: ويجوز على هذا التفسير أن يكون منصوبا بالإغراء, أي: والأرحام فاحفظوها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r2.claim: This interpretation entails that severing kinship is forbidden and maintaining it obligatory.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r2.anchor: وهذا التفسير يدل على تحريم قطيعة الرحم، وينبئ بوجوب صلتها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r3.speaker: حمزة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r3.claim: Hamza reads الأرحام in the genitive, coordinating it with the attached pronoun in به; the interpretation of polytheists invoking God and kinship motivated this reading.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r3.anchor: وقرأ حمزة {والأرحام} جرا (¬3) بالعطف على المكني في {به}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r4.speaker: النحويون كلهم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r4.claim: All grammarians considered this reading weak and objectionable.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r4.anchor: وضعف النحويون كلهم هذه القراءة واستقبحوها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r5.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r5.claim: Abu Ali calls coordination on a genitive pronoun weak by analogy and rare in usage, making it better to avoid.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r5.anchor: هذا ضعيف في القياس قليل في الاستعمال، وما كان كذلك فترك الأخذ به أحسن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r6.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r6.claim: He argues that coordination should join like forms: a bound genitive pronoun resembles a particle rather than a free noun, so a visible noun should not be coordinated onto it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r6.anchor: المضمر المجرور قد خرج عن شبه الاسم وصار بمنزلة الحرف بدلالة أنه لا ينفصل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r7.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r7.claim: The attached pronoun also resembles tanwīn: it is a one-letter suffix and replaces tanwīn in possessives; deletion of yāʾ in يا غلام is common, supporting that analogy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r7.anchor: فصار كالتنوين؛ فلأن المضمر المجرور أيضا قد صار عوضا من التنوين إذا اتصل باسم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r8.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r8.claim: Since the genitive pronoun behaves like tanwīn or a particle, a stand-alone noun should not be coordinated onto it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p287/r8.anchor: فلم يعطف على المضمر المجرور لخروج المعطوف عليه عن شبه الاسم إلى شبه الحرف، وقد ذكرنا شأن التشاكل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p291/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p291/r1.speaker: سيبويه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p291/r1.claim: Sibawayh says an explicit noun cannot coordinate with an attached genitive pronoun unless the preposition is repeated, except in poetic necessity; the cited lines illustrate the poetic exception.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p291/r1.anchor:
وقال سيبويه: لا يجوز عطف الظاهر على المكني المخفوض من غير إعادة الخافض إلا في ضرورة الشعر (¬3)، وأنشد:
فاليوم قربت تهجونا وتشتمنا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p291/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p291/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p291/r2.claim: Al-Farra also cites a poetic example coordinating with a genitive pronoun without repeating the preposition.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p291/r2.anchor:
وأنشد الفراء أيضا:
نعلق في مثل السواري سيوفنا ... وما بينها والكعب غوط نفانف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p291/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p291/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p291/r3.claim: Despite its grammatical weakness, Abu Ishaq calls Hamza's reading a grave religious error because the Prophet forbade swearing by one's fathers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p291/r3.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق (¬2): وقراءة حمزة مع ضعفها وقبحها في العربية خطأ في أمر الدين عظيم؛ لأن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: "لا تحلفوا بآبائكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p291/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p291/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p291/r4.claim: His reasoning is that coordinating kinship with God's name would make swearing by kinship permissible, which it is not.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p291/r4.anchor: يعني أن الحلف بغير الله لا يجوز، وإذا عطفت الأرحام (كالمكني) (¬6) عن اسم الله أوجب جواز الحلف بالأرحام، وذلك غير جائز.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p291/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p291/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p291/r5.claim: رقيب means guardian or watcher; God watches people's deeds, so they should fear Him regarding what He prohibits.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p291/r5.anchor: الرقيب: الحافظ، يقال: رقب يرقب رقبة ورقوبا (¬1). ومعناه: أنه يرقب عليكم أعمالكم فاتقوه فيما نهاكم.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:1-2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:1-2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:1-2/r1.claim: The address يا أيها الناس means the people of Mecca; the single soul is Adam, and his spouse Eve was created from one of his ribs.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:1-2/r1.anchor: { يا أيها الناس } يا أهل مكة { اتقوا ربكم الذي خلقكم من نفس واحدة } آدم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:1-2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:1-2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:1-2/r2.claim: Bithth means spreading and dispersing people from Adam and Eve.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:1-2/r2.anchor: { وبث } أي: فرق ونشر { منهما } ، { واتقوا الله }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:1-2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:1-2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:1-2/r3.claim: People ask one another for needs and rights by invoking God, and the command about wombs means fearing God about severing family ties.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:1-2/r3.anchor: أي: تتساءلون فيما بينكم حوائجكم وحقوقكم به، وتقولون: أسألك بالله، وأنشدك الله،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:1-2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:1-2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:1-2/r4.claim: God watches and preserves their deeds, so they should fear Him in what He commands and forbids.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:1-2/r4.anchor: أي: حافظا يرقب عليكم أعمالكم، فاتقوه فيما أمركم به ونهاكم عنه.

BURHAN:v4p130/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p130/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p130/r1.claim: The use of “made” for Adam’s mate in al-Aʿraf and “created” in al-Nisa shows that the two verbs can be near-synonyms.
BURHAN:v4p130/r1.anchor: فهو يدل على انهما قد يستعملان استعمال المترادفين

BURHAN:v4p52/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p52/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p52/r3.claim: The two sūras beginning يا أيها الناس divide the themes similarly: al-Nisāʾ in the first half explains creation, while al-Ḥajj in the second treats the afterlife.
BURHAN:v4p52/r3.anchor: انه ورد في القران سورتان اولهما

BURHAN:v1p260#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p260#2/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p260#2/r1.claim: The surah order appears divinely fixed, with alphabetic grouping, matching adjacent endings and beginnings, verbal rhythm, and thematic similarity among its reasons.
BURHAN:v1p260#2/r1.anchor: لترتيب وضع السور فى المصحف أسباب تطلع على أنه توقيفى صادر عن حكيم أحدها بحسب الحروف

BURHAN:v1p260#2/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p260#2/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p260#2/r9.claim: Al-Nisa contains rules for relationships, including God-created kinship and marriage ties and human agreements.
BURHAN:v1p260#2/r9.anchor: وأما سورة النساء فتتضمن جميع أحكام الأسباب التى بين الناس وهي نوعان محلوقة لله تعالى ومقدورة لهم كالنسب والصهر

BURHAN:v1p260#2/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p260#2/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p260#2/r10.claim: Its opening invokes the single soul, spouse, God, and kinship; the surah then treats agreements, property, marriage, inheritance, and prophetic covenants.
BURHAN:v1p260#2/r10.anchor: ولهذا افتتحها الله بقوله ﴿ ربكم الذي خلقكم من نفس واحدة وخلق منها زوجها ﴾ ثم قال

BURHAN:v3p106/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p106/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p106/r1.claim: Arabic can delete the nun of a dual or plural while its grammatical trace remains; the reading al-muqīmī al-ṣalāh illustrates this, as do shortened forms in extended relative clauses.
BURHAN:v3p106/r1.anchor: حذف نون التثنية والجمع وأثرها باق نحو الضاربا زيدا والضاربو زيدا

BURHAN:v3p106/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p106/r2.speaker: الأخفش
BURHAN:v3p106/r2.claim: Al-Muʾarrij al-Sadūsī asked al-Akhfash why ya is omitted in wa-l-layli idhā yasri; the answer was that Arabs reduce letters when a word is shifted from its ordinary sense, since night is traveled through rather than traveling.
BURHAN:v3p106/r2.anchor: ويحكى عن الأخفش أن المؤرج السدوسي سأله عن ذلك فقال لا أجيبك

BURHAN:v3p106/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p106/r3.speaker: الرماني
BURHAN:v3p106/r3.claim: Al-Rummānī explains final ya deletion as preserving the verse ending: endings are treated as if paused, like poetic rhyme.
BURHAN:v3p106/r3.anchor: وقال الرماني إنما حذفت الياء في الفواصل لأنها على نية الوقف

BURHAN:v3p106/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p106/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p106/r4.claim: In Moses' answer to Pharaoh, the subjects before the repeated Lord descriptions are omitted; Moses magnifies Pharaoh's audacity and points instead to God's distinctive acts, establishing that God has no likeness.
BURHAN:v3p106/r4.anchor: حذف المبتدأ في ثلاثة مواضع قبل ذكر الرب أي هو رب السموات والله ربكم

BURHAN:v3p106/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p106/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p106/r5.claim: The subject is omitted in ṣummun bukmun ʿumyun, with the pronoun hum understood, to spare the tongue from stating it explicitly.
BURHAN:v3p106/r5.anchor: كقوله تعالى ﴿ صم بكم عمي ﴾ 6 أي هم

BURHAN:v3p106/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p106/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p106/r6.claim: Some divine descriptions admit no other implicit subject: ʿālim al-ghayb and faʿʿāl li-mā yurīd are understood of God.
BURHAN:v3p106/r6.anchor: كقوله تعالى ﴿ عالم الغيب والشهادة ﴾ 1 ﴿ فعال لما يريد ﴾ 2

BURHAN:v3p106/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p106/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v3p106/r7.claim: When an omitted element is so familiar that stating it adds nothing, contextual evidence can speak more clearly than words; al-Zamakhsharī applies this to Hamza's reading, where the preposition before al-arḥām is understood from the preceding phrase.
BURHAN:v3p106/r7.anchor: قال الزمخشري وهو نوع من دلالة الحال التي لسانها أنطق من لسان المقال

BURHAN:v3p106/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p106/r8.speaker: الفارسي
BURHAN:v3p106/r8.claim: Al-Fārisī explains the genitive al-arḥām with an elided repeated preposition, wa-bi-l-arḥām, recoverable from the preceding genitive pronoun.
BURHAN:v3p106/r8.anchor: قال الفارسي متلخصا من عدم إعادة حرف الجر في المعطوف على الضمير المجرور

BURHAN:v3p111/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p111/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p111/r1.claim: An omission must be indicated by wording or context; otherwise the expression becomes unintelligible or an inelegant riddle. What remains must guide the reader to what was omitted.
BURHAN:v3p111/r1.anchor: لا بد أن يكون فيما أبقى دليل على ما ألقى

BURHAN:v3p111/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p111/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p111/r2.claim: Inflection can signal an omitted governor: on the accusative reading of al-arḥām, an understood command such as wa-iḥfaẓū al-arḥām supplies its case.

BURHAN:v3p111/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p111/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p111/r3.claim: Meaning and contextual knowledge can require an omitted object; the broad expression yaḥillu wa-yarbiṭu means that someone manages affairs and has full discretion.
BURHAN:v3p111/r3.anchor: والحالية قد تحصل من النظر إلى المعنى والنظر والعلم فإنه لا يتم إلا بمحذوف

BURHAN:v3p111/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p111/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p111/r4.claim: Syntax can reveal omissions: lā uqsim is understood as la-anā uqsim because a present-tense act is not sworn by, while tafʾat tadhkuru Yūsuf requires a negative lā.
BURHAN:v3p111/r4.anchor: وقد تدل الصناعة النحوية على التقدير كقولهم في ﴿ لا أقسم بيوم القيامة ﴾ 5 إن التقدير

BURHAN:v3p111/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p111/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p111/r5.claim: A single construction may allow multiple implied comparisons; one reading of afaman zuyyina lahu says it contrasts the beautified sinner with someone whose evil deed was not beautified.
BURHAN:v3p111/r5.anchor: أحدها كمن لم يزين له سوء عمله والمعنى

BURHAN:v4p113/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p113/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p113/r1.claim: Conjunction may be omitted when the first of two statements already calls for the second; each then sounds like an independent statement while the mind still links them.
BURHAN:v4p113/r1.anchor: من حيث إن المتقدم من القولين يستدعي التأخر منهما فلهذا كان الكلام مبنيا على الانفصال

BURHAN:v4p113/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p113/r2.speaker: الجمهور
BURHAN:v4p113/r2.claim: Most grammarians require a separator before coordinating onto an independent nominative pronoun; the examples emphasize the pronoun before adding the conjunct.
BURHAN:v4p113/r2.anchor: عند الجمهور خلافا لابن مالك في جعله من عطف الجمل

BURHAN:v4p113/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p113/r3.speaker: ابن مالك
BURHAN:v4p113/r3.claim: Ibn Mālik treats اسكن أنت وزوجك as coordination of clauses, supplying an implicit wa-li-taskun zawjuka rather than coordinating onto the pronoun.
BURHAN:v4p113/r3.anchor: خلافا لابن مالك في جعله من عطف الجمل بتقدير ولتسكن زوجك

BURHAN:v4p113/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p113/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v4p113/r4.claim: On the reading with an open wāw, al-Zamakhsharī analyzes aw ābāʾunā in the resurrection question as a conjunct on the pronoun, with the hamza as separator.
BURHAN:v4p113/r4.anchor: وجعل الزمخشري منه ﴿ أئنا لمبعوثون أو آباؤنا ﴾

BURHAN:v4p113/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p113/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p113/r5.claim: The proposed analysis of aw ābāʾunā is challenged because an interrogative hamza does not govern an isolated noun.
BURHAN:v4p113/r5.anchor: ورد بان الاستفهام لايدخل على المفردات

BURHAN:v4p113/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p113/r6.speaker: الفارسي
BURHAN:v4p113/r6.claim: Al-Fārisī gives mā ashraknā wa-lā ābāʾunā as another coordination example; Ibn al-Dahhān instead parses wa-lā ābāʾunā as a subject with an implicit predicate, ashrakū.
BURHAN:v4p113/r6.anchor: وجعل الفارسي منه ﴿ ما أشركنا ولا آباؤنا ﴾ 8 واعرب ابن الدهان

BURHAN:v4p113/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p113/r7.speaker: الكوفيون
BURHAN:v4p113/r7.claim: The Kufans allow coordination onto a pronoun without an intervening separator, citing wa-alladhīna hādū wa-l-ṣābiʾūn.
BURHAN:v4p113/r7.anchor: وأجاز الكوفيون العطف من غير فاصل كقوله تعالى ﴿ والذين هادوا والصابئون ﴾

BURHAN:v4p113/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p113/r8.speaker: الفارسي
BURHAN:v4p113/r8.claim: Al-Fārisī parses wa-huwa as a fresh subject rather than a conjunct on the pronoun in fastawā; he also says a genitive pronoun cannot be coordinated onto without repeating its preposition.
BURHAN:v4p113/r8.anchor: فقال الفارسي ﴿ وهو ﴾ مبتدأ وليس معطوفا على ضمير ﴿ فاستوى ﴾

BURHAN:v4p113/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p113/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p113/r9.claim: In wa-min Nūḥ, repeating the preposition is required if the phrase joins mink, but is optional if it joins al-nabiyyīn.
BURHAN:v4p113/r9.anchor: فان جعلنا ﴿ ومن نوح ﴾ معطوفا على ﴿ منك ﴾ فالاعادة لازمة وان جعل معطوفا على ﴿ النبيين ﴾ فجائزة

BURHAN:v4p113/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p113/r10.speaker: الكوفيون
BURHAN:v4p113/r10.claim: The Kufans say a preposition need not be repeated before a conjunct on a genitive pronoun, citing Hamza's genitive reading al-arḥām; an alternative parses it as an oath.
BURHAN:v4p113/r10.anchor: وقال الكوفيون لاتلزم الاعادة محتجين بآيات الاولى قراءة حمزة

BURHAN:v1p318/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p318/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p318/r1.claim: The Qurʾān is the revelation given to Muhammad for exposition and inimitability, whereas readings are variations in its written letters or their performance, such as lightening and doubling.
BURHAN:v1p318/r1.anchor: واعلم أن القرآن والقراءات حقيقتان متغايرتان فالقرآن هو الوحى المنزل على محمد

BURHAN:v1p318/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p318/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p318/r2.claim: Al-Dānī's al-Taysīr is recommended for the seven readings; al-Shāṭibī versified it, Ibn al-Bādhish wrote al-Iqnāʿ, and al-Shahrazūrī's al-Miṣbāḥ covers the ten readings.
BURHAN:v1p318/r2.anchor: وأحسن الموضوع للقراءات السبع كتاب التيسير لأبى عمرو الدانى وقد نظمه أبو محمد القاسم الشاطبى

BURHAN:v1p318/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p318/r3.speaker: الجمهور
BURHAN:v1p318/r3.claim: The majority regard the seven readings as mass-transmitted, while another view calls them merely well-known.
BURHAN:v1p318/r3.anchor: القراءات السبع متواترة عند الجمهور وقيل بل مشهورة

BURHAN:v1p318/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p318/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p318/r4.claim: The objections of al-Mubarrad to Hamza's al-arḥām and miṣrikhī, and of Ibn ʿAṣfūr to Ibn ʿĀmir's reading, do not count against the canonical readings.
BURHAN:v1p318/r4.anchor: ولا عبرة بإنكار المبرد قراءة حمزة ﴿ والأرحام ﴾ و / مصرخي /

BURHAN:v1p318/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p318/r5.speaker: أبو شامة
BURHAN:v1p318/r5.claim: Abū Shāma noted that the documented chains for the seven readings pass from one transmitter to another and do not uniformly meet the conditions of mass transmission at every level.
BURHAN:v1p318/r5.anchor: وقد أشار الشيخ شهاب الدين أبو شامة في كتابه المرشد الوجيز إلى شيء من ذلك

BURHAN:v1p318/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p318/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p318/r6.claim: The seven readings are mass-transmitted from their seven imams, though whether that transmission is mass-transmitted all the way back to the Prophet requires qualification.
BURHAN:v1p318/r6.anchor: والتحقيق أنها متواترة عن الأئمة السبعة أما تواترها عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ففيه نظر

BURHAN:v1p318/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p318/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو بن الحاجب
BURHAN:v1p318/r7.claim: Ibn al-Ḥājib excludes performance features such as lengthening, imāla, and easing hamza from the claim that the seven readings are mass-transmitted.
BURHAN:v1p318/r7.anchor: استثنى الشيخ أبو عمرو بن الحاجب قولنا إن القراءات السبع متواترة ما ليس من قبيل الأداء

BURHAN:v1p318/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p318/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p318/r8.claim: The exclusion is weak: lengthening and imāla are certainly mass-transmitted as shared categories, although readers differ over their degree.
BURHAN:v1p318/r8.anchor: وهذا ضعيف والحق أن المد والإمالة لا شك في تواتر المشترك بينهما

BURHAN:v1p318/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p318/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p318/r9.claim: Readers differ in measured length: Hamza and Warsh use six units, with reports of five or four; ʿĀṣim uses three, al-Kisāʾī two and a half, Qālūn two, and al-Sūsī one and a half.
BURHAN:v1p318/r9.anchor: فحمزة وورش بمقدار ست لغات وقيل خمس وقيل أربع وعن عاصم ثلاث

BURHAN:v1p321/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p321/r1.speaker: ابن الحاجب
BURHAN:v1p321/r1.claim: Ibn al-Ḥājib explains that an interrogative hamza is followed by a long vowel before an open wasl hamza to avoid confusing a question with a statement, as in āl-ḥasanu ʿindak.
BURHAN:v1p321/r1.anchor: قال ابن الحاجب في تصريفه واغتفر التقاء الساكنين في نحو آلحسن عندك وآيمن الله يمينك

BURHAN:v1p321/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p321/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p321/r2.claim: Some Arabs soften the wasl hamza between two pronunciations; readers transmit both forms, though the lengthened form is standard, and the Uthmanic spelling of a second hamza as wāw signals the softened form.
BURHAN:v1p321/r2.anchor: وبعض العرب يجعل همزة الوصل فيما ذكرنا بين بين ويقول آلحسن عندك وآيمن الله يمينك

BURHAN:v1p321/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p321/r3.speaker: الشاطبي
BURHAN:v1p321/r3.claim: For two hamzas in separate words with matching vowels, Abū ʿAmr drops the first according to al-Shāṭibī; another view says the second is dropped, as in jāʾa ajaluhum.
BURHAN:v1p321/r3.anchor: وقد قرأ به أبو عمرو في الهمزتين من كلمتين إذا اتفقتا في الحركة فأسقط الأولى منهما على رأي الشاطبي

BURHAN:v1p321/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p321/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p321/r4.claim: In the open-hamza case, Nāfiʿ through Qālūn and Ibn Kathīr through al-Bazzī also transmit dropping a hamza; Qunbul transmits its deletion within the single word shirkāʾī.
BURHAN:v1p321/r4.anchor: ووافقه على ذلك في المفتوحتين نافع من طريق قالون وابن كثير من طريق البزي

BURHAN:v1p321/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p321/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p321/r5.claim: Qurʾānic readings are fixed by transmission, not selected through grammarians' taste or eloquent reasoning; this rejects al-Zamakhsharī's criticism of Hamza's genitive al-arḥām and other disputed readings.
BURHAN:v1p321/r5.anchor: أن القراءات توقيفية وليست اختيارية خلافا لجماعة منهم الزمخشري حيث ظنوا أنها اختيارية

BURHAN:v2p120/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p120/r9.speaker: أبو بصر بن القشيري
BURHAN:v2p120/r9.claim: He argues that rejecting a reading established from the Prophet is perilous; Arabic is learned from the Prophet, whose eloquence is beyond doubt, rather than from language authorities who criticize it.
BURHAN:v2p120/r9.anchor: واختار أبو بصر بن القشيرى فى تفسيره التفاوت فقال وقد رد على الزجاج وغيره تضعيفهم قراءة

BURHAN:v2p120/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p120/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p120/r10.claim: The grammarians may only have meant that Hamza's reading is sound and eloquent though another reading is more eloquent; not every Qurʾānic expression must be at the highest degree.
BURHAN:v2p120/r10.anchor: ولعلهم أرادوا أنه صحيح فصيح وإن كان غيره أفصح منه فإنا لا ندعى

BURHAN:v2p466/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p466/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p466/r2.claim: Scholars differ whether a specific member stated after a general term was already included; the added mention can be emphatic, and al-Rūyānī reports a related two-view dispute in a bequest case.
BURHAN:v2p466/r2.anchor: وأيضا فالخلاف السابق في أن ذكر بعض افراد العام بعد العام هل يدل على انه لم يدخل في العام

BURHAN:v2p466/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p466/r3.speaker: الروياني
BURHAN:v2p466/r3.claim: Al-Rūyānī reports two views on whether a poor Zayd receives both a named dinar and a share of a bequest to the poor; the stronger view gives him only the dinar because the specification limits the executor's discretion.
BURHAN:v2p466/r3.anchor: وحكاه الروياني في البحر من كتاب الوصية وخرد عليه ما إذا أوصى رجل لزيد بدينار

BURHAN:v2p466/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p466/r4.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
BURHAN:v2p466/r4.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī and Ibn Jinnī say a specifically named member is not included in the general expression; on that view, this verse is not an example of the rule.
BURHAN:v2p466/r4.anchor: والقول بعدم دخوله تحت اللفظ هو قول أبي علي الفارسي وتلميذه ابن جني

BURHAN:v2p466/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p466/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v2p466/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī sometimes allows a later conjunct to attach either to the first conjunct or to the nearer preceding phrase.
BURHAN:v2p466/r5.anchor: فإذا اجتمع في الكلام معطوفان هل يجعل الآخر معطوفا على الأول أو على ما يليه

BURHAN:v2p466/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p466/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v2p466/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī attaches mukhrij al-mayyit to fāliq rather than yukh’rij, avoiding coordination of a noun with a verb; Ibn Mālik disagrees and offers another analysis.
BURHAN:v2p466/r6.anchor: فذكر في قوله تعالى ﴿ إن الله فالق الحب والنوى يخرج الحي من الميت ومخرج الميت من الحي ﴾ أن مخرجا

BURHAN:v2p466/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p466/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v2p466/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads al-malāʾikah in the phrase about God's coming as coordinated with Allah, linking it to the eternal decree.
BURHAN:v2p466/r7.anchor: وذكر ايضا في قوله تعالى ﴿ إلا أن يأتيهم الله في ظلل من الغمام والملائكة وقضي الأمر ﴾

BURHAN:v2p466/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p466/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p466/r8.claim: If yā ayyuhā al-nās is universal, wa-khalaqa minhā zawjahā coordinates with an omitted verb, meaning He originated and brought her into being; if addressed to Meccans, khalaqa coordinates with khalaqakum, avoiding repetition.
BURHAN:v2p466/r8.anchor: حاصله أن قوله ﴿ يا أيها الناس ﴾ إذا اريد به العموم

BURHAN:v3p252/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p252/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p252/r1.claim: The text commonly gives precedence to men as a mark of their distinction, as in its mention of many men and women.

BURHAN:v3p252/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p252/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p252/r2.claim: Precedence can mark distinctions in prophethood, freedom, reason, faith, knowledge, life, and the nobility of what is known; the cited examples place the more honored item first.
BURHAN:v3p252/r2.anchor: ومنها شرف الإيمان كقوله تعالى ﴿ وإن كان طائفة منكم آمنوا بالذي أرسلت به وطائفة لم يؤمنوا ﴾

BURHAN:v3p252/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p252/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p252/r3.claim: When daughters are named first in the gift of children, the order compensates them as a vulnerable group; the definiteness used for sons compensates them for losing precedence.
BURHAN:v3p252/r3.anchor: فلجبرهن إذ هن موضع الانكسار ولهذا جبر الذكور بالتعريف للإشارة

BURHAN:v3p252/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p252/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p252/r4.claim: Another possible reason for naming daughters first is to show that all creation follows God's will rather than human preference.
BURHAN:v3p252/r4.anchor: ويحتمل أن تقديم الإناث لأن المقصود بيان أن الخلق كله بمشيئة الله تعالى

BURHAN:v3p252/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p252/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p252/r5.claim: Other orderings follow causal or temporal priority: livestock precede people as the cause, and death precedes life because it existed earlier.
BURHAN:v3p252/r5.anchor: فمن باب تقديم السبب وقد سبق

BURHAN:v3p252/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p252/r6.speaker: القرطبي
BURHAN:v3p252/r6.claim: Al-Qurṭubī reports an unusual dispute over whether a free person is more noble than an enslaved person and directs readers to the discussion in his Sūrat al-Nisāʾ commentary.
BURHAN:v3p252/r6.anchor: ومن الغريب حكاية بعضهم قولين في أن الحر أشرف من العبد أم لا حكاه القرطبي

BURHAN:v3p252/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p252/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p252/r7.claim: The unseen is nobler than what is witnessed, explaining the order in ʿālim al-ghayb wa-l-shahādah.
BURHAN:v3p252/r7.anchor: ومنها شرف المعلوم نحو ﴿ عالم الغيب والشهادة ﴾ 9 فإن علم الغيبيات أشرف من المشاهدات

BURHAN:v2p301/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p301/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p301/r3.claim: One purpose of kināya is to draw attention to divine power: creating humanity from one soul alludes to Adam.
BURHAN:v2p301/r3.anchor: التنبيه على عظم القدرة كقوله تعالى ﴿ هو الذي خلقكم من نفس واحدة ﴾ ( 4 ) كناية عن آدم

BURHAN:v3p366/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p366/r1.speaker: أبو البقاء
BURHAN:v3p366/r1.claim: Abu al-Baqa explains the feminine ذائقة in كل نفس ذائقة الموت by following the feminine sense of كل, as each soul means a set of souls.
BURHAN:v3p366/r1.anchor: أن التأنيث في ذائقة باعتبار معنى كل لأن معناها التأنيث قال لأن كل نفس نفوس

BURHAN:v3p366/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p366/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p366/r2.claim: Zarkashi rejects Abu al-Baqa's analysis: when كل is annexed to an indefinite noun, agreement should follow the noun, not كل.
BURHAN:v3p366/r2.anchor: وهو مردود لأنه يجب اعتبار ما يضاف إليه كل إذا كانت نكرة ولا يجوز أن يعتبر كل

ITQAN:v3p303/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p303/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p303/r2.claim: The two suras beginning with يا أيها الناس fall in opposite halves of the Qur'an: the earlier explains creation and the later explains resurrection.
ITQAN:v3p303/r2.anchor: ورد في القرآن سورتان أولهما ﴿ يا أيها الناس ﴾ في كل نصف سورة فالتي في النصف الأول تشتمل على شرح المبدأ

ITQAN:v2p543#2/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p543#2/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p543#2/r8.claim: Al-arḥām is read accusative as coordinated with God's name, genitive as coordinated with the pronoun in bihi, or nominative with an omitted predicate: it is something to revere and guard.
ITQAN:v2p543#2/r8.anchor: ﴿ واتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به والأرحام ﴾ قرئ بالنصب عطفا على لفظ الجلالة وبالجر عطفا على ضمير به

ITQAN:v2p583#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p583#3/r1.speaker: جمهور البصريين
ITQAN:v2p583#3/r1.claim: Most Basran grammarians forbid coordinating a word to a genitive pronoun without repeating its preposition.

ITQAN:v2p583#3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p583#3/r2.speaker: بعض البصريين والكوفيون
ITQAN:v2p583#3/r2.claim: Some Basrans and the Kufans permit this construction, which they use to explain Ḥamza's genitive reading of al-arḥām.
ITQAN:v2p583#3/r2.anchor: وبعضهم والكوفيون على الجواز وخرج عليه قراءة حمزة

ITQAN:v3p154/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p154/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ITQAN:v3p154/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains Ḥamza's reading without repeating the preposition as omission made possible because the repeated preposition is so familiar that its fame substitutes for stating it.
ITQAN:v3p154/r1.anchor: قال الزمخشري وهو نوع من دلالة الحال التي لسانها أنطق من لسان المقال وحمل عليه قراءة حمزة

ITQAN:v3p298/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p298/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p298/r1.claim: Sūrat al-Nisāʾ governs human ties, including divinely created lineage and acquired affinity; its opening links marriage, prohibitions, inheritance, and kinship to the creation of Adam, his spouse, and their many descendants.
ITQAN:v3p298/r1.anchor: وأما سورة النساء فتضمنت أحكام الأسباب التي بين الناس وهي نوعان مخلوقة لله ومقدورة لهم كالنسب والصهر

ITQAN:v3p298/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p298/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p298/r6.claim: Suyūṭī calls the ordering of the four Medinan sūras exceptionally apt.
ITQAN:v3p298/r6.anchor: وهذا الترتيب بين هذه السور الأربع المدنيات من أحسن الترتيب

ITQAN:v1p203/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p203/r1.speaker: جلال الدين البلقيني
ITQAN:v1p203/r1.claim: Al-Balqīnī classifies the seven famous readings as mutawātir, the other three of the ten plus Companion readings as āḥād, and Successor readings such as al-Aʿmash's as anomalous.
ITQAN:v1p203/r1.anchor: القاضي جلال الدين البلقيني قال القراءة تنقسم إلى متواتر وآحاد وشاذ

ITQAN:v1p203/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p203/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p203/r2.claim: Suyūṭī questions al-Balqīnī's scheme and endorses Ibn al-Jazarī's criterion: a sound reading fits Arabic somehow, fits an ʿUthmānic codex at least potentially, and has an authentic chain, regardless of its reader.
ITQAN:v1p203/r2.anchor: وهذا الكلام فيه نظر يعرف مما سنذكره وأحسن من تكلم في هذا النوع إمام القراء في زمانه شيخ شيوخنا أبو الخير بن الجزري

ITQAN:v1p203/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p203/r3.speaker: أبو شامة
ITQAN:v1p203/r3.claim: Abū Shāma warns that attribution to one of the seven does not guarantee correctness: conformity to the three criteria matters, though the seven inspire greater confidence through their fame and many agreed sound readings.
ITQAN:v1p203/r3.anchor: قال أبو شامة في المرشد الوجيز لا ينبغي أن يغتر بكل قراءة تعزى إلى أحد السبعة ويطلق عليها لفظ الصحة

ITQAN:v1p203/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p203/r4.speaker: ابن الجزري
ITQAN:v1p203/r4.claim: Ibn al-Jazarī says 'fits Arabic in some way' includes grammatical options that are disputed or less eloquent when sound transmission is established; grammarians' objections do not invalidate readings such as genitive al-arḥām.
ITQAN:v1p203/r4.anchor: ثم قال ابن الجزري فقولنا في الضابط ولو بوجه نريد به وجها من وجوه النحو سواء كان أفصح أم فصيحا مجمعا عليه

ITQAN:v4p396/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p396/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
ITQAN:v4p396/r1.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says Adam had 40 children in 20 pregnancies, each a boy-girl pair, and lists sons including Cain, Abel, and Seth and daughters including Aqleema, Ashuf, Juzuzah, and Azura.
ITQAN:v4p396/r1.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق أولاد آدم لصلبه أربعون في عشرين بطنا كل بطن ذكر وأنثى وسمي من بنيه قابيل وهابيل

ITQAN:v1p41/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p41/r7.speaker: عائشة
ITQAN:v1p41/r7.claim: A report in al-Bukhārī from ʿĀʾisha says al-Baqara and al-Nisāʾ were revealed while she was with the Prophet, which was after Hijra; another view dates it to the migration.
ITQAN:v1p41/r7.anchor: ما أخرجه البخاري عن عائشة قالت ما نزلت سورة البقرة والنساء إلا وأنا عنده ودخولها عليه كان بعد الهجرة اتفاقا وقيل نزلت عند الهجرة

DAMGHANI:v1p198/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p198/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p198/r3.claim: Arḥām can mean kinship ties; the source groups this with the statement that blood relatives have precedence.
DAMGHANI:v1p198/r3.anchor: " وأولو الأرحام بعضهم أولى ببعض " كقوله سبحانه في سورة النساء " واتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به والأرحام "

DAMGHANI:v1p191/r24.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p191/r24.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p191/r24.claim: Rijāl can mean male human beings, as distinguished from women.
DAMGHANI:v1p191/r24.anchor: " وبث منهما رجالا كثيرا ونساء " يعني ذكورا وإناثا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p310/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p310/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p310/r1.claim: Raqib is an active-participle form from muraqaba; raqaba can mean to wait for something.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p310/r1.anchor: الرقيب : فعيل من المراقبة ، وهو اسم الفاعل . وتقول : رقبت الشيء ، أرقبه ، رقبة ، ورقبانا : إذا انتظرته

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p310/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p310/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p310/r2.claim: Al-mirqab is a high, overlooking place where a watcher stands.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p310/r2.anchor: والمرقب : المكان العالي المشرف يقف عليه الرقيب

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p310/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p310/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p310/r3.claim: Irqāb is a conditional grant of a house; it was named from mutual waiting for the other person's death.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p310/r3.anchor: وتقول : أرقبت فلانا هذه الدار ، وهو أن تعطيه إياها فيسكنها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p310/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p310/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p310/r4.claim: The conditional arrangement takes its name from each party awaiting the other's death.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p310/r4.anchor: فأخذت من المراقبة ، لأن كل واحد منهما يرقب موت صاحبه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p310/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p310/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p310/r5.claim: Raqib means guardian or vigilant keeper here and in 5:117 and 50:18.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p310/r5.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الرقيب في القرآن على وجهين : . أحدهما : الحفيظ

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p310/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p310/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p310/r6.claim: Raqib can mean one who waits, as in 11:93 and 44:59.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p310/r6.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الرقيب في القرآن على وجهين

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p219/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p219/r8.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p219/r8.claim: Taqwā can mean fear or reverence; Noah, Hūd, Ṣāliḥ, and Shuʿayb use it in exhortations to their people.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p219/r8.anchor: والخامس : الخشية ، ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r8.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r8.claim: One Qur'anic sense of خلق is bringing into existence, illustrated with creation of people, the heavens and earth, and humanity from clay.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r8.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الخلق في القرآن على ثمانية أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r12.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r12.claim: One Qur'anic sense of nafs is Adam, from whom humanity was created.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r12.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن النفس في القرآن على ثمانية أوجه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p270#2/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p270#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p270#2/r3.claim: Zawj also means a companion: Eve, the wrongdoers' companions, souls paired together, or spouses joined with the houris.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p270#2/r3.anchor: والزوج: القرين، قال الله تعالى: وخلق منها زوجها

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10/r1.claim: Quranic expression is deliberately exact at word and letter level; choices account for local context, surah construction, and parallels across the Quran as a whole.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10/r1.anchor: كل كلمة بل كل حرف وُضِعَ وضعاً فنياً مقصوداً في غاية الدقة والجمال

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10/r5.claim: Surat al-Nisa begins with the creation of humanity and the spreading of descendants, then ends with a person dying without a child, picturing life’s beginning and end.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10/r5.anchor: وهي صورة فنية عظيمة لبدء الحياة ونهايتها.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10/r13.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10/r13.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10/r13.claim: Correspondence between surah openings and endings is an intentional, prominent feature of the Quran, not an incidental coincidence.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10/r13.anchor: وإنما هو سِمَةٌ بارزة من سمات هذا الكتاب الكريم وأمرٌ مقصود في هذا الكلام الرفيع.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10/r15.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10/r15.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10/r15.claim: Al-Anam uses أنشأكم من نفس واحدة, while al-Nisa, al-Araf, and al-Zumar use خلقكم من نفس واحدة; the choices suit each context and recurring vocabulary across those surahs.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r10/r15.anchor: وقد راعى في هذا الاختيار السياق الذي وردت فيه الآية كما راعى تردد لفظ (الإنشاء) في الأنعام والنساء والأعراف والزمر

NASHR:v2p247/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p247/r1.speaker: الكوفيون
NASHR:v2p247/r1.claim: The Kufans lighten the sīn in تساءلون; the remaining readers geminate it.
NASHR:v2p247/r1.anchor: تساءلون فقرأ الكوفيون بتخفيف السين، وقرأ الباقون بتشديدها

NASHR:v2p247/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p247/r2.speaker: حمزة
NASHR:v2p247/r2.claim: Hamza reads the mīm of والأرحام in the genitive; the rest read it in the accusative.
NASHR:v2p247/r2.anchor: والأرحام فقرأ حمزة بخفض الميم، وقرأ الباقون بنصبها

NASHR:v1p10/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p10/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p10/r1.claim: A sound reading need not come from one of the seven: sound transmission and the stated criteria determine its status. Readings attributed to any reader divide into accepted and anomalous, though the famous seven inspire greater confidence.
NASHR:v1p10/r1.anchor: بل إن نقلت عن غيرهم من القراء فذلك لا يخرجها عن الصحة

NASHR:v1p10/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p10/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p10/r2.claim: For agreement with Arabic, any valid grammatical face suffices, even if it is not the most eloquent or is disputed; widespread sound transmission outweighs grammarians' objections.
NASHR:v1p10/r2.anchor: نريد به وجها من وجوه النحو، سواء كان أفصح أم فصيحا مجمعا عليه

NASHR:v1p29/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p29/r9.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p29/r9.claim: The genitive reading والأرحام and the passive with accusative reading ليجزى قوما support positions held by some Arab grammarians.
NASHR:v1p29/r9.anchor: ما يكون حجة لقول بعض أهل العربية كقراءة (والأرحام) بالخفض، و (ليجزى قوما)

NASHR:v1p29/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p29/r10.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p29/r10.claim: The total meanings of the seven aḥruf, counting sound and anomalous repetitions, are too numerous to enumerate and reduce to two broad categories.
NASHR:v1p29/r10.anchor: معانيها من حيث وقوعها وتكرارها شاذا وصحيحا لا تكاد تنضبط من حيث التعداد

IBNHIBBAN:3308/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:3308/r1.speaker: جرير بن عبد الله
IBNHIBBAN:3308/r1.claim: Jarir reports that after seeing poor, unshod men, the Prophet recited 4:1 and 59:18 to urge charity; an Anṣari gave generously, others followed, and the excerpt begins the promise for whoever initiates a good practice.
IBNHIBBAN:3308/r1.anchor: عن عون بن أبي جحيفة، قال: سمعت المنذر بن جرير يحدث عن أبيه قال: كنا عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNHIBBAN:v8p101#2/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:v8p101#2/r1.speaker: جرير بن عبد الله
IBNHIBBAN:v8p101#2/r1.claim: When destitute men arrived, the Prophet urged charity by reciting 4:1 and 59:18; an Anṣari's gift prompted others to give, and the Prophet taught that initiators of good or bad practice share its reward or burden and that of followers.
IBNHIBBAN:v8p101#2/r1.anchor: قال: سمعت المنذر بن جرير يحدث عن أبيه قال: كنا عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من صدر النهار

MUSLIM:2351/r1.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:2351/r1.speaker: جرير بن عبد الله
MUSLIM:2351/r1.claim: Jarir reports that the Prophet recited 4:1 and 59:18 while urging a destitute group to give charity, even a half-date; an Anṣārī’s large gift prompted others to contribute food and clothing.
MUSLIM:2351/r1.anchor: عن المنذر بن جرير، عن أبيه، قال كنا عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في صدر النهار

MUSLIM:2351/r2.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:2351/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUSLIM:2351/r2.claim: The Prophet says whoever begins a good practice in Islam receives its reward and the reward of followers without diminishing theirs; whoever begins an evil practice bears its burden and theirs.
MUSLIM:2351/r2.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r1.claim: A report from ʿUthmān, going back to the Prophet, says the best people are those who learn the Qurʾān and teach it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r1.anchor: وروى عثمان بن عفان رضي الله عنه، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «أفضلكم من تعلم القرآن وعلمه»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says every educator wants their teaching followed, and God’s teaching is the Qurʾān.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r2.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن مسعود: «إن كل مؤدب يحب أن يؤتى أدبه، وإن أدب الله القرآن»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r3.claim: When a Bedouin asks what Qurʾān readers are doing, Ibn Masʿūd calls them sharers in Muḥammad’s inheritance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r3.anchor: أعرابي على عبد الله بن مسعود وعنده قوم يقرؤون القرآن، فقال: ما يصنع هؤلاء؟ فقال له ابن مسعود: يقتسمون ميراث محمد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r4.speaker: عيسى ابن مريم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r4.claim: Jesus answers a woman’s praise of his mother by saying blessed is the person who reads God’s Book and follows it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r4.anchor: فقال عيسى: طوبى لمن قرأ كتاب الله واتبع ما فيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r5.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r5.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī identifies the caller of faith in 3:193 as the Qurʾān, since not everyone saw the Prophet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r5.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب القرظي في قوله تعالى: ربنا إننا سمعنا مناديا ينادي للإيمان [آل عمران: 193] قال: هو القرآن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r6.speaker: بعض العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r6.claim: Some scholars interpret the bounty and mercy in 10:58 as Islam and the Qurʾān.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r6.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء في تفسير قوله تعالى: قل بفضل الله وبرحمته [يونس: 58] قال: «الإسلام والقرآن»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r7.claim: Asked why he fasts little, Ibn Masʿūd says fasting distracts him from Qurʾān recitation, which he prefers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r7.anchor: قيل لعبد الله بن مسعود: إنك لتقل الصوم؟ فقال: «إنه يشغلني عن قراءة القرآن، وقراءة القرآن أحب إلي منه»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r8.claim: Anṣār report that the Prophet attributed the lamp-like glow around Thābit ibn Qays’s house to his reciting Sūrat al-Baqara.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r8.anchor: للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ألم تر يا رسول الله ثابت بن قيس لم تزل داره البارحة يزهر فيها وحولها أمثال المصابيح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r9.speaker: أسيد بن حضير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says an authentic hadith similarly reports angels descending in a canopy because of Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr’s recitation of al-Baqara.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r9.anchor: وفي هذا المعنى حديث صحيح عن أسيد بن حضير في تنزل الملائكة في الظلة لصوته بقراءة سورة البقرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r10.speaker: علي الأثرم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r10.claim: Al-Athram recounts dreaming of al-Kisāʾī radiant in white; al-Kisāʾī said God forgave him through the Qurʾān.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r10.anchor: وذكر أبو عمرو الداني عن علي الأثرم قال: كنت أتكلم في الكسائي وأقع فيه، فرأيته في النوم وعليه ثياب بيض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r11.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r11.claim: ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir says the Prophet enjoined holding fast to the Qurʾān at the Farewell Pilgrimage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r11.anchor: وقال عقبة بن عامر: «عهد إلينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في حجة الوداع فقال: عليكم بالقرآن»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r12.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAmr lists public speech with concealed action and the reversal of moral ranks among the Hour’s signs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r12.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص: إن من أشراط الساعة أن يبسط القول ويخزن الفعل ويرفع الأشرار ويوضع الأخيار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r13.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAmr defines al-muthannā as material written outside God’s Book, advises accepting hadith from trustworthy people, and urges teaching the Qurʾān to children.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p37/r13.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص: إن من أشراط الساعة أن يبسط القول ويخزن الفعل ويرفع الأشرار ويوضع الأخيار وأن تقرأ المثناة

MUSNAD-AHMAD:3720/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:3720/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود عن النبي
MUSNAD-AHMAD:3720/r1.claim: The Prophet taught the opening formula for a need-addressing sermon: praise and seek God's aid and forgiveness, testify to faith, recite three verses including 4:1, then state one's need.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:3720/r1.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة، عن عبد الله، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، قال: " علمنا خطبة الحاجة

MUSNAD-AHMAD:19174/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:19174/r1.speaker: جرير بن عبد الله
MUSNAD-AHMAD:19174/r1.claim: After seeing impoverished people from Mudar, the Prophet recited 4:1 and 59:18, urged almsgiving even in small amounts, and rejoiced as the community responded.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:19174/r1.anchor: عن عون بن أبي جحيفة، عن المنذر بن جرير، عن أبيه قال: كنا عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

MUSNAD-AHMAD:19174/r2.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:19174/r2.speaker: النبي
MUSNAD-AHMAD:19174/r2.claim: The Prophet says whoever begins a good practice receives its reward and the reward of later followers; whoever begins an evil practice bears its burden and theirs.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:19174/r2.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " من سن في الإسلام سنة حسنة، فله أجرها

NASAI:1404/r1.author: NASAI
NASAI:1404/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASAI:1404/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd transmits that the Prophet taught the sermon of need: praise, seeking help, forgiveness and refuge, the testimony of faith, then three verses including 4:1, 3:102 and 33:70.
NASAI:1404/r1.anchor: عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ

NASAI:1404/r2.author: NASAI
NASAI:1404/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن
NASAI:1404/r2.claim: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān flags disconnections: Abū ʿUbayda did not hear from his father, and he names ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAbd Allah and ʿAbd al-Jabbār b. Wāʾil as similarly unlinked.
NASAI:1404/r2.anchor: قال أبو عبد الرحمن أبو عبيدة لم يسمع من أبيه شيئا ولا عبد الرحمن بن عبد الله بن مسعود

NASAI:2554/r1.author: NASAI
NASAI:2554/r1.speaker: جرير بن عبد الله
NASAI:2554/r1.claim: Jarīr reports that the Prophet addressed needy arrivals, recited 4:1 and 59:18, and urged everyone to give what they could, even half a date; companions brought food and clothes.
NASAI:2554/r1.anchor: سَمِعْتُ الْمُنْذِرَ بْنَ جَرِيرٍ، يُحَدِّثُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ، قَالَ كُنَّا عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم

NASAI:2554/r2.author: NASAI
NASAI:2554/r2.speaker: رسول الله
NASAI:2554/r2.claim: After an Anṣārī led the donations, the Prophet taught that whoever begins a good practice in Islam receives its reward and the reward of those who follow, while a bad precedent carries their sins too.
NASAI:2554/r2.anchor: فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ مَنْ سَنَّ فِي الإِسْلاَمِ سُنَّةً حَسَنَةً فَلَهُ أَجْرُهَا وَأَجْرُ مَنْ عَمِلَ بِهَا
